Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why doesn't everyone dream big?
Answer: Recently, during my internship class, an intern openly shared her disappointment with life. She is happily married with two beautiful children, but deep down, she feels unfulfilled. She often experiences a sense of incompleteness. She had dreams of becoming a successful businesswoman but never pursued them. “Why?” the faculty asked. “I don't know the reason.” She replied. “Do you have financial issues? Is your family supportive?” the faculty probed further. “I don't have financial issues, and my husband is very loving and supportive. But I think I'm scared.” She stammered. “Scared of what?” “I feel like I can't do it. Starting a business seems like a big deal to me, even though I have knowledge in the field.” She explained. “This indicates a lack of confidence.” The faculty concluded. “I also worry about what will happen if I don't succeed.” She added. “That’s the fear of failure.” Today, many people are so paralyzed by fear of failure that they don't even dare to dream, let alone work on those dreams. Also, they want to reach the destination in one go, which is never possible. People avoid dreaming big because they lack self-confidence. They don't believe in their potential, and the fear of failure holds them back. Like the intern, I too have experienced moments of doubt and fear. However, I have many dreams, both big and small. I dare to dream, and with all my effort, strength, and potential, I am striving to achieve them. When I was publishing my book, I wondered, “Who will read my book?” But then I thought, even if just ten people read it, that would be enough for me. So, I went ahead and published it. Now, people from around the world read it and love it. I also encourage you to dream - whether big or small. Work on those dreams without fear. The journey won't be easy, but maintain your determination. If you fall, you'll still have the satisfaction of knowing you tried. Isn't that worth it? So, take that first step toward your dream today, no matter how small it may be. You never know where it might lead. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do women stay in a relationship with men who treat them badly?
Answer: I know many women who are not treated well by their boyfriends or husbands but continue to stay in the relationship. Even when these women are financially independent, they find it difficult to leave an abusive relationship. After a few months of my marriage, I realized that it might not work out. Yet, I continued it for more than seven years. Emotional dependency is the biggest factor that keeps women in loveless relationships. The man they share their life with becomes their world, making it hard to forget and move on. For women who are not financially independent, leaving becomes nearly impossible. “Where would you go? Your parents have already closed their doors to you. So, it's better to adjust with the man who at least provides food and shelter.” is often the advice they receive from people around them. Many women are wise enough to foresee the consequences of separation. In their current relationship, one man mistreats them, yet they maintain a certain level of respect in society. After separation, however, there is a possibility of being mistreated by multiple men. A single woman is often taken for granted, seen merely as an object of pleasure. As a single mother for years, I've experienced firsthand how society struggles to accept me. People either pity my status as if I am a loser or become angry when I stand up for myself. They're more comfortable when I appear needy and vulnerable. This is why many women, even in today's modern world, choose to stay with their partners, whether they're treated like queens or slaves. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you deal with an attraction to other people when you’re married?
Answer: Every day, when I drop my child at school, I pass by a beautiful apartment building on the way. It's stunning—full of greenery and looks lavish and luxurious. I find myself fascinated. I wish I had a flat in that building. I wish I could live there. But when I return to my flat, it feels like home. I feel comfortable here and love every corner of it because I’ve decorated it with great effort. Even though I'm happy here, I still feel attracted to that other apartment. Why? Because we are human beings, made of emotions. We think, feel, like and dislike things. There are 36,000 emotions, and attraction is one of them. It's a natural instinct that's nearly impossible to control. But as Srinath Nalluri once said, “Marriage is a social construct, and Monogamy is a cultural construct.” These man-made constructs often label simple things as crimes. They have instilled so much fear in people that they feel compelled to hide their true feelings. Eventually, this game of hide and seek can lead to actions that result in real harm. When I was married, and fully committed to my husband, I could share everything with him. I liked some of our mutual friends a lot, and I openly told him why. He understood and agreed. Feeling attracted to someone doesn't mean you want to leave the person you're with. It's just like how I admire that beautiful apartment every day but find comfort in my own flat. Admiring and feeling attraction are what make us human and set us apart from a robotic existence. How do you deal with an attraction to other people when you're married? Don't deal with it. Just feel it, acknowledge it, and move on. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What was the moment when you did something that was right but everyone kept thinking it's wrong?
Answer: After completing my studies and securing a job at a reputed MNC, I received a marriage proposal. The suitor was settled in the US. My family knew his family well, and interestingly, he had visited our home years ago for a few hours, so we had seen each other before. At that time, I had just entered college after completing my 10th grade. He was handsome, and now, he held a PhD and was well-settled in the US. We talked over the phone and didn't find any reasons to reject the proposal. However, I had just started my career then, and I wasn't ready to become a housewife. For me, marriage was not the ultimate goal in life. I couldn't see a promising career for myself in the US, so I politely declined the proposal. This decision disappointed everyone, and some even said it was a mistake. Looking back now, as a divorced woman, I firmly believe it was one of the the best decisions of my life. Imagine if I had been destined for divorce while being jobless - how would I have managed? This is why I strongly advocate for women's financial independence. It is one of the most crucial things in life. I know many women (both online and offline) who are trapped in unhappy marriages because they have no financial independence. They have no source of income and, as a result, have to depend on their spouses for their livelihood. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why should I live?
Answer: “Anshu dear, please don't think about dying all the time. The universe listens to our thoughts and grants our wishes. One day, life might become beautiful, and you'll wish to live a long life, but it might be too late.” This was exactly what a friend said to me over the phone in the year 2018. Why should you live? Because you don't know what the future holds for you. I understand that your pain must be intense; otherwise, you wouldn't be asking this question. Once upon a time, I too had the same question. I questioned the purpose of my existence. My distress made it hard for me to see any hope beyond my immediate suffering. There are people who love and emotionally depend on me. I mean the world to them. But I was so consumed by despair that I couldn't think about that. I couldn't fathom the pain my absence would cause them. When we're depressed, we become self-centered. We focus only on our pain, not on our loved ones. I urge you to have faith. Believe that there is a benevolent force or power working in your favour. It's already working on your situation. Remember that time is ever-changing; it won't remain the same forever. It will change. Work on yourself and look forward to that change. Live for yourself. You didn't choose to come into this world, so you don't have the right to end your life either. Allow the Universe to guide your path. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Why do I feel worthless most of the time?
Answer: You feel worthless because: Nowadays, I am so busy with my job, studies, child, and household work that I don't have time to think of anything extra. I am committed to achieving my goals with unwavering focus. Along the way, I may stumble, and all my efforts might be in vain but I am not dwelling on that. Many people, like myself, find that taking small steps towards self-improvement can gradually change how we perceive our worth. Wish you all the best! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What are the instances when you felt happy as well as disgusted at the same time?
Answer: As a single mother, I encounter numerous challenges in my day- to-day life. Society often doesn't accept a woman who is courageous enough to lead her life on her own. Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I thoroughly screw up my life?
Answer: In my life, I have encountered many individuals who blame others for their failures. They regret having listened to others and spoiling their lives. “Oh, I was very young. I had no idea what to do. My senior misguided me, and I took this step.” “I was naive. My friends tempted me with alcohol and drugs. Now, because of them, I have become addicted.” “I was an obedient child of my parents. I chose to marry a person of their choice whom I don't like, or I chose a career of their choice where I don't want to be. I feel depressed.” “Throughout my life, I worked diligently, earned money, and built a status in society to meet societal expectations. I am 60 now and wonder what I have done for myself.” I hear such confessions, which astonish me. These confessions reveal their vulnerability. Regardless of the age, we all have the capacity to think and analyze what is good or bad for us. Then, why do we listen to others? We understand ourselves better than anyone else. We don't need advice for everything we do. We may seek guidance from experienced people, but we must be mature enough to assess how beneficial that guidance could be to us. Blaming others for our failure doesn't impress me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What's your dream job?
Answer: I aspire to work as a Psychologist. I am currently pursuing an internship as a psychologist. I have experienced depression and severe mood swings for almost a decade. Therefore, I understand how it feels. As a student of psychology, I believe that sadness, anxiety, and stress should not to be taken lightly. One must consult a psychiatrist or psychologist. Trust me, it helps and changes life for the better. This is my personal experience. Medication, which I had considered as a taboo, also helped me significantly. If you're experiencing similar feelings, don't hesitate to reach out to a mental health professional. Sometimes, our brain is unable to release certain chemicals (Serotonin, dopamine, oxytocin, etc.), which can cause sadness and depression. This needs to be addressed through medication and therapy. I wish to work as a psychologist and help people. I want to have my own clinic and treat my patients successfully. This should be my main source of income. I would treat a maximum of five patients per day and come home with great satisfaction. I would then spend time teaching my child, reading books, and writing for my readers. This is my dream job that I keep visualising together with my child, who is my soulmate. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is the best first step to save money?
Answer: Recently, my friend's little daughter had a birthday, and I wanted to buy her some new dresses, so I visited a nearby mall. While shopping for her, I found a dress for myself and ended up spending a thousand bucks on it. Then, my child wanted something to eat, so we decided to have lunch there. All these were unnecessary expenses except for the dresses I bought for the little girl. So I would suggest - Avoid visiting malls every weekend if you want to save money. I live in Bangalore where malls are not only appealing, but also great for passing a few hours without getting bored. However, I rarely visit these malls. Going to a mall often leads to unnecessary spending: You might end up buying new clothes. You may find a unique pair of shoes and feel tempted to purchase them. Your child might insist on taking a ride on a toy car. After wandering for a few hours, you'll likely feel hungry and head to the food court. An expensive dinner done! So, I have almost stopped going to malls unless I'm in a shopping mood. I work hard to earn money, and I can't waste it on unnecessary things. Dining out frequently not only wastes money but can also lead to health issues. So, I choose my means of entertainment wisely. You can also try it if you have limited money and want to save it. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it possible to be too helpful?
Answer: Yes. It's possible. But I would ask you to not be too helpful. Excess of everything is bad. If you are always available to help someone, it loses its allure. The person who is receiving your help might not value your efforts. My uncle taught me Sanskrit and English during my school days. I used to sit along with his students for tution. Everyone knew that I was his favourite student because I was excellent in academics. Additionally, I had a keen interest in studies and learning new things, which made not only him happy but other teachers in the school as well. Still, he acted weird sometimes. He made me wait for hours, and sometimes for days, to correct the essays that I voluntarily wrote. I had to chase him for his time. He was very proud of me but expressed it as if I were just another ordinary student of his. I learnt about his affection for me through my seniors with whom I occasionally interacted in his absence. I was always grateful to him for teaching me and tried hard to please him to get his attention. He loved me and helped me grow, but he never let me take his efforts for granted. This not only kept me grounded but also helped me progress continuously. So, my uncle's approach taught me patience, resilience, and the importance of valuing others' efforts. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do you think most relationships fail?
Answer: I have a few close friends who are always there through my ups and downs. One of them is a bit cranky, and I am cranky all the time. So, many times, we have conflicts, argue, and fight. We stop talking for a week, and sometimes for a month. But still, one of us will reach out, and the connection restarts with the same strength and energy. We approach each other even after conflicts because we don't have egos. We value each other and understand that everyone is different and unique. This is just friendship. But in any relationship, the absence of ego is essential. Only then can a relationship last. Nowadays, everyone has an ego. This ego is the prime killer of any relationship. I admire one thing about children - they are forgetful. They fight with each other and play together again the very next day. We are not like them. We remember everything and continue to feel hurt. Life is too short and unpredictable. We don't know what will happen the next moment. The person whom I loved most and whom I am not talking to now due to some conflicts may leave the world, and I would miss them forever. So, set aside your ego. No relationship would fail. It's challenging, but you can maintain it to some extent. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What does it mean to be true to yourself? How can I be true to myself?
Answer: “At least, stay in the marriage for the sake of your child”, I often heard when I was grappling with the idea of divorce in my loveless marriage. I too thought of my child but my inner self longed for freedom. My soul wanted no more pain. Finally, I made the decision to divorce because I believed I wouldn't be doing justice to myself otherwise. Even now, I receive a lot of advice about remarriage. I receive proposals from wonderful men, but I decline them all. I know, I wouldn't do justice to a new relationship as I have transformed. I have aspirations and goals for my life, and I wish to work on them. I have a wonderful child who has become my soulmate, and I don't want him to ever feel neglected. So, I am aware of my wants and needs. And therefore, I act accordingly. Being true to yourself means you are aware of your needs and desires. You are honest with your thoughts and feelings and don't suppress them just because others are uncomfortable with them. You respect your views, ideas, and decisions and don't change them because they don't get approval from society. You remain who you are. Hope this answers your question. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: I am suffering from regret, feeling that I have had many missed opportunities in life and have made bad decisions. I feel like my life has been for nothing. I am suffering daily. How do I cope with this?
Answer: Recently, a reader from Quora reached out to me with a similar heartache. Reading her messages, I could sense how restless and depressed she was. She had been sexually abused by her boyfriend, who has now abandoned her. She has no one to share her pain with. All her friends have distanced themselves from her, and she feels terribly lonely. She regrets her past decisions and feels like quitting. Many of us experience regrets in our lives. We feel sorry for the actions we took in the past and wonder how we can rectify them. But we can't. The past is gone. What is done is done. We need to let it go and restart. There are two types of issues in our life - ones that you can resolve and those that can not be resolved. If it cannot be resolved, then accept it. Don't punish yourself for things you did by mistake or out of unawareness. Don't be too hard on yourself. You are human and humans make mistakes. Learn from those mistakes and guide yourself toward self-awareness and growth. Take responsibility for your future. Restart your life - this time, to show the world how strong you can be. Have a little compassion for yourself. You haven't committed a crime. So, move forward! Life is all about moving forward. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you tell me something weirdly funny?
Answer: My father shares interesting stories from the early days of his career. He is an eminent doctor. When he began his profession 50 years ago, he used to get calls from remote areas where there were no roads, and he had to walk long distances to see a patient. Once, during one of these calls, which he recalls being in 1978, a middle-aged man suffered from severe diarrhea and became unconscious, losing all his strength. He was a wealthy farmer with plenty of land in the village. However, he was notoriously frugal. When my father reached the man's home, his condition was critical. He had lost consciousness and was lying unresponsive. My father hurriedly administered IV fluids. He stayed with him throughout the night, administering several bottles of glucose to stabilize him. Early in the morning, when my father felt the situation was under control and the patient would recover in a few hours, he decided to leave. As he came downstairs to discuss the situation with the patient’s younger brother and to collect the payment, the patient woke up, full of energy. He came out running and asked about the cost. Upon learning the expense, he scolded his younger brother, exclaiming, "Who asked you to use so many bottles for me? I was alright, I didn't need that many. I am not going to pay this much to the doctor." And with that, he went back inside. Everyone laughed at his reaction, while the younger brother sheepishly apologized to my father and settled the bill. Hope I made you laugh. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do I learn anything?
Answer: I have a few wise friends. They are well-read and have experienced many aspects of life. Sitting with them means exchanging ideas, beliefs, ideologies, and discussing various types of operant behaviour. (Operant behaviour is a behaviour that is controlled by its consequences.) I meet them once, twice, or perhaps thrice a month. Whenever I sit with them to converse, I ensure that I am zero. Zero means I know nothing. The feeling of being zero makes me a learner who is receptive and open to new ideas. Even if I am aware of something they are talking about and I am already implementing it in my life, I try to be quiet without revealing it. Because if I reveal, they may stop there and I may be deprived of learning something they know that I am not aware of. Recently, I was strolling with a friend in a park. He was talking about the sun and its power, explaining how greeting the sun every morning can impact our lives in a positive way. I listened quietly, even though I was aware of the topic. My silence led me to discover a new aspect of wisdom that I hadn't known before. So whenever you read a blog online or a book, or interact with someone wise, set aside your ego, embrace zero, and be receptive. The outcomes will be evident and will propel you to new heights. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your "golden rule" when it comes to relationships?
Answer: Reciprocate. I believe in a relationship where both the parties are good at reciprocating. If I love someone, I want that person to respond to my love. If I care about them, they must show their concerns for me when I am in need. If I am available for them, I expect them to be equally available for me. If this reciprocation is not there, the relationship goes into darkness. We don't understand if our love is accepted or appreciated. Once we know our love has been accepted and cherished, we tend to give more. And the relationship thrives when the receiver returns the same gesture. I have witnessed many relationships becoming monotonous over time, and one partner blames the other, stating that they have become careless. Actually, they have not become careless; they have simply forgotten to reciprocate. So, learn to reciprocate. Give as much as you receive. One-sided effort makes a relationship stagnant. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu .

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: At the end of the day, what matters the most?
Answer: I have not been keeping well these days. A few days ago, I went for several tests, and all the reports were normal. I still feel too weak and tired. Mentally, I am fatigued. At times, I am unable to walk from my bedroom to the living room. Somehow, I am managing my office work and household chores. Today, after taking a bath, I was reciting my daily mantra and felt very irritated. I stopped chanting, put the book aside, and lay down in bed. I felt like I couldn't do anything in my life. All my aspirations and dreams seemed unachievable. I doubted my survival. I felt so numb. I have been under medication for many years. I have changed doctors many times and now, I don't trust them. Because, they couldn't diagnose the root cause of my sickness. According to tests, I am perfectly alright. I don't have any disease, yet I fall sick every six months. And it's horrible. I feel drained and helpless. I wish I was strong and healthy. I have been working hard in my life and I never complained. I have gone through different kinds of mental trauma in my personal and professional life, yet I didn't lose my enthusiasm and zeal. I have been determined to improve and shine. However, when there is no health, all the enthusiasm, zeal, determination, and aspirations seem futile. So, what matters most at the end of the day is health. Now, I understand the value of the saying, “health is wealth.” If you have good health, you are the king. So, take care of yourself. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why is it hard for people to accept non-romantic friendships between men and women?
Answer: As I am doing my internship as a psychologist, I have learnt that there are 36,000 emotions. Each emotion has been categorised into subcategories, making them quite vast. When we develop some liking towards others, especially towards the opposite gender, it is not always romantic love. Love itself is categorised into many sub-categories, such as liking, affection, lust, friendship, and admiration, which can cause attraction. But not all attraction is romantic. However, in life, whenever we feel inclined toward someone of the opposite gender, people often relate it to romanticism. Being an emotional person, I often feel attached to people who have been kind to me. If they are female, it's acceptable. If they are male, it's everyone's concern. The more painful part is that the person who you are inclined toward, starts romanticizing your affection, leaving you with no option but to cut off the relationship. We need to understand that not all relationships between opposite genders are romantic. Some can be based on affection, respect, kindness, and mutual liking. Not all love is about taking you to bed. Some is just for sharing and caring. And I am sure there are many people who appreciate this love. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some advice for someone who is depressed?
Answer: Dear Readers, Recently, someone in his late 30s approached me seeking guidance. He is going through a challenging period, having lost interest in life. He has had a few failed relationships and is currently jobless. He feels depressed and lonely. I could easily understand his situation because I was in the same position once upon a time. During my depressive spell, either I wept with and without a reason or stared at the ceiling for hours, thoughtlessly. I didn't know how to move forward with my life. When we go through this phase, we feel like quitting. However, deep down, we all wish to come out of it. But the question arises: how? My answer to this is: Slowly. Take your steps one by one. Cultivate the belief that you can do it. This faith will not always persist, and every other day, you will feel like giving up. Still, try to rekindle this faith. Just as you trust your mother - she is the one who can not harm you - trust the universe. Our creator wants the best for us. Believe in the universe that has created all of us; a creator always wants to see its creation shine. So, ask the universe to help you by all means. Meanwhile, you keep trying to improve. Engage in regular exercise, go for a walk, and keep yourself busy with tasks. Share your agony with trusted friends and talk to like-minded people who can motivate you. Read some good books. Write a few lines in your diary every day about how you are feeling. Initially, all these efforts will seem futile, and you will find them fruitless. But eventually, you will start feeling better. These efforts will not give you quick results, but slowly and slowly, you will get back on track. Wish you all the best. Take care! Stay Calm! Your Psychologist friend, Anshu.

Question: I am leaving a job that I love because I hate the people I work with. What should I say when they ask why I am leaving?
Answer: Once upon a time, I had a job where I liked my work, but a few people there tried to make my life miserable. I struggled to deal with them, which caused me severe stress and anxiety. My mental peace was at stake. My husband straightforwardly asked me to leave the job, but I was hesitant to quit as we were struggling financially. However, I despised the people there as they were extremely manipulative. They engaged in office politics and always tried to paint a false picture of me to the new manager. I was deeply hurt and eventually started loathing everything there. And one day, I handed in my resignation. After serving the notice period, I left the job quietly. I left without saying a word to anyone; they didn't deserve me. Now, those same people see my progress through social media, which fills me with satisfaction. Their congratulations on my achievements give me a sense of pride. I have forgiven them but not forgotten them. Life is all about moving on. So move on. Focus on your life and do well. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What am I supposed to do now in life?
Answer: “What am I supposed to do now?” I asked my teacher in school, feeling restless and wanting to roam outside. He instructed me to sit quietly in my chair and focus on my studies. However, his instruction neither helped me focus on my studies nor allowed me to roam outside. "What am I supposed to do in my life?" I asked people when I was enduring a miserable marriage. "Stay calm, listen to your husband, and try to adjust with him. Things will change with time," they advised. I wondered how long I would let my soul get crushed. "What am I supposed to do?" I asked my colleague when I was fired from a job without reason. "Don't raise your voice. Try to get your experience letter and move on quietly," they suggested, even though I hadn't been paid for two months. I was shocked because I believed I had the right to be paid for the months I had diligently worked. In a nutshell, whenever I asked this question to others, it seemed I was just supposed to meet their expectations. Their advice never seemed genuine or practical and was never in my favor. They were least concerned about my mental peace and personal desires. They could never offer me the freedom I truly deserved. So, I stopped asking such questions to others. What I am supposed to do in life is absolutely my decision and my choice. Following my own rules and choices may cause criticism from others, but at least I will be at peace. I urge you also to listen to your heart instead of asking others for advice. You know yourself better. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Why don't introverts fall in love easily?
Answer: Have you ever wondered why some people seem to fall in love effortlessly while others don't? According to psychology, there are two major types of personalities - Extraversion and introversion. Extroverts are outgoing and sociable, whereas introverts are reserved and shy. However, personality type doesn't affect the possibility of falling in love. It's just about finding a suitable partner. So, the belief that introverts don't fall in love easily is incorrect. I’ve seen many extroverts with lots of friends but no partner, and a few introverts deeply in love. It can be vice versa too. We need to understand why people fall in love. There are many reasons for falling in love, and the basis of all the reasons is attraction. Attraction occurs when people have similar attitude, feelings, and thoughts. They share goals and purposes, and interact with each other frequently. Such individuals unconsciously form a bond that can lead to falling in love. This kind of attraction is called interpersonal attraction in psychology. Interpersonal attraction plays a significant role in falling in love regardless of age, personality type and marital status. As I am currently completing my internship as a psychologist and establishing myself in the field, I have gained valuable insights through both practical and theoretical experiences during my studies. Hope this knowledge helps. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Is it okay to act okay when you are not okay?
Answer: Recently, at the onset of a meeting, my Finnish stakeholders asked me how I was doing. “I am not doing well.” I quickly answered without a second thought. They laughed and told me they liked me for being straightforward and honest. They asked me for the reason for not being fine, and I explained them about the heavy workload situation that day. They offered me some support and asked me to avoid doing a few tasks for the day as they were not mandatory. I was relieved. However, it doesn't work with all the people we meet. Some people love to hear that we are not okay. For them, our not being okay is a feel-good medicine. So, we need to be careful. The straightforwardness that I showcased in front of my stakeholders doesn't work everywhere. Therefore, you need to act even you are not okay. A friend used to tell me how she presented herself as completely fine in front of her enemies who waited for her downfall, even though she was going through very tough times. The world around us consists of both good and bad people. Surviving with them is not an easy job. We must learn to handle them to protect ourselves from negativity. Hope you like this practical advice. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What are some random thoughts that enter your mind?
Answer: In our hostel room, my roommate and I shared a study table for studies. Alongside our books, we placed our water bottles on the table. I had a habit of sipping water while studying, so the bottle cap was often left open. One night, while studying, the bottle fell onto the table, and water started flowing, drenching our books. My roommate promptly removed our books from the table and began wiping the water with a cloth. "Hold on! Please don't wipe it, let it flow." I exclaimed. "Are you crazy, Anshu? So much water will wet the floor too. Let me wipe it". She insisted. "Doesn't it seem mesmerizing and fearless as it flows?" I asked. "What do you mean?" "It means it has just gained its freedom to flow. It was stagnant in the bottle which is not its nature. Water is meant to flow, Nah?." "Ohh! I see, your thoughtful mind is at work." She chuckled. "Why can't I be like water - flowing freely with the life stream? Let me work on myself so that no one can cage me in a bottle." I pondered to myself and smiled. "What?" She asked, confused by my sudden smile. "Nothing, dear. Let's wipe the water." I replied. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Who died recently?
Answer: A beautiful part of me died recently. A few days ago, I had a big bust-up with some people, and I shouted at them like a badass. I shout like this when I realise that people are taking me for granted, considering me a single woman. In our society, a woman without a man is often considered poor, weak, and soulless. I have experienced this mentality in the last few years, which made me stronger, more straightforward, and firm. I think I have become harsh and stern too. For me, no means no. If I decide on something, whether it is too hard to follow, I would stick to it. The softness of my personality has vanished. Now, I strongly believe in Charles Darwin’s theory of survival of the fittest. In the last few years, I noticed how people intended to take me easy, how easily they try to consider me vulnerable, and if they don't find me how they have predicted, they declare me rude and responsible for my divorce. So, I have drawn a line and make sure nobody crosses it. In any kind of relationship, I ensure that my love for solitude is not mistaken, and I am given space. I lost the soft, emotional part of me. I can't still love people who don't reciprocate the same love. My love is no more selfless. If I give my time and attention to people, I expect them to be there for me in the time of need. Otherwise, I have my way to walk out. I had not been like this earlier. I was emotional and chased people for love and attention. I gave them everything without expecting anything in return. That pure soul has died now. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Are you worried that you will be single forever?
Answer: My seven-year-old son wants to live abroad when he grows up. He seems as determined as I am in every decision that I make. As I love him a lot, I would never clip his wings. I would let him fly from my nest and explore the world. And if I do so, I will be left alone. My close friends often suggest to me to find a partner, but I am not ready. I am still struggling with my inner conflicts and feel helpless when it comes to trusting the world. Also, I am not ready to settle for less. If I ever look for a relationship, I will make sure that I am not people pleaser - there is no politics in the relationship and I am not expected to do any unexpected things. Also, my partner must be available for me with all his heart. With so many conditions, I feel, it would be really hard to find a partner. So, I gave up on finding Mr. Right and embraced my aloneness. At times, this aloneness converts into loneliness and it sucks. Last month, I was seriously ill and I wished to have someone who could happily volunteer to take me to the hospital. This was a bad time - a need and a craving for someone special. However, once I am cured, this need and craving take the backseat. I am no longer worried about being single forever. I know I will have lots to do as long as I live. I will always be focused on writing. By heart, I am a good, cheerful person, so I will never lack good friends. I can easily keep myself busy with children and elderly people in an orphanage. I have a special affection for older individuals. This is how I think and believe about myself. The rest is up to the universe. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is the most important decision you made this year?
Answer: It was 3 am. My train was scheduled to reach Kottayam station in 20 minutes. I called my friend to check if he had already reached the station to pick me up. "Yes, my dear, I am already at the station." He answered. Later, he told me what he realised after this call. If he had not appeared at the station, what I would have done with my child at this hour in a completely unfamiliar city, where I don't even know the language. He felt honored that I trusted him and accepted his invitation to come to Kerala. On the other hand, I was also worried as I was going to someone's house whom I met through Quora. "Why in the world did I accept this invitation?" I had expressed my annoyance to my sister over the call before I boarded the train. However, after reaching Kerala, I realised certain events have to unfold and one cannot control them. Because they happen to teach you something brilliant that you have been seeking for a long time. My Kerala trip was such a thing. I stayed at my reader's house for four days, and I was overwhelmed by his hospitality. His wife and children wholeheartedly accepted me and my child as their guests. I met their relatives, visited many places, had a wonderful experience with a houseboat, savoured the food, walked in a forest, had a drink with my reader-turned-friend along with a heartfelt conversation. There was no moment when I felt tired or bored. It felt like the universe was my side, granting my wish to explore the world. After a long time, I was stress-free, eager to experience everything fully, and I could do so. When the day arrived to leave from Kottayam, I was in tears. I didn't feel like leaving the land that I had newly discovered as my own. But I had to leave. Life is about perpetual motion, always moving forward. The silent trees in the forest taught me to trust the world anew. The water in the ocean urged me to radiate as much positivity as possible. And the occasional rain amidst the hot weather whispered a gentle reminder: there is always hope amidst adversity. While returning home, my bag was full of sweet memories that I received from this beautiful land. Here are some pictures from the trip: Houseboat: Food: The school where our great president K. R. Narayanan studied . A 1200 years old temple. The forest. Houseboat. Easter in a church hall. The excellent taste of countryside tea. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What have you learned from your mistakes?
Answer: I had a crush on someone. I could only see him in the office canteen, town hall meetings, or office parties as he worked in a different department on a different floor. Whenever I tried to see him discreetly, I made a eye contact. “Does it mean that he too feels drawn to me?”, I asked my relative. I often joked about this unknown emotion as I had no courage to express myself to him. And the fear of rejection was at the top of my mind. Later, I got married and completely forgot about him. What have I learnt from my mistakes? One must ask without fearing. If I like someone, I would let them know. If I wish for reciprocation, I would solicit that. If I want to get a discount on something, I would reach out for the same. If I need help from someone, I would request. I don't want to lament in the future thinking that I didn't try. I didn't try to give happiness to the baby inside me who was longing for something. Rejection is okay, moving on without grudges is fantastic, accepting things is bold and admirable. But I wouldn't stop trying. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Why is it important to change yourself?
Answer: My roommate in the hostel was always busy with her boyfriend over phone, making it difficult for me to concentrate on my studies. I had a big bust-up with her. Later, when I entered the corporate world, I encountered various kinds of people. Some were nice, while others seemed intent on hurting me. As an emotional person, I often felt hurt and struggled to adjust to those who were rude by nature, whether it was in the hostel, college, office, or even within relationships. I kept thinking about how I could make them realize that they were doing wrong to me. However, I couldn't succeed as there are hardly any receptive people in today's world. Everyone thinks they are right. And they might be right too from their perspective. Since I have no choice but to live among them, I realized that for my own mental peace, I need to change myself. I can't change others or their perspectives, but I can definitely change myself. I can make myself less sensitive to the world around me and lessen my expectations. I can teach myself that I'm not here to adjust to everyone. It's perfectly okay to maintain some distance, even from our loved ones, if we don't align with them. I can learn not to take everything personally and to absolutely ignore certain things that hurt me. By changing myself, I can make my life easier and more adaptable in this world. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Can you write a short story with a twist ending?
Answer: "Pack your belongings, Mom. You can't remain in this house any longer," Ananya said to Reshma, leaving her utterly stunned. "Why, child? We are family, aren't we? Please reconsider it. You're all I have," Reshma pleaded as tears streamed down her face. Ananya's father remarried Reshma when her mother left him for another man. Reshma accepted 7-year-old Ananya wholeheartedly and cared for her as if she were her own child. After three years of this union, Ananya's father tragically passed away in a road accident. Since then, Reshma took care of her, even though her parents tried persuading her to remarry. But she dedicated her life to the little girl. Ananya is 24 now, settled with a job when she asks her stepmother to pack her things and leave the house. "Gather your belongings. Tomorrow morning, I will drop you off wherever you wish to go," Ananya declared. Reshma packed her suitcase and waited for the morning to leave the house. She didn't know where she would go. She wondered if her parents were right, saying that a stepdaughter can't be her own. Those words were ringing in her ears now. Her elder brother lived with his family 200 km away from the city. She might stay with him for a month and find another house for herself, she thought. "Is this the same little girl whom I cradled in my arms years ago?" Reshma questioned herself in disbelief as they drove in silence the next morning. After traveling approximately 100 km, Ananya pulled up to a quaint, picturesque bungalow. "Step out," She instructed Reshma. "What is this place, child?" Reshma asked in a low voice. "This is our new home, mom. We'll make a fresh start here," Ananya replied, her smile lighting up her face. "Buttt...." Reshma stammered. "You've done so much for me, Mom. Today's your birthday. Forgot? I purchased this house as a surprise gift for you," Ananya whispered, taking her in her arms. "Oh, love!" Reshma burst into tears. They stayed in each other's arms for a few minutes, crying, sobbing, and expressing gratitude. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Daily Life: Who are the villains in our life?
Answer: A few years ago, when I was experiencing depression, I perceived everything as impossible. In 2016, a friend asked me to write poetry again. “I can't. It's been seven years since I wrote last.” I replied. However, he managed to convince me that I can write again. The first few poems were immature, and I myself laughed at them, but slowly I found my footing. There have been many such instances in my life when I felt I wouldn't succeed. I was afraid of even trying. The biggest villain in our life, who demotivates us whenever we want to do something amazing, is ourselves. We underestimate our capabilities and give less value to our achievements. We are often harsh to ourselves and neglect our wants and needs. We are generous to appreciate others but we rarely recognise our achievements and feel proud of them. We wake up late, laze around on weekends and eat junk, neglecting our health, even though we care for our family members at the same time. We work continuously without taking breaks and allow our bodies to suffer. We avoid attempting new endeavours and even avoid dreaming about success. We remind ourselves of our weaknesses and past failures. Now you decide how you would terminate this villain from your life forever. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it a life to live without doing anything to people who talk behind us?
Answer: Yesterday, an acquaintance called my father. She had talked enough about me in the past and spread gossip of my divorce. Unfortunately, I had to answer the call as my father was in the shower. “How are you, child? It's been long since we talked. Hope you are doing well.” She said sweetly. “Oh yes, I am good. Thank you, Aunty.” I replied. The call went on for 10 minutes, where she was the speaker and I was listening to her with zero interest. But yes, I was responding to her without letting her feel that I was not interested. Why? Because my life is more than her talks and deeds. I have moved on from all the negative people. I try my best to avoid any thoughts of them that come to my mind. Because thinking of them brings bitterness to me. This bitterness is nothing but negative vibes. If you are familiar with the law of attraction, you will know that thinking negatively about others brings negativity to your own life. For example, if you keep repeating in your mind that X did something wrong to you, you are sending the word ‘WRONG’ to the universe. And the universe will act as it hears from you. That means more wrong things will happen in your life. So stop thinking that you need to do wrong to people who did wrong to you. Let the universe take ownership of it; your job is to focus on your own life. Embrace happiness. Be as joyful as a child and welcome abundance into your way. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
