Question: The person you love most will hurt you the most. Do you agree with this quote?
Answer: During my college days, I had a friend who was close to my heart. I truly loved her and shared everything with her. We spent hours discussing literature and books as our interests were the same. My emotional dependency increased, and I decided to shift to her hostel to live closer to her. However, after a month of staying in the same hostel, I noticed a change in her behaviour. She started neglecting me. I couldn't understand what my fault was. I tried connecting with her again and again but failed. I was immensely hurt and wept alone. I shared it with a mutual friend who helped me come out of it. This is a 15-year-old story. Still, I wonder what wrong I did to her. This means she's still in my subconscious mind. I don't complain because now I understand that people change, their preferences change. I don't carry bitter feelings anymore. However, I was hurt and those feelings still haunt me. In my professional career, I encountered another girl who was never my friend. She did everything possible to trouble me. Because of her I cried my heart out and feared to go to the office. But I was not that hurt as I was with my college friend. Why? Because I was not attached to her. When we love someone, we make them our world. Our expectations heighten. They become our life, and we find it difficult to accept their changed behaviour. I request you all to be prepared for everything. Nothing is permanent in this universe. At times, an ocean dries, and a mountain crumbles. Then how can you expect a relationship to stay with you forever??? So, please learn to move on. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Did you have an unusual childhood? What made it different?
Answer: I was that child who thought that education was the most important thing in life. I was worried about forgetting the knowledge I obtained from my textbooks. On December 31st, I wept, thinking it was the last day of the year and I wouldn't get the time back. While everyone eagerly awaited Jan 1st to celebrate the new year, I spent my time studying. I started reading newspapers, including their editorial pages, when I was 11. I read biographies, books by Swet Marten, and also the magazines my mother read. I wanted to gain a lot of knowledge. Also, I secretly read some cheap tabloid magazines that my dad's assistant carried inside his shirt and often hid them here and there. I loved playing with children my age, but I was fascinated by how elders thought and behaved. I was often attracted to my teachers and found the separation painful whenever I had to change schools or when teachers were transferred. I loved new notebooks, books, pen, pencils, and erasers and felt immensely happy when my father took me to the market to buy them. I didn't want my friends to know that I loved to read things beyond the textbooks. I don't know why. I didn't like the fact that I was born as a girl. I always had short hair and dressed up like boys, especially imitating my father. During adolescent, I disliked the hormonal changes in my body but could never express my anxiety to my mother. Now, I wonder what sort of child I was. Strange, notable, and weird too! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you learn how to be lucky?
Answer: No matter how many challenges I face, I always have something better than someone that reminds me of my blessings and good fortune. I look at my house and feel grateful to own it. I feel ecstatic when I see things around without which my life could be difficult. Be it anything - the bed, the sofa, the vehicle, food, and even clean water. I am overwhelmed with emotion when I gaze upon my collection of books and express my gratitude to a higher power for giving me reading and writing abilities. I can easily read books, understand the writer's perspectives, and absorb the wisdom. What a blessing! My family, where we all carry different opinions towards life, is still united. I receive the rarest thing from everyone in family, which is love. I possess mental stability and can think clearly. I can articulate my thoughts which can motivate others. I receive overwhelming comments from my readers which bring abundance to my life. There are numerous individuals in this world who are deprived of things that I mentioned above. They are even deprived of basic needs. There are several people who have every materialistic thing with them but they miserably lack mental peace. However, I find myself serene, calm and content with my life. So yes, I feel immensely lucky. In my daily prayers, I thank God for everything that I have. I know you are suffering, but remember that there are always people suffering more than you. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best thing you've ever learned on Quora?
Answer: “The online world can be deceitful. You should not trust anyone on social media.” I believed in this statement until I joined Quora. But Quora changed my perspective. It taught me that both good and bad people are there online, just like the real world. I placed my trust in people here, and they reciprocated with overwhelming love, support and blessings. I forged meaningful friendships with several individuals on Quora who have become an inseparable part of my life. They have shared in my tears, celebrated my happiness, and rejoiced in my success. Am I exaggerating? No. Initially, I too didn't believe those people. How could I trust online people? But gradually, their genuine kindness and selflessness earned my trust. They encourage me to do better in life. If I am sick or depressed, they talk to me as if I am their family. I have a friend here who is in the merchant Navy. Our families have met twice, and we eagerly anticipate deepening our connection in the future. A young man from Quora, whom I sent Rakhi, keeps on promising me to be there for me forever. And I made some more friends who selflessly helped me to write and publish my book. One of them is trying hard to get my book recognition. Whenever I talk to them, they request me to focus on my aspirations and goals. They inspire me to pursue a career in psychology. I have learned incredible kindness from them. Recently a reader called me for guidance. She was feeling lost and directionless. I spoke to her for nearly two hours while my work was getting affected. “Why did you talk so long?” My mother asked me. “She genuinely needed my assistance, and I felt compelled to help her as a way of reciprocating the kindness shown to me by others.” I said. Every single one of my readers is truly remarkable. I get so many heartfelt comments on every answer I write here. As I write this, I feel the moistness in my eyes, a lump in my throat. I deny the statement that says the online world is always deceptive. Here is a picture of one of such meetings: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the difference between children and adults?
Answer: My father is 76 and suffering from the initial stage of dementia. However, he is a doctor and still successfully treats patients. Recently, I spent almost 10 days in hospitals for his treatment. I was exhausted from taking him for a multitude of tests every day and felt weak and frustrated. After a few days, I fell sick myself. One day, out of frustration, I lashed out at my parents, stating that I wouldn't be able to do anymore for them. They didn't say anything. I retreated to my bedroom and lay on the bed. My childhood days flashed before my eyes as soon as I closed them. I remembered how my parents took care of me when I was sick. Once, my father held me in his arms throughout the night when I had a high fever. Recalling those memories, tears rolled down my cheeks, and a sense of guilt engulfed me. I pondered how my child gets angry at me and, after a few minutes, he comes to apologize as he realizes his mistake. I wished to do the same. I wanted to go to my parents and say sorry to them. I wanted them to lecture me on how to behave, just as I do it with my child. I wanted to be like my child; I wanted to be a child again. But I couldn't. I continued lying in bed with regrets. I apologized to the universe and requested to give me patience like lord Shri Ram's. As adults, we find it challenging to emulate the innocence of children. Here is a recent picture with my parents and child: Edit- Some of you have unnecessarily started bashing me. I love my parents and they know it. I am still going to hospitals for their check ups, of course happily.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What's something I should learn while I’m still young?
Answer: Not everyone is good for you. The world is full of amazing people but not all are conducive to your well-being. You can not just go to anyone asking for guidance. They might not understand you, and their counsel might lead you astray. Some of them do not wish good for you. They don't want you to do better in life. When you reveal your vulnerabilities to them, they get a chance to demoralise you. With certain people, your vibes may not match. They will not like whatever you do. They are always unhappy with you, and you may fall into a trap of pleasing them all the time. Be wise when you trust people. Trust them, but not blindly, no matter how close they are. I have witnessed numerous instances where close friends, relatives and even siblings stab one in the back. If you have aspirations, work on them secretly. Disclose them only when you achieve them or are about to achieve them. If you share them in the beginning itself, others may feel threatened by your progress and demotivate you to work on them. In today's world, people are highly competitive. This is causing jealousy, ego, and arrogance. People are quick to feel frustrated looking at other's success. You need to stay away from them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I want my husband and I to have our own separate bedrooms when I get married. Is it okay and is it not embarrassing?
Answer: Once I was talking to a friend about marriage. I introduced him to a new concept of marriage, where spouses stay in separate houses and they should invite each other once a week to spend quality time. He was amazed by this idea. But when I explained the benefits of staying separately, he loved it. Staying in separate houses will protect our individuality as we will be less inclined to alter one another. There will be less possibility of taking each other for granted. We can set our boundaries and have enough space for ourselves. The relationship will never be tedious. Also, we can have enough time to invest in our personal growth. We can work on our goals and aspirations, if there are any. In our culture, marriage often means confining two people in a room forever, and then only it is considered a loving relationship. However, they fail to understand that seeing the same face for 24/7 can lead to aversion. I have seen old couples fighting. In their 70s or 80s, they reach the saturation point. How long can they tolerate each other? How long can they find excitement being together? No more surprises to uncover. Everything is known and seen. So answering to your question, I would say that you are not wrong but seeking a permanent vitality in your relationship. You are just willing to maintain your individuality. So this is very much okay. P.S.- I want to credit the great Indian writer Rabindranath Togore for inspiring me with this idea. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is Anshu Bharti ready to marry a guy though she is a single mother?
Answer: Anshu Bharti has lost interest in marriage and relationships, though she feels empty and craves a companion at times. However, this craving has taken a backseat in her life and she is busy discovering unseen facets of life. During her marriage, she went through a bout of internal disarray which made her firm, and more compassionate towards the world. She doesn't want anyone to go through any kind of pain due to social constraints and their outdated beliefs and ideologies. She advocates complete freedom for everyone, and she is vigorously working on it. She has written a self-help book for people who are going through tough times and living in dilemmas. This book offers valuable insights and guidance to individuals of all ages. She has engrossed herself in writing that can dispel the darkness of people's lives. She aspires to become a psychologist and help people with her knowledge. She has set some goals for her life that she ardently desires to accomplish. Also, she adores her child and is occupied with nurturing him to become a better person. Marriage and relationships scare her to some extent. She has been a bit unlucky in romantic endeavours as people couldn't walk with her parallelly. She has wholeheartedly accepted her present and past, and has moved on to forge a brighter future. Motivating others to live life to the fullest has become her ultimate goal. Please keep her in your prayers so that she succeeds in her noble mission. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What does it cost you to be a polite person in life?
Answer: I am not perfect. I am aware of my flaws. At times, I am short-tempered, impatient and feel frustrated over small things. However, I try my best to stay calm. I am often a polite and humble person. I talk to everyone softly and quickly express my gratitude to them if they reciprocate the same behaviour to me. Being polite doesn't cost me anything but it earns me love, support, and smiles from others, which I find precious. Since last week, I am occupied with my father's treatment at the hospital. Almost every day, I spend half a day there. I meet various people - from security guards to receptionist, staffs at billing counters and in the lab, nurses, and doctors. I talk to everyone politely. Running from one corner to another in such a big hospital often makes me feel drained and helpless. However, amidst the chaos, their humbleness serves as a comforting balm for my weary soul. I request them to prioritize my case first as I need to go to work as well. At times, they heed my request and help me. In return, I thank them profusely and they smile. I have experienced that a polite person receives more attention than other people. They are helped if needed. Our arrogance, and ego don't let us remain polite forever. However, we must learn to overcome them because they affect our mental peace. I request you all to be polite while interacting with others. Your politeness will bring you blessings and abundance. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How does insecurity affect our lives?
Answer: Insecurity is an emotion, and we all carry this emotion as long as we live. You are anxious about losing your job, even though you hold a higher position in the organization. You have insecurities about old age and the fear of being left alone if your spouse passes away before you. Insecurities about failure in career, relationships, and even about your complexion and appearance. This insecurity is like a cobra, staying far away, but hissing from time to time and snatching your mental peace. You have all the comforts for getting a peaceful sleep but you still can't close your eyes because you are scared of the cobra coming to bite you. If you can summon a little courage to believe in yourself - that you can restart from scratch even if you lose everything - you can easily get rid of insecurity. I have my insecurities about failing in life as a single mother, but it doesn't compel me to settle for less. I am ready to accept everything that comes my way because I have learnt to believe in myself. I also encourage you to believe in yourself because you are powerful. You are the energy that can change circumstances positively. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I am male. Why does my mom expect me to clean the house when she and my sister can do it perfectly fine themselves?
Answer: I believe everyone should possess the skills of cooking and cleaning, regardless of gender. When you share meals and a household with your female family members, why not equally share the responsibility of cooking and cleaning? Your gender does not make you superior. I have begun teaching cooking and cleaning to my seven-year-old son, and I am very firm about it. If I need help, I ask him to sweep the house. I drink hot water several times a day and candidly ask him to heat the water for me. I will soon be teaching him to prepare Maggie, tea, and coffee. No one can live in a mess. For a healthy lifestyle, cooking and cleaning are basic skills. They are essential for survival. And I dislike seeing the new generation of men who are still dependent on women for these basic skills. So if your mom expects you to clean the house, be grateful to her for making you independent. She is a real woman who strives to improve her son in all areas of life, sidelining patriarchy. Because patriarchy may betray you someday as your partner stops cleaning and cooking for you, but not your skills. You can still survive. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: When did you feel that you discovered something so profound in your life that there was no going back?
Answer: I know an amazing woman from my previous job who seems perfect at everything. I love her for her liveliness and vitality. She is a fitness freak and motivates her thousands of followers for the same on Instagram. Although I seldom have conversation with her, I see her WhatsApp status every day. And I am captivated by her beauty, fitness and numerous talents, such as painting, crafting, singing, and dancing. Recently, I saw her status where she talked about something that I couldn't agree with. She supported a group of people who didn't seem empathetic to me. I wondered how she could think so. My ego was not ready to accept her views. It seemed she broke my heart. It seemed I lost my respect for her. “This is so ugly. How could she find this group authentic?” I questioned myself. “Hold on.” I then heard a voice from within. “Her opinion has nothing to do with yours. It's your ego that is not letting you accept that there can be another perspective of looking at things. You are judging her because that makes you feel superior. You want to fix her because that makes you feel better. You want to prove your worth by proving her opinion wrong and worthless.” I heard. I then realised how pointless it is to nurture hostility with someone just because they hold an opinion different than mine, when I still have so much to learn from them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some things elegant women always do?
Answer: To my wonderful female readers, would you consider incorporating these traits into your personality? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm. Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How does a woman feel when she is getting old and no one wants her?
Answer: It is entirely an individual matter. Some women are very emotional by nature. They deliberately look for emotional dependency as they need someone throughout life to share their journey. As they grow older, and encounter loneliness, they feel utterly depressed. Believe it or not, irrespective of gender, all of us crave the feeling of being ‘WANTED’, no matter how independent we are. This is a natural instinct, and we can not deny it. Once, my professor shared a heartfelt story about his mother. She was 65 and had separated from her husband. My professor was working in Japan at that time. When he visited his mother in Germany during a vacation, he found her depressed. One evening, he took her for a stroll in a countryside, where he suddenly hugged her. Tears rolled down her cheeks. “It's been eons since I last received a warm hug. Thank you.” She whispered. My professor could see the yearning for affection and validation in her eyes. It was a very emotional moment for both. Most women are emotional by nature. They love to be loved. At any age, they love to receive attention. And there's nothing wrong with that. It doesn't make them weaker or lesser. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I want to change the world; where do I start?
Answer: My roommate in the hostel was a lazy lass. Although she was a medical student, she wasn't interested in studies and seemed aimless. At night, She stayed up late, reading comics, and woke up just 30 minutes before her class. In contrast, I was studious, with a zeal to excel in life. Over time, we got along well and became close to each other. Out of concern and affection, I wished for her to become a disciplined student. I spoke to her about it several times, but it didn't work. She remained unchanged - least bothered about studies. I made sure not to be affected by her laziness. I woke up early, revised my notes, completed homework and arrived at college on time. As a result, I consistently scored well in exams. During our recess time, I discussed studies, teachers, and why I admired some of them. Since I had an inclination towards writing for newspapers, this became another topic of our conversation. Gradually, she developed a zeal to improve her academics as our conversations centered solely on studies. One morning, she woke up before me. I saw her reading her textbook. I was amazed but I didn't say anything. We just exchanged smiles. Gradually, we became a team. We studied late night together and discussed our goals. Once, her mother, on one visit, thanked me for making her so sincere. What should we do to change the world? Change yourself. Stick to this change and become a role model for others. No matter how many distractions come your way, you continue to stand your ground. The world will slowly begin to follow you. P.S.- We humans are like monkeys. We end up imitating each other. If you want your children to read books, read yourself first. If you want to silence your noisy neighbours, show them your extreme calmness. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you converse with yourself?
Answer: I don't like social gatherings. Phone calls and chats don't interest me, though I love people. I never want to lose those people in my life who love me. However, I prefer to be alone most of the time because I love to converse with myself. I have numerous thoughts and topics to explore, discuss and analyse, and I feel, I am the one who can be my greatest partner in debate and discussion. While talking to myself, I discover my authentic self. I get to know my capabilities, vulnerability, and determination. I learn about things that I wish to have in my life. I feel more capable of deciding what I need to embrace and what I need to discard. Conversing with myself gives me direction in life. It makes me more flexible to the outer world and helps me accept my inner turmoil. I feel more adequate and less judged. By talking to myself, I can easily plan for my future goals and choose the path to walk on. I encourage you too to take some time for yourself. Talk to yourself and get to know yourself better. No friends, teachers, and family members can tell you better about yourself than you. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: At what point does love become pain?
Answer: I am in love with someone. My emotions for him run deep. He is now the focal point of my aspirations. I think about him every moment of my life. All I focus on is him. For me, he is in everything and everywhere. I sleep with thoughts of him and wake up missing him. Yeah, I love him so much. I have forgotten about my aspirations. I don't want to work on the goals I always aspired to achieve. I tell him I feel so complete with him that I don't want anything else in life. I just want him. That's it! And here, the pain starts. Since I am only focused on him, I experience insecurities and fear. “What if he leaves me?” “What if he doesn't love me in the future?” “What if he changes?” And then, with these insecurities, anxiety begins to set in. I feel upset when he doesn't reply to my messages. I am hurt when he doesn't show up on a date. I am unable to understand his difficulties. I wish I could focus on my goals, channelize my energy into personal growth. I wish I could pay some attention to my health, well-being, and other activities to enhance my wisdom. I wish I had not given him the remote control of my happiness. P.S - If you are going through the same, shift your focus to things that I wished for in the last paragraph. Wish you all the best. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What brings you happiness in your day to day life?
Answer: You can also include these habits in your life. They have helped me become a better version of myself. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is there a book that helped you survive your childhood?
Answer: When I was 11, my father took me to Delhi to visit the Indira Gandhi Memorial Museum. Looking at items that once belonged to our prime minister Indira Gandhi, I was deeply moved. Her clothes, bag, footwear, books, and study room made me realise that someone great had existed. Emotion welled up, I felt a gentle moisture in my eyes as I gazed upon the saree she wore on her final day. As we were leaving, my parents bought me her biography. This book greatly influenced me. I was captivated by her strong personality from childhood, and her love for reading inspired me to read more. The insightful letters from her father also fueled my aspirations to become a better human being. In one letter, Nehru told Indira a brilliant thing to distinguish between right and wrong, which I still follow: “When you are afraid of doing things in the light, consider it wrong.” This means if you have to hide your actions from the world, that action can't be right. Indira Gandhi undoubtedly became my role model. I loved her personality and earnestly wanted to become like her. Now, I realize how much good books matter in our lives, especially during childhood. A little brain is quickly molded in the right direction if it is fed good thoughts. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Should I keep telling a depressed person “It’s all in your head”?
Answer: There was this friend who always listened to me when I was going through depression. “I am unwanted. Nobody needs me. I have no one. I feel like quitting. I don't find any purpose in life.” I kept iterating the same thing whenever I met him. And he heard me out patiently, without telling me that it's all in my head. He understood that I was going through a mental illness where I had lost all my zeal. Nothing could brighten my mood. Even the happy moments seemed so temporary to me that I couldn't enjoy them but wept. I wonder if he had said that it was all my assumption, how I would have felt. Maybe I would have found him heartless and insensitive, and I would not have opened up to him. I would not have shared my insecurities with him, considering that he wouldn't understand me. Right? Then, maybe, all my rotten, ill feelings would have accumulated, making me even more sick. Because, in depression, a patient doesn't need your suggestions or biased conclusions but your ears to hear them when they vent out. Your statement, “It's all in your head” is disheartening, tending to isolate them. A person going through mental illness becomes too sensitive. Be careful when you speak. Your words can either heal them or intensify their distress as they lose their capability to analyse your intention. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you know that you like someone?
Answer: I eagerly await their presence. I have a strong desire to share every aspect of my life with them and am equally keen to learn about theirs. Witnessing their success brings me immense joy. Their achievements feel like my own. I proudly talk about them and introduce them to my family. I worry about their health. I offer suggestions as their well-being becomes a genuine concern for me. I give them enough space. I admire their unique perspectives on the world and seek their approval for the choices I make. I find joy in preparing meals for them rather than opting for restaurant food. Serving them food with my own hands gives me immense satisfaction. Thoughts of them occupy my mind frequently, and I consistently wish the best for them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What surprised you today?
Answer: The prominent newspaper, Deccan Herald, appeared quite irresponsible today. Let me provide you some context. A 12-year-old boy named Parinav went missing after failing to return home from his coaching centre in Bangalore. He was later found in Hyderabad after three days. Now look at the headline in Deccan Herald: “12-year-old traced to Hyderabad, had fled after cheating in exams.” Was it necessary to mention cheating in exams? The child was already in immense pressure which led him to this state. And now, this statement will shatter him. It will not only affect his mental well-being but also impact how he's perceived by society, parents, and classmates. Deccan Herald’s choice of words has damaged the child's image within his peer group. He may not be able to face his teachers and friends at school. The label of cheating in exams may affect his chances of admission to reputable educational institutions. Numerous such unpleasant possibilities may haunt the child for a lifetime. The child was already traumatized, and the Deccan Herald has only intensified his trauma through its insensitive reporting. This inhuman approach to journalism is shocking. I am surprised to experience the lack of compassion to this extent. Undoubtedly, it's a disgusting display of insensitivity. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the difference between emotional dependency and true affection?
Answer: I am in love with someone, and I feel like I can't live without him. I seek his support for everything I do because without it, I feel helpless. I express to him that I can reach new heights only if he is there. His presence brings me great joy, while a sense of neglect from his side suffocates me. The other day, he mentioned his desire to go abroad for a few years to build his career, and I couldn't fathom how I would live without him. “No, no, be here. I can't live without you.” I sobbed. My tears saddened him, and I realized I had become an obstacle in his growth. This is how emotional dependency manifests. I love him. Yes, with all my heart. I can't bear to see him in pain. When he expressed his plan to build his career abroad for years, I let him go with a smile. Because, his happiness means more to me than my own. When he said he couldn't marry me due to certain reasons, I didn't make a fuss but smiled. I cherish the beautiful moments we've shared, and I am immensely thankful for them. I won't curse him but I will pray for his happiness. This is true affection, where I am selfless, generous, and compassionate. My lover’s happiness is supreme to me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I want a strong comeback in life with my success in an exam which is in 3 months. What should I do?
Answer: Three months means 90 days that consists of 2,160 hours. Not bad! Make a daily routine and follow it vigorously. Try to utilize your time for your studies as much as you can. Aim for 6–7 hours of sleep every day to enhance concentration. Drink more water to keep yourself hydrated. Eat healthy and light. This will keep you active and focused. Give a break to all your social media accounts. Uninstall them from your phone. While studying, turn off the internet or keep the phone away. Read your notes thoroughly, write them and revise them quickly in every three days. There are three stages in our brain - When we read something, it enters our sensory memory, where it stays briefly. Repetition helps it transition to our short term memory (STM). After revising for a couple of days, it is stored in our long term memory (LTM), making it difficult to forget. Consider putting your friends, family and relationships on hold for three months to achieve better results. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you think about the Ram Mandir Consecration ceremony on 22 January by Modi?
Answer: I have come across numerous impactful write-ups since yesterday. Some Muslim brothers have also penned responses filled with wisdom. While watching the live show of Pran pratishtha, I found myself moved to tears. My heart was brimming with emotions and pride for being a witness to such significant moments. Reflecting on this, I wondered why these emotions surfaced. I've never participated in discussions about the Babri masjid and Ram mandir dispute. For me, whether it is a temple or a mosque, God matters. I believe in God, in power/Shakti, whether it's Ram, Allah or Jesus. Yet, yesterday, the emotional tide overwhelmed me, while I was watching the consecration ceremony of Ayodhya Mandir on TV. Tears flowed without warning. I think my parents are right; they say bhagwan Ram is an emotion. Ram is a synonym for peace, compassion, strength, patience and understanding. Lord Ram was a man of honour. He taught us to be better humans, loving and obedient sons, compassionate rulers, and much more. The temple in Ayodhya isn't just for idol worship; it is the birthplace of Ram. Those who have faith in Ram and find inspiration in him, can visit his birthplace. Wishing you all a joyous and harmonious Ram Rajya, filled with peace, prosperity, and unity. May the ideals of Lord Rama guide us towards a society of righteousness and compassion. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What's the most life changing thing you can tell me?
Answer: In college, I had a friend who saw positivity in everything. For example, "Nidhi Mam speaks at a rapid pace, it's so difficult to take a note of her lectures." I complained. "But she is knowledgeable. Her lectures are really good." She replied. "Huh! Rashmi is so arrogant. I always find her flaunting her things." "Her choice is brilliant. Her new watch really looks elegant." This is how she responded. She saw beauty in everything - the bright sun, the soothing mango tree with its lush green leaves in the campus, delicious samosas in the canteen, and even the strict principal's persona was impressive to her. While other students complained about the extended exam date, she calmly sat in her room reading a novel. She was always cool. Content and happy. Surprisingly, people were very supportive towards her. In later years, when I discovered the law of attraction and how it works, I realised why my friend remained calm in all situations and received positive responses from everyone and everything. The law of attraction states that whatever you give out in life is what you receive back in life. Give positivity, you receive back positivity; give negativity, you receive back negativity. Blame, criticism, finding faults, and complaining are all forms of negativity, and all of them bring back nothing but strife. So, from now on, be careful with your words and actions. Make sure you think and speak only positive words, if you wish to bring abundance into your life. As Newton said, “To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.” Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some things that look easy but are difficult?
Answer: Maintaining stability in our thought process. No matter how composed and confident we are in our life, there are moments when we feel vulnerable, lacking confidence and fearing judgement. My German professor, who also happened to be a close friend, was a scholar. He had penned books and attended many seminars as a speaker. Once, he had a seminar at Delhi University where he was to speak on cultures. I accompanied him as a guest, and on the way, he confided in me that he was not feeling confident. After the seminar, he revealed that he was sweating when an audience member asked him a question. He had trouble understanding the accent of the audience. This is just one example. In our lives, we all face situations where we feel inadequate. Our confidence levels drop, and we feel like losers. A bit of grief can cause us to fall apart and we forget all the good things that we have. We find ourselves in instability and chaos. Our goals begin to crumble, and we feel helpless. We lose focus, become lethargic, and procrastinate. When things settle down, and we feel better, we regret everything mentioned above. If you also face such situations, I want you to know that there is nothing to worry about or regret. Feelings are fickle, and stabilizing them is more theoretical than practical. Accept when such weak thoughts creep in and wait for them to leave. You are still capable of doing the things you desire. So, don't get low-spirited during these emotional turmoils. Take it easy! P.S.- The picture is just for attention to reach more people with my thoughts. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should parents teach their kids?
Answer: My parents are coming to Bangalore soon, and I am teaching my child to do the following things: This little boy is a subject to me in the lab of life. I am conducting the experiments on him to see the results in the future. I expect him to become a kind, loving and compassionate person. Let's see how much I succeed. Teach your children to be respectful to their grandparents so that one day, they will also respect you.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Who are you grateful for in your life?
Answer: As I reflect on my early life, I realise how my parents unknowingly shaped me into a writer. My father, an eminent doctor, often hosted learned guests at home. They had intellectual talks which were a learning experience for me. I had the opportunity to meet some of the warmest and nicest people I have ever come across. We had servants, maids and a gardener with whom my parents were very respectful. I got a chance to sit with them and learn about their life, by listening to their heartfelt stories. When dad returned home in the evening, his conversation with mom was about his patients and their struggles. Some ministers occasionally visited my father and discussed societal issues that heightened my awareness. My mother, an avid reader, spent her savings on novels and magazines at railway stations. She encouraged my love for books and happily indulged in celebrating various occasions, be it Eid or Christmas. Though my parents always emphasized the importance of education, they encouraged artistic pursuits. All these experiences enriched me with stories to pen as a writer. So if you ask me who I am most grateful to, I would blissfully mention the names of my parents.😊😊😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would you like written on your tombstone?
Answer: Anshu Bharti The one who wished everyone to realize the light within them, which is sufficient to dispel the darkness in their lives. 😊😊😊 Thank you. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Have you ever tried to bring some light to the dark in someone's life?
Answer: My childhood friend and I grew up together. She came from a poor background. Her family was not educated, but she had a keen interest in studies. Even though she was not good in academics, she always managed to pass her exams. During summer vacations, she stayed at my house, studying with me and learning new things from my mother. She observed how my mother draped a saree or adorned her hair with jasmine, though these things never captivated me. This way, she was dear to my mom as well. I helped her with math and other subjects, and my mother treated her like family. One day, she came home in tears. When asked, she revealed that her father was not allowing her to continue her studies. At that time, we were in the 7th or 8th standard. My mother urged my dad to speak to her father about this. Finally, her father agreed to let her continue her studies as he couldn't say No to my dad. (My father is a reputed doctor and people are very respectful to him). She continued her education, passed board exams, graduated and became a teacher in a government school. She is currently serving as a principal. She married an unemployed man from her community through an arranged marriage and helped him establish a business. It's been years since I met her but my mother encountered her last year. With a smile, she told my mom that she was able to prepare gulabjamun for her children that she had learnt from her during school days. She gave all the credit to my family for her better life. Though her resilience helped her to reach the new heights, our support helped her overcome obstacles. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you write something that will fundamentally change how I see the world?
Answer: A few months ago, I found myself under the weather. No major health issues, just frequent sickness. I underwent various tests, but nothing severe appeared in the reports. Still, I felt tired, fatigued all the time. At times, I was exasperated with my condition as I couldn't work on things I wanted to achieve in my life. Negative thoughts crept in, making me believe that I was destined to be sick. “I eat healthy food, drink enough water, and go for a walk. What else to do to stay fit?” I asked my mother with a lot of irritation. I was quite disappointed, thinking of all this. But suddenly, a thought came to my mind that changed my perspective. Many people battle diseases, swallowing 15–20 tablets daily for survival, and they are supposed to take those tablets for a lifetime. The moment they stop taking those pills, their life would be at risk. How pathetic! How painful! I was in a much better situation than those people. Right? So whenever you feel depressed about anything, compare yourself with less fortunate ones. You couldn't get the promotion. That's okay. Many unemployed people just wish to get a job. You are suffering from a disease; some are suffering from deadly diseases with no cure. You are going through a painful breakup, some children lost their parents in an accident and are living in darkness. You can still restart, but they are clueless. Look at the world a little more closely, you will realise how blessed you are. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best random conversation you overheard?
Answer: I was traveling on the metro, and a couple sat beside me. The husband appeared upset and angry, while his wife tried to calm him down. Their little daughter with two ponytails, quite playful and naughty, was unable to get attention from them. So, she was secretly pulling my sleeves and grinning at her mischief. While I was also enjoying her activities, I overheard the couple's conversation. “I can't. I can't listen to them every time.” The husband said in a terse voice. “Why can't you? They are your parents, Rishi.” The wife responded softly. “Soumya, don't you see how they ask for money every time? Just last month, I transferred 5000 Rupees to their account.” He expressed in agitation. “That's okay, Rishi. They need it so they are asking.” “If they need money, why don't they ask Aniket too. He is also earning well. Why me always?” He questioned. “Because they feel more comfortable with you. You are close to their heart.” She explained with a reassuring tone. “But what about us? What about our life? If we keep on giving our money to them, how shall we manage our life?” “We will manage. We have the blessings of our parents. We will never lack anything in life, trust me.” The wife smiled, leaving me genuinely moved. Suddenly their daughter gave me a sharp pinch on my right arm, and I got up from my seat, pulling her cheek softly as my station was about to arrive. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are you banned from? Why?
Answer: The little man captured in the photograph is fond of paper planes. He is skilled in making numerous types of planes with different features. Some soar straight, while others gracefully twirl in circles. Some can go really high, others will take a turn from the middle of the way and fall back at his feet. He has boxes full of such planes, a bag full of white and coloured sheets for manufacturing. The drawers at home have his planes, and the mattresses hide some beneath them. The exhibition takes place if any of our guests show interest in them. Some are quite fascinated by his paper planes. For a while, they stop talking to me just to give them a try. A sense of pride envelops him when he bribes his friends with these planes to shut their mouth whenever he does any mischief in the class. Undoubtedly, children adore him because they occasionally get their shares. While the whole world seems to be crazy about these paper wonders, I remain an outlier. I don't find any charm in them. I am fed up seeing them in every corner of my house. Once, by mistake, I threw a few, considering them garbage. I had to face great hue and cry. The complaint travelled from high court (my sister) to supreme court (my mom). Since then, I am highly restricted from touching them. I am completely banned for going near them. I ponder whether this little munchkin would ever be able to get rid of this passion. Please let me know if any of you is equally passionate about it. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the weirdest thing that happened to you today?
Answer: I was driving to the school to drop off my child this morning when he complimented my bike, mentioning it felt smoother since I had it serviced the previous day. He asked me to drive a little faster, and feeling happy, I increased the speed. However, after 100 meters, I felt a pang in my heart as if an accident was imminent. Immediately, I slowed down and started reciting Gayatri mantra, something I had never done before. I even persuaded my son to join me and with a bit of hesitation, he started chanting as well. As we approached the main road where I needed to take a right turn, another man on a bike with his child joined me to cross the road, but I was behind him. My child and I were still reciting the mantra. Once the man and his child safely crossed the road, I followed suit. However, in the middle of the road, a tractor came speeding towards us and abruptly applied its brakes as it was about to hit us. My heart was filled with fright and uncertainties. I scolded the tractor driver and continued on our way. After dropping my child at school, I had planned to stop for shopping but changed my mind, sensing that the day was not favourable. I decided to return home immediately. The strange part for me was that I had never recited Gayatri mantra before, and later in the evening, I discovered a picture of goddess Gayatri in my phone gallery. I have no idea who sent it to me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I love myself? Are there any tips or a book that can help me start?
Answer: For me, my mental peace is the most important thing in life. I can't compromise on it. I had a boyfriend in the college with whom my inner tranquility was often at stake. Later I was in a marriage where I forgot about my wants and needs. I completely lost my mental health and became insomniac. At present, my emotional well-being is my first priority. I can gracefully exit any relationship where my mental health is at risk, no matter how emotionally involved I am with the person. Because I know how it feels after losing it. So, safeguarding my mental peace is the first sign of loving myself. No book or tip can help you to love yourself. You need to identify your preferences, wants and needs, and then you have to protect them. You need to set boundaries and make sure no one crosses them. Currently, ‘selfless love’ is not in my dictionary. I can only love those who reciprocate the same to me. I make sure I don't chase people blindly. I let people know that they can not take me for granted. It hurts me a lot when I am emotionally involved with someone and that someone neglects me. So, in a relationship, I ensure that I am not hurt. I focus on things that I want in my life. I take care of my health and sleep. This is another version of loving myself. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I get over a break up?
Answer: Stay busy. Immerse yourself in various activities. Take a regular walk, and exercise daily. Connect with friends and talk to them; this can include sharing your struggles, future plans, and goals. Meet new people and exchange ideas. This will provide you with a fresh perspective on your current situation. Read books. Reading books is engaging and will heal you to some extent. During my divorce, I lacked guidance. However, my parents were there and supported me with all the means they could. But they were equally in pain. And at the same time, I lost my job that increased my grief and uncertainties of life. Though I was trying to keep myself busy with writing, it proved insufficient. I spent my days in profound anguish. I wish I had been more thoughtful and used my time more productively during that one year without a husband and a job. Those days are behind me now. I encourage you not to repeat the same mistakes. Break ups, divorce, separation are part of life. Embrace them with grace and move forward. Whining, crying, panicking, or cursing your partner will take you nowhere. So accept the situation and smile, thinking - you are still alive; you still have the potential to transform your circumstances and improve your life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do we handle an argument if there's a difference of opinion when both of us feel that we are right in our own way?
Answer: Pause when you sense a heated argument is brewing. Stay Calm for your own mental peace. There is no need to prove yourself, Mr. or Miss Right. Remember, you are not here to win all the arguments. Everyone is right from their own perspective. So be respectful. You need to understand that everyone is influenced by their upbringing and external factors to have a perticular opinion. So no one is at fault. Gracefully smile as you walk out of the argument. You can not lose a relationship just to prove your opinion is correct or better. Last but not least, you must have lots to do instead of wasting time in arguments. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some life lessons you learned in 2023?
Answer: Yesterday, while I was still in 2023, I completed the book, ‘The Alchemist’ written by Paulo Coelho. With every paragraph, I felt that the author was conveying a message. The book talks about omens, right time, soul, life, dreams, and discovery. It delves into people, their thought process and fear of failure. It provides insight into relationships and commitment, illustrating how people tend to change others when they meet frequently or spend more time together. Though the book didn't introduce anything new as I was already aware of, and practiced most of its concepts consciously or subconsciously, it gave me a new confidence in things I do or plan to pursue. I remember being denounced on Quora when I shared my opinion about relationships. The criticism didn't shake me but I did feel that I couldn't be a part of this society with my out-of-the-box thoughts. While reading this book, I realized that there are many people in this world who think like me; I just need to discover them. ‘The Alchemist’ taught me that everything in the universe has a soul. God is nothing but energy, and the energy exists in each molecule of an object or in each cell of our body. Therefore, be respectful and kind to each and everything. The book has strengthen my belief in myself and my aspirations. I learnt that one can achieve everything they aspire. When we want something, the entire universe conspires to help us achieve it. “Life attracts life.” - The Alchemist. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the 5 things that complicate your life?
Answer: So live your life with ease. Take things easy. You don't belong to Chandragupta’s Dynasty, where one wrong action will spoil its entire history. Do what you like. Speak up without worrying about what others will think. The universe grants equal opportunities to all; Identify and seize them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why is it bad to be overly competitive?
Answer: My sister shared a story about a neighbour who was never content with what she had. Although her husband was a successful businessman, and abundance surrounded her, she lacked peace, not money. My sister was astounded by the way she spent money in the market. She wanted to buy things that her relatives had, purchase dresses she saw her college friend wearing on Facebook, regardless of whether they suited her or not. She desired the same crockery in which she was offered food at her husband's friend's house, even though she already had plenty at home. She bought all the stuff. And the result? Overflowing cupboards filled with beautiful yet seemingly useless things. At times, she grew fed up looking at them, but she couldn't help it. Her day started accumulating things and ended arranging them in cupboards. In between she kept scrutinizing who had what. She could never look at horizons beyond her material acquisitions. She could never experience the sense of satisfaction and peace. She was restless. Disturbed and anxious too. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How has 2023 been for you?
Answer: The year 2023 has been very kind to me. It gave me a clear picture of what I want to do in my life and a determination to achieve my future goals. I have developed a profound desire to write more and more and motivate people who are struggling with life. I am studying psychology to enhance my wisdom so that I can guide people with increased confidence in the future. My book, ‘Towards A Better Life’ is being loved globally and has been placed in 23 libraries worldwide. My readers across the world are unconditionally helping me to reach new heights. I receive several emails and messages from them, stating how my writing is changing their lives. When they encourage me to write more, I feel immensely blessed and see abundance all around. In 2023, I had the privilege of meeting some readers who travelled to Bangalore for a heartfelt conversation, and some are planning to visit Bangalore in the first quarter of 2024. I am looking forward to exchanging ideas and thoughts with them. I also received an invitation from a school to speak to their students. When I look back, I wonder how drastically, beautifully my life has changed in a year. With the right attitude, full of gratitude and away from criticism, ego and gossip, I am moving forward with life. And I believe I will achieve what I wish to achieve. Thank you everyone for your unwavering love and support. When I close my eyes, I visualise you all standing beside me. What a blessing! May prosperity accompany each of you in 2024. Thank you, again and again. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How come I never learn lessons from mistakes?
Answer: I am currently pursuing my master's degree, and three months ago, I faced a practical exam. Unfortunately, due to time constraints and my child's illness, my preparation was not thorough. I left an important but lengthy theory unread, believing that the universe would favour me by not including it in the question paper. This overconfidence backfired when the exact theory appeared in the exam. Though I wrote it with my limited knowledge and also could expand it through my writing skill, the results were not upto par. Fortunately, I passed with the help of the viva. This experience left me somewhat disheartened. In December, I had exams again and this time, I studied well, tried to cover as much as I could. I refused to leave anything to luck. And my hard work paid off as I performed well in the exams. I have cultivated a determination to achieve my life goals. So the mistakes that I make become my greatest teacher. I don't want to repeat them. My aspirations hold great value and I am earnestly dedicated to reaching them. How come you never learn lessons from your mistakes? Perhaps because you haven't fully embraced and loved your life or developed a profound desire for improvement. The day you yearn for self-improvement, you will truly begin to learn from the mistakes that have hindered your growth. I wish you all the best on your journey. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you agree with the statement "parents are always right"?
Answer: My child is 7. There have been many times when he made me realise that I was wrong. “You didn't understand what I was saying and scolded me unnecessarily.” He pointed out when I rushed to conclude something about him. Yeah, he speaks up. At times, he is very scared of me as I am a strict mother. However, if he is not wrong, he dares to speak up. And I appreciate it. Before being parents, we are humans. And we humans can never be flawless. We can make wrong decisions for ourselves and our children. We can be emotionally drained, due to which we may overlook the right path and deviate. So if one says - parents are always right, it wouldn't be realistic but superficial. Parenting is a tough job and there are no specific rules for that. It depends on circumstances that lead a parent to make a decision. And the decision can be wrong and right too, so the parents. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something you find frightening that most people don't?
Answer: While dropping my child off at school each day, I pass by a slum that leaves a lasting impression. Children, half-naked, play around their tent houses, women wash dishes with a single bucket of water, and men rush, probably to their work. Their lifestyle sends shivers down my spine. Near their tents lie bushes and a filthy, empty field. There is no hygiene, safety, or privacy - comforts are a distant reality. I can't help but wonder how they endure winter nights. I have no idea how they manage their privacy. No separate rooms, no washrooms, and toilets. I find it so difficult and if I think deeply, I find it horrible. This lifestyle seems incredibly unfortunate, especially when we compare it with our concerns about promotion, buying new flats or cars. We never pay heed to the food that we eat everyday. It's undoubtedly healthier than what people in slums consume. We forget to be grateful for our beds and cozy blankets, oblivious to the harsh reality of their sleep conditions. During a conversation with a friend, we both felt a profound sadness for these people. She mentioned that she wouldn't survive if she had to live in such conditions. It's truly frightening! Yes, it is indeed terrifying. So, the next time you're about to complain, consider the lives of those in the slum, if only for a moment. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: When was the last time you did something for the first time?
Answer: Recently, I found myself in an unexpected situation during an exam. The invigilator handed me a theory to write without an alternative choice. When I read the theory title, I felt totally blank as I knew only three key details: the topic, the theorist's name, and the year of publication. These three points could be summarized in three lines, yet I was expected to fill three pages. The invigilator read my mind and shot me a nasty glance. I could feel the disdain in his eyes for an unprepared examinee. However, I ignored him and decided not to waste time staring at a blank paper. So, I started observing my surroundings. The invigilator's large key ring, jingling as he walked, drew my attention. His black shoes, though old, were meticulously polished. I liked them. The guy at desk 13 was busy writing like he knew everything about the world. He had this stopwatch, which I thought was pretty cool. And then, there was a woman at desk 21. She kept staring at the ceiling while writing, maybe trying to remember stuff like me. But boy! she didn't forget to put on her dark red lipstick. I admired her resilience. When I looked at the clock on the wall, I noticed it displayed the incorrect time. It made me remember something Paulo Coelho said, "Nothing in the world is ever completely wrong; even a stopped clock is right twice a day." Empowered by these observations, my writer's spirit awakened. A writer can turn a tiny idea into something big. With this realization, I gathered my writing spirit and began to pen down my thoughts. Two pages later, I confidently handed over my answer sheet to the invigilator. And guess what? I passed the exam.😅😅😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the examples of the worst feeling ever?
Answer: When you have everything to feel happy but you don't feel happy. You have money to buy entertainment, you have a loving, supportive family, you have a wonderful, high paying job. And maybe a lot more! But still, you are not happy. You don't feel excitement for anything. You have no hobby to pursue. You sit idle for long hours, not knowing what is happening to you. Your loved ones try to cheer you up, and you find it hard to give a smile to them. Your friends crack jokes, laugh their heart out, and you struggle to accompany them for the same. It's just because you might be suffering from serotonin deficiency. Serotonin is a chemical messenger released in your brain that helps to regulate mood, happiness and other aspects of your emotional well-being. When you lack serotonin, you face depression, anxiety and sleep disturbances that affect both your physical and mental health. What is the worst feeling ever? When you have everything to feel good, but you are unable to feel it due to serotonin deficiency, and people wonder what is wrong with you. P.S.- If you recognize these signs, consider seeking professional help or confiding in someone you trust. Take care of yourself! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What am I missing out on in life if I am an introvert?
Answer: In our family, my sister is the extrovert star. She loves the buzz of people, spending hours talking, dancing and partying. She effortlessly connects with everyone at family events, making them livelier. I have been quite the opposite, finding comfort in my own world. Even at weddings, I liked to be alone with a book. People asked about my reading, shared a smile and moved on. Sometimes, I wanted to be like my sister - so that I could be the centre of attention in family functions. I admired her outgoing personality, yet found contentment in my introversion. As an introvert, I couldn't have great fun with a lot of people but had a heartfelt talks with a few. In my solitude, I got more time to figure out what I wanted from this life. I could develop the ability to think deep, observe and analyse things more candidly. I had enough time to read and write. I have been buddies with my diary since I was 15, jotting down my thoughts and feelings. I am not the classic introvert anymore, but I still prefer smaller gatherings. It lets me focus on what I love. This gives me immense bliss. If an extrovert finds ease in social settings and adapt quickly to new environments, the introvert’s path is equally rewarding. In my chosen solitude, I discover profound joy and contentment. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do some people overthink more than others? Is this ingrained in some personalities?
Answer: They overthink because they have to figure everything out on their own, making decisions solo and facing the consequences without emotional support. In the past, they were made to feel they were not good enough, leading to a lack of confidence. They were judged harshly for making mistakes. So they are extra cautious and overthink whenever they have to make any decisions. They get hurt in the relationship no matter how hard they try. They became like a burnt child that dreads fire. There are many such reasons why people overthink. They have their past experiences that have impacted their thought process. Some fear the societal judgement due to which they think a lot before taking a step. The fear of failure is another reason for overthinking. Trust issues don't let them form relationships with others quickly and they ponder a lot before getting into a new relationship. In a world where every step is scrutinized and judged, some prefer to be extra careful in their actions. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What one incident that you would never forget in your life?
Answer: I was 7 or 8 years old. My house is situated near the main road. One afternoon, I was playing alone outside the house when I found five one-hundred-rupee notes scattered on the ground. I jumped with sheer joy. I ran to home to show it to my mother. Dad had just arrived to have lunch. He inquired about the money a little and sat for lunch. An hour later, he left for his clinic and returned home within 10 minutes, seeking me out. “Give me that money; it belongs to someone else.” He said to me. “No, I can't. It's mine, I found it.” I cried, clutching the notes tightly. “But it's not yours. Its rightful owner is an elderly woman who is fighting with the grocery shopkeeper. She insists she gave him the money but he denies it. They are locked in a heated argument, and she is in tears. I varified with her about the money, and she described the notes exactly as you found them. Please give it to me.” He urged. “I won't.” I replied adamantly. “Okay, don't give. But come with me and see the woman at the shop, please”. He persuaded me. Reluctantly, I walked with him to the shop, stood in a corner and saw the woman. She was old and poor, wiping her tears with her saree. I looked at my dad sadly. “Please. I will give you a few coins, and with them, you can buy your favourite candies at school tomorrow.” He promised with a warm smile. I smiled back and went straight to the woman to return her money. She was shocked. My father compassionately explained everything to her, while the shopkeeper scolded her for baseless accusations. I happily left for home, playing with coins that dad had rewarded me with. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What questions should a guy ask a girl in an arranged marriage?
Answer: When a man (known to me) visited the girl for the purpose of marriage, he politely asked, “Would you like to serve me with a glass of water as soon as I reach home from the office in the evening?” He continued, “I will never impose control on you. I cherish and respect your individuality and freedom. All I seek from a wife is wholehearted love. The second thing I expect from her is to be a housewife. If these expectations align with your vision, I would gladly say yes.” What I admire most about this man is his profound self-awareness. He articulates his desires and expectations with clarity, leaving the decision now in girl's hands. With his clarification, the girl now knows the kind of life she would lead if she says yes to him. If she is ambitious in her career, this guy might not be the right match. However, if she is willing to have a loving and respectful relationship, this guy is a perfect match. Regardless of gender, transparency is crucial in an arranged marriage. Both partners must communicate their wants and needs for the marriage to work. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some small things that you miss the most in your life?
Answer: My father adored me when I was a little girl. He was so fond of me that he wanted to see me as soon as he returned from his clinic. He would scoop me into his arms, planting a tender kiss on my forehead, tousling my hair and gently rubbing his chin against mine. At night, he would cradle me and we’d playfully roll in bed, creating moments filled with laughter. This was the love he showered on me during the childhood. “I love her the most” He proudly declared to everyone, expressing his deep affection for me. I cherish those beautiful moments the most in my life. Yesterday, my mother conveyed over the phone that he no longer wishes to travel to Bangalore. He says his body no longer supports extensive journeys; he is now 76. I feel a profound sadness, thinking how things change in our life. He is sacrificing his fondness for his daughter and grandson due to his weakened body. And I am struggling to accept this reality. I miss my father, his love and his fondness. I yearn for those gentle kisses, surprising tickles and daily hugs. I miss him a lot! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If you are in a complete and total despair, does it mean you gave up with your life?
Answer: "I've lost all interest in life. I don't want to live anymore. I want to quit." Shared a reader, reaching out with deep agony. "I don't believe it," I replied. "What do you mean? I want to commit suicide," he emphasized. "Nope, I don't think so," I said. "You still want to live, my dear. There's a great interest in life within you," I continued. "How can you say that?" He seemed annoyed with my words. "If you had truly lost interest in life, you would have already taken that step. But you didn't. You came to me, seeking motivation. You still want to live, but you've lost your drive. Something has deeply hurt you, leading to these negative thoughts," I explained. "Hmm..." He calmed down a bit. "You already have a light within you. You just need to recognize it. As you've come to me, finding solace, you are very close to finding it. Awaken your spirit, confront the odds, and overcome the negativity that has engulfed you. Remember, you can!" I continued. "Got it. Thank you! I'll come back to you soon with a new version of myself," he said with a determination, and left. P.S.- At some point in time, we all go through a depressive spell. It's important to open up to someone and share your inner feelings. Depression doesn't mean the end of life; we just need someone to listen, provide emotional support, and guide us toward the right path. So, discover the light within you! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I make life easier for people around me?
Answer: Don't poke your nose in their affairs. I grew up in a small town and observed that people were more engrossed in others’ lives than their own. This phenomenon persists even in a bustling city like Bangalore where I am living currently. News about someone's personal life spreads faster than wildfire. A girl has an affair, and the neighbours get to know about it before her parents. They just can't keep quiet after knowing about it, but add some spice to the story and spread the rumour. Now according to the rumour, the girl already slept with the boy and is pregnant. This leads the girl to take her own life. And the story is over! You see most people talk about others. The topics vary from ‘who is doing what’ to ‘who bought what’. Meet your friends, colleagues, relatives, neighbours and talk about others, which fills our life with discomforts. These discomforts are sometimes not negligible. Some are scared of being judged. Some feel hurt when they hear rumours about themselves. Some find it hard to share their feelings openly. They are so afraid of your big nose poking into their life. If you genuinely want to make a positive impact on others' lives, then focus on your own affairs. Redirect your energy from talking about others to cultivating empathy and kindness. Wish you all a very happy diwali! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Are controlling and manipulative relationships loving relationships?
Answer: If you ever find yourself losing your originality and sense of self in a relationship, that can not be considered a loving relationship. A person, who truly loves, allows you to live as you want. They don't control or manipulate you but respect your individuality. The true definition of love is giving freedom. If I love someone, I would let them do what they like. I will never clip their wings or be a hurdle in their life. This is how love acts. Buddha said, if you truly love a flower, you will not pluck it. So if you truly love someone, you will not control them but let them grow and flourish. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best thing you can say to a woman?
Answer: Don't say anything, just love her. In a world where words often fall short, let your love speak volumes. Be with her when she needs you. Assure her that she is not alone, but she has you as an unwavering support system. Make it known - she is the most special person in your life. Show her through your actions that someone is always by her side to share both joy and pain. Hold her close during her emotional lows, and give her assurance of being with her for a lifetime. Be true to her. Don't toy with her emotions. Cultivate sensitivity to understand her, especially when she is feeling dejected. Be true to yourself while being with her. Don't do anything just to please her. Please her only when you find a pleasure in seeing her happy. She can easily sense your willingness or unwillingness in doing things for her. Don't make false promises to her. You don't know to what extent they can break her. She can be broken, and might not recover for a lifetime. P.S.- I wrote this, considering you love her and want to say the best thing to her. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your biggest mistake or regret?
Answer: Yesterday, it rained all day. In the afternoon, my slipper broke, and I panicked since I'm not accustomed to walking barefoot, even at home. In the evening, my child went to play with his friend in our neighbor's house while I was engrossed in my office work. Suddenly, I realized that the rain had subsided, and I could go out to purchase a new pair of slippers. So, I quickly locked the house, and headed to the nearby market, thinking I would return in 15 minutes. I didn't inform my neighbor, and I rushed to the market. However, due to the rain, heavy traffic had built up. The sky had already darkened, and it was still drizzling. It took me 30 minutes to return home. As soon as I reached home, I went to my neighbor's house to inquire about my child and got to know that he had left their place long ago. I became worried. Due to the bad weather, everyone had locked themselves in their flats, making the corridors look deserted. I wondered where my child could be. I decided to check with another neighbor whose child was my son's age. I rushed to their floor and knocked on the door, praying to find him there. Fortunately, he was there! I brought him home and quickly joined a meeting. Later, when we retired in bed, he recounted the incident that had occurred in my absence during the evening. In his words: "Aunty asked me to leave because it was Rohan's study time. I came home, rang the bell, but you didn't open the door. I rang the bell 11 times. At first, I cried, then I felt angry and banged the door in frustration. I went to the terrace, searching for you, but you weren't there. It was dark, and I got scared. I ran from there and stopped on the 3rd floor. I sat on the stairs for a few minutes and wept again. Then, I went to the basement to find you, but you weren't there either. That's when I went to Mayank's house, and within a few minutes, you arrived there." "Why didn't you go back to Rohan's house?" I asked, holding back my tears. "Because they had already asked me to leave," he replied sadly. I hugged him tightly, cried my heart out, and apologized to him countless times for the mistake I had made, while he kept repeating, "That's okay, mumma!" Here is a picture of us, for the attention: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Are you afraid of falling in love with someone?
Answer: Yes. Because, falling in love leads to togetherness. Lifelong togetherness which scares me to the bones. After experiencing a failed marriage once, I have quite a different idea for marriage now. I believe, even after marriage, partners should stay in separate houses and visit each other periodically. Maybe, once in a week or month. This concept of marriage will not only help a person to be himself, but also save him from emotional turmoil. The partners in this concept will be emotionally independent and can focus more on their aspirations. It reduces the likelihood of taking each other for granted and keeps the craving for each other alive. It also breaks the monotony of 24/7 togetherness. Partners can maintain their individuality while nurturing their love. This can lead to a healthier and more fulfilling relationship. If I ever fall in love with someone, I will be asked to live together. This frightens me. For most individuals, relationship should be legalized and stamped on paper. For me, a relationship should be only based on emotions. If it is not there, one must move on. I fear of being mistaken and misunderstood by my idea of marriage. Also, I have no time to invest in a relationship due to my job, child, households, writing and studies. I hope you now understand why I fear falling in love. However, if I find someone who shares my perspectives, I’d embrace love without hesitation, time and time again. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What makes you happy?
