He was opposed, defamed and denounced, yet he chose to drink hemlock rather than compromise his principles. Then there was Rousseau, who emphasized the importance of emotions and the natural state of human beings, which he believed was corrupted by civilization. In the 18th century, he was a controversial figure, challenging the norms of his time.. Osho spoke of enlightenment through absolute freedom. His interpretation of freedom was often misunderstood. And he was brutally criticised. Despite facing criticism from many, these men stood by their ideas. During my college days, I delved into the works of these wise thinkers, perticularly Socrates and Rousseau. Their unconventional thinking fascinated me. Even now, I revisit their words. There's something about reading their thoughts that never fails to bring me happiness. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What was the weirdest compliment you've ever received?
Answer: 18 years ago, when my niece was born, my mother visited an astrologer to have a birth chart written for her. He was a well-known astrologer in our town. One evening, I accompanied her to his office. He had converted the front room of his house into a small office. There was a computer desk with a chair in one corner, and a few chairs were placed nearby for his clients. As I looked around, I couldn't help but notice a a shelf adorned with books on astrology. However, what truly caught my eye were the 30–40 dark red notebooks. My mother told me that each notebook contained a birth chart that he had written for his clients as per their orders. Out of curiosity, I showed him my hand. He scrutinized both of my palms for a moment, and abruptly closed them, stating, “This girl is remarkably imaginative.” I chuckled at the comment. However, as the years passed, I realised how true it was. My imagination knew no bounds. I can imagine anything - even things that never happened or that may happen in the future. Randomly and out of context. I am frequently overwhelmed by my imagination, whether it's in a positive or negative context. For instance, if I aspire to achieve something in my life, I can vividly visualise it with the same intense emotions as if it has already been accomplished. When explaining complex things to my child, I find that my vivid imagination becomes a powerful tool. I can effortlessly create stories or examples for his better understanding, making the learning experience both enjoyable and effective. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you do daily?
Answer: I am a single mom and my days are a whirlwind of responsibilities. Managing my job, the household and taking care of my child often feels like chaos. However, in the midst of this daily chaos, I don't forget to live the moments. I make sure I call my mother and make her feel wanted every day. Her blessings are a source of strength that I don't want to miss any day. Every day , I set aside a few minutes to hug my child with all my heart and make him feel safe, loved and protected. I also take a moment each day to express my gratitude to the universe. I count my blessings, which include my parents, sister, child, friends, readers, and my writing skills. This daily practice reminds me of how fortunate I am. I emphasize the importance of education to my child. Before bedtime, we engage in thoughtful discussions about what we've learned. I share stories of great personalities from around the world, and he tells me about interesting things he's discovered in his textbooks. I secure some moments to think deeply about what I want to do in life. I try to find the root cause of my disturbance if there is any. Like everyone else, I have only 24 hours in a day. But I make an effort to set aside time to truly live and cherish life. It's these moments that keep me grounded and grateful. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do popular Quorans follow any unpopular Quorans?
Answer: Why not? When I started writing on Quora and gained a small following, just a few thousand followers, some very popular Quorans began to follow me. I was amazed because I was not sure about the value of what I was writing at that time. I received messages from two popular Quorans who encouraged me to continue writing my unconventional thoughts. They were genuinely impressed. Unfortunately, both have left this platform now. Now, I believe I have gained a modest level of popularity with 36,000 followers. However, I am being followed by great writers with more than 1 lac followers. It really feels great. For me, the quality of the content matters more than the quantity of followers. I also follow many Quorans who write excellently but may have a smaller following. This doesn't matter to me. If I can learn something from their writing, that's enough for me. Popularity on Quora doesn't hold great significance for someone like me, who still has a long journey ahead beyond Quora. But yes, it does instill confidence in walking a similar path outside, which one has chosen. So don't disharten yourself. Keep writing. If your thought can change even one person's life, it's worth writing. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is real beauty according to you?
Answer: Someone criticizes you and you feel offended. A close friend suddenly changes and starts ignoring you and you feel low. If someone doesn't like your idea and denounces you for the same, you stop sharing your ideas fearing just a bunch of people. You don't like someone's idea and therefore, you waste all your energy and time demeaning that person. Your partner betrays you and you blame him/her for creating the miseries in your life. I don't find any beauty in those reactions of yours. I wish you could be busier working on you, your life, and your happiness. I wish you wouldn't have wasted your time thinking, regretting, and cursing the agonies that took place in your life. Instead, you would have concentrated on your well-being and personal growth. I am a deeply flawed person. Also, I have aspirations to pursue. I have a lot of work to do on myself and therefore, I have no time to think about criticism, gossip, my ex, toxic neighbors, and relatives. I am busy improving my life and find real beauty in doing so. Would you like to do the same? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it right to judge a person without knowing them?
Answer: My friend Ranjana has everything in her life. A loving husband and bright children. She is inherently loving and caring. However, at times, she becomes extremely cranky and furious without apparent cause. She seems adamant and very dominating. People judge her, criticize her and make disparaging remarks about her. No one wants to investigate why she overreacts sometimes. In the past, she experienced a few failed relationships in which she was exploited. She sank into severe depression and swallowed multiple tablets each day to break free from this depressive spell. There were days when she was ill and no one was there to care for her. People, whom she had loved, abandoned her ruthlessly. She lay on the floor for hours, crawling and creeping in the grip of her illness. These episodes of her life made her harsh. The memory of those days still hampers her mental peace and makes her suspicious about the world. However, people judge her, often brutally and ruthlessly. Forming perceptions and jumping to conclusions about others is easy, but understanding them and approaching things with positivity isn't everyone's forte. Show a little compassion. You never know what someone has experienced or is currently going through. Your judgmental comments can be deeply hurtful to a person battling depression, someone who might never feel comfortable sharing their emotions with anyone. P.C.- Google. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Have you ever had a conversation with a stranger, what did you talk about?
Answer: As I entered the bustling schoolyard, the laughter and chatter of children filled the air. I had just arrived to pick up my son. Out of the crowd, a young boy with curly hair and cute nose approached me. “Aunty! Aunty! Your son beat me today.” he complained. “Oh! I am sorry, baby.” I apologised. “Look at these scratches, he did this to me.” He showed me some scratches on his arms, leaving me in disbelief. “Oops! I am so sorry, darling. Why did he beat you?” I asked, while I lowered myself to his level and hugged him. “I swear, Aunty, I didn't do anything. I just took his new pencil box and he got angry.” He explained. “A new pencil box? But he didn't get any new pencil box, Sweetheart.” “He got, he got! A golden colour one!” He screamed. I wondered. I made a strong effort to recall if I ever bought my son a golden colour pencil box. “Look, he is there - your son is there”. He suddenly yelled pointing out to a child. “Whoa! He is not my son, Sweetheart.” “Look, that's my son.” I luckily saw my child running with his friends in the playground. “Ohh! Is Shourya not your son?” He rolled his eyes in exasperation. “No.” “But Shourya said you are his mother before I came to you.” “Umm! Shourya was just playing a little trick on you, Sweetheart.” “Umm, ok” the little stranger nodded and walked away. A warm smile spread across my face. I hope, it made you smile too. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you evaluate maturity?
Answer: When someone speaks something controversial which is not liked by mass, there arise three groups of people whom the speaker faces: Group A and Group B are for and against. They will be there for everything that occurs in the world. However, people from Group C are not obligated to be found. They are progressive and non judgemental. Though they don't support the speaker’s perspective, they tend to believe that there can be another perspective too for looking at things. What they have not experienced or seen in life doesn't mean that it doesn't exist. So, they don't argue, and try to prove the speaker wrong. For them, everything is a learning. In a world divided by opinions, it's the Group C who offers us a path to understanding. I admire Group C and find their maturity captivating. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you find the most difficult to do while going through a depression?
Answer: I experience panic attacks and bouts of depression, which can last for several days. During these times, I lose interest in life, and my dreams and aspirations seem to crumble. Reading gives me a headache, and I struggle to understand a simple sentence. I often find myself wondering why I'm feeling so sad and what I truly want. I feel clueless. And lifeless too. To cope with these emotions, I try various things. I play cards with my child, reach out to close friends for a chat, and call my mother just to hear her comforting voice, as if it might be my last day. I take soothing strolls, but unfortunately, none of these activities seem to work. Sometimes, I stand in front of the wooden temple at home, feeling numb, but I don't ask God for anything. It's a struggle to lift my mood. I feel weak and exhausted. I often lose my appetite, to the point of almost stopping eating. However, I hold onto one thought: I will restart. I will get better. I'll return to Quora and share my thoughts once more. I will guide others who may be going through similar struggles. And fortunately, I manage to overcome this phase. I emerge from these depressive spells feeling like a conqueror. I have accepted my depression as I would a normal headache or tiredness, and I no longer feel ashamed of it. If you're going through something similar, I encourage you to take it easy, have faith, and work towards overcoming it. Don't let it become too severe. Keep working on yourself, and remember, you're not alone. A recent picture taken during a depressive spell. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What makes you feel old?
Answer: My thoughts. I have witnessed a lot in my life. So many ups and downs. Happy moments and extremely miserable days when I just wanted to quit. I formed connections with people much older than me. During high school, an old man in his 90s was my friend. I’d sneak over to his house to sit with him and listen to his words. I don't know what pleasure I found listening to him and observing his trembling hands. In college, I was inclined towards my English professor who was a true rebel. He had read thousands of books which led him to question every societal norm that I had always considered auspicious. We’d engage in long conversations and argue. He often called me an “emotional fool” whenever I opposed his ideas. He urged me to see the world with a more logical lens. On a train journey, I met an editor from the Times of India, a man of wisdom who treated me like his daughter. While talking to him, I received unique insights about the world whenever he visited me in my hostel. Simultaneously, I have been fortunate enough to get closer to people and learn life’s harsh lessons through their experiences. I got to know that a few circumstances in life can't be changed no matter how strong, affluent, or successful one is. Also, I read a lot. All these episodes in my life helped me develop my own ideas and views which may not align with conventional thinking. I am no longer interested in activities that people of my age find fascinating. I am unable to judge people and make a perception about them immediately. I would like to go deeper to understand why someone holds a different opinion or lifestyle. Sometimes, I feel I am either outdated or too advanced. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What’s the worst advice you ever received about relationships?
Answer: While growing up, I heard my relatives talk about an acquaintance who was leading a deeply unhappy marriage. She was highly appreciated in family for her remarkable patience. Her husband tortured her to the core but she never complained. She kept quiet and kept on serving her husband. Once I visited her when I was in college. At this time, I was mature enough to understand things. I observed how suffocated she felt in her life. She had suppressed all her emotional and physical needs. She was so scared of her abusive husband that she couldn't make a simple decision on her own despite being highly educated. “Why do you endure so much pain? Why don't you stand up against your husband’s brutality?” I asked her. “My patience and love will change him someday. He will realise my value. Wait and watch!” She said with a smile, while I could see her eyes glistening with tears. I felt sad but couldn't agree with her. The husband will realise her selfless love after 20 years and for 20 years, she will be in ‘Waiting’ mode. She would suffer for 20 years, hoping things will change. Enduring with patience, offering selfless love and waiting for change is the worst relationship advice one can receive. In this waiting process, a soul is crushed, a life is damaged and mental peace can be ruined. I find this waiting worst for everyone, irrespective of their gender. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why are assumptions bad?
Answer: I messaged my friend and asked if she could spare some time for me this weekend, but she didn't reply. The initial thought that crossed my mind was that she might be trying to avoid me, even though I had no information about her current situation. He didn't attend the party. Every time he provides excuses, he appears arrogant. I tend to believe this, even though I have no knowledge of his mental or financial status. These people rarely like my posts. Damn egoistic! We make these judgments without considering their social media activity or availability. My domestic help didn't show up today. I feel like she might be taking advantage of my leniency. I decide I need to be a little strict. My colleagues forgot to invite me for lunch today. I felt hurt, and I assumed that maybe I was unwanted in the group. This hurt me even more. We tend to assume. These assumptions are stories we create without having all the facts. They often stray far from the truth, and there's no guarantee that they are accurate. If you ever realize that your assumptions are causing you pain, stop assuming. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Have you ever caught your child doing something that shocked you?
Answer: At this time, my son was four. One evening, a little before sunset, I was sitting in the dining room, I saw him secretly dialing some numbers on his phone. “What are you doing, Sweetie?”, I asked softly as I felt something fishy in his eyes. “Umm…. Calling Nana.” He answered. He calls my father Nana. “Why are you calling him?” “I will ask him for medicine.” He said rolling his eyes. “For whom?” “For you.”, “What happened to me?” “You have pain in your throat. That's why you don't eat food. And your eyes are itching, that's why you get tears. I will ask Nana to give you medicine. You will be alright, Mumma.” He replied sadly. I clutched him tightly, and let the flood of my tears release the pain from my heart. This incident was just after my divorce. This little munchkin was observing things but not knowing what exactly was happening. But he always tried his best to have my smile intact. P.S.- My father is a doctor. And he was aware that I reached out to him for medicines during sickness. A picture of my son from those days: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the biggest irony of today's modern life?
Answer: I know a family and their social media accounts. In this family, old parents are staying with their son and daughter-in-law. If I watch them on social media, I see happiness overflowing. The son and daughter-in-law never miss to celebrate the parents’ birthdays and anniversaries. They click hundreds of photos together and post them on Facebook. It feels so good looking at their love for their old parents. But in reality, their parents are not that happy. When it comes to buying fruits or dry fruits for them, suddenly all become very expensive in the market, though they belong to the upper middle class and they can easily afford it. When it comes to visiting doctors for them, it's often delayed because of time and expenses. If the daughter-in-law cooks chicken at home, the worst pieces are given to the father-in-law. The old man struggles to eat though he is fond of nonveg. I wonder how deceptive social media is. Or, how cunning and diplomatic people have become. They are so much into show-offs. What do they want to prove??? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do I always end up dating the wrong guys?
Answer: Because you rush. You rush for relationships. After breaking up with someone, you immediately start looking for another relationship. You don't give time to yourself. You don't analyze your wants and needs. You don't set your destination, but catch the train whichever appears before you at the station. And here, you make a mistake. You regret your hurry when you have to get down at the wrong station. So be wise. Figure out what exactly you want from your partner. Check if you have those traits in your partner while dating them before indulging in them emotionally. Never become so thirsty that you drink from any cup that's presented to you. Be selective, be smart, be wise. Be pragmatic. Be clear with the person you are going to date. Tell them what you expect from them and if they don't meet your expectations, you will not continue the relationship. That's a deal. This way, you will not only have your mental peace, but you will also give them a clear picture of the future. They will not feel offended or cheated when you move on, considering them not suitable for you. However, I will again say the same thing - give some time to yourself. Don't rush. Accept yourself and learn to live life on your own first. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why are parents so picky about who their kids hang out with?
Answer: When I was a teenager, I spent time with a girl my age who came to his father's grocery shop every evening. The shop was near my house. I enjoyed her company. We talked and laughed together. At this time, her father left the shop for other work, and she handled the shop alone. I enjoyed looking at how she weighed the grains or potatoes and sold them to the customers. One evening, my father, an eminent doctor, saw me giggling with her. He didn't say anything then, but at night, he advised me to focus more on my studies instead of spending time with that girl. I kept quiet and followed his advice. I lessened my visits to her shop. I started reading books and newspapers or memorizing new English words from the dictionary. However, I didn't understand my father's intention at that time. But now I get it. In her family, nobody was educated. There was no environment for studies. There was no intellectual talk. She was herself a below-average student. Later, she studied until the 10th and got married. If my father had not advised me at the right time, I might have been influenced by her lifestyle and had not focused on my career. Parents always long to see their children in better positions. They know good company and surroundings always matter, be it any age. Therefore, they become picky about who their children hang out with. I will do the same for my child as well. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the best tactics for dealing with haters?
Answer: Quora is the place where I frequently visit, sit with a cup of coffee, and talk to people about my opinions. If my out-of-the-box ideas helped me find some great friends here, it also got me some haters. Though the number of haters is comparatively less, their emotions are intense. They have developed a perception that I am misguiding people in the name of freedom. They write ugly comments and express their hatred for me. They have even written long answers defaming me. How do I deal with it??? I keep quiet. I don't react. I don't give explanations in defense. I listen to them only when I am sitting idle, which is the rarest thing in my life. I don't oppose them. I think of the most remarkable people in the world who were denounced by others despite being great. Why? Because ordinary people could not understand them. So, no matter how many followers I have, there will always be a group of people disdaining me. I understood this in the beginning when I started writing on social media. I understood that I couldn't change people but could protect my mental peace by not reacting. So I stay calm, which brings more turmoil to my haters' life. Right? My haters would be agreeing with this. P.S.- I have worked hard to develop my thoughts. During college, I sat with my professor for hours to gain wisdom, who squeezed me in return with his strictness. I read several books to understand life. I speak what those brilliant people taught me. I can not change my thoughts to align with a bunch of people. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you know that most people don’t?
Answer: Even a stopped clock is right twice a day. I had read it in one of Paulo Coelho's books long ago. The more I analysed this statement, the newer conclusions I reached. And the outcome of my analysis is that there is nothing wrong in this world. Last month, I was bashed by trolls on Quora. They got a notion that I supported extramarital affairs in one of my writings, though I talked about something else. However, I also realized there is nothing wrong with an extramarital affair. I know a man who married an abusive wife and is dying every day. He meets another woman who is loving, kind, and compassionate towards him. He falls in love with her. Now, people would say he should divorce his current wife because he is doing unethical work as an extramarital affair. But he can't divorce. His wife is not letting him go. If he asks me for advice, I would say - Continue your affair with another woman because you have all the right to find solace for yourself. You deserve to live happily. Life is too short. So it would be best if you did something that alleviates your suffering. I appreciate you for this audacious step. Everyone on this planet is leading a different life. Their circumstances are different. We don't know who is going through what. So, one concept or social norm (be it marriage, monogamy, etc.) cannot apply to everyone. So I say - Nothing in the world is ever completely wrong, my dear. Even a stopped clock shows the correct time twice a day. You need to change your perspective to look at things and go deeper before generalizing something for the masses. I hope this helps. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you get worried about how you look?
Answer: For me, appearance matters a lot. When you meet someone, appearance is the first thing that gets noticed. When you go out and meet people, you must be well-maintained. Being well-maintained doesn't mean you wear tons of makeup or put on expensive clothes, but you should have some glow in your face, your hair is neatly combed, and your clothes are ironed. Your footwear should be clean and comfortable. I get worried if these things are not in a place for me. I wish to look good; trust me, you receive extra attention from your surroundings by looking good. The doctor will listen to your complaints more patiently. If you are a student, teachers will pay you more attention, considering you a decent student. Your colleagues may feel drawn towards you and talk to you more friendly. No one likes messy people or things. An example here - When you visit a stationary or toy shop, the most beautiful, colorful items will first catch your attention. They might be useless for you, but you feel drawn towards them and pick them up to check once. And if you are not like that useless toy, your look will be an addition to your talent. You will quickly create a place for yourself in people's minds. So look good, look smart. Polish your personality and be presentable to the world. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is one thing you hate about the mentality of Indians? Why?
Answer: When I talk about women's empowerment, I emphasize equal opportunities at work and career and equality in behavior, attitude, and action. I advocate the complete freedom for women. But Indians don't like it. Indians can easily digest: However, a woman can not be accepted doing the same. In the Indian mindset, a woman is portrayed as an idol of virtues. She is a goddess of purity. She is not supposed to love, romance, and have sex as if the term "commitment" came to the surface only for her. Here, morality is a burden only to be shouldered by women. Once, a woman was highly denounced in my hometown for having an extramarital affair. Nobody focused on her background. Her husband was an alcoholic and hardly paid attention to her. So she fell in love with someone who paid attention to her. What is wrong with that? But Indian mentality called her a slut. And they would call me a slut, too, as I support that woman. Their insensitivity to accepting women as women amazes me to the hilt. They forget that a woman is just a co-living human with the same sensuality, feelings, and emotions as men, in fact more than men. They, too, have the right to slip and melt as often as they find someone suitable. But alas! Indian mentality miserably fails to understand this. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If you could write a love letter to any food or drink, what would you choose, and what would you say?
Answer: Dear Fruits, I want to express my gratitude and affection to you through this letter. I want to tell you how much I feel for you. I love to see you in the fruit basket that I place on my dining table. I fall for you for being so colorful when I open my fridge. My days are incomplete without you. I become cranky when I don't savour you. You are so caring by nature. When I suffer from acid reflux, you are the one who takes the utmost care of me. You have already healed me to some extent. My body feels at its best when I add you to my meals. I am thankful to nature for gifting you to us. If I have nothing to eat or feel too lazy to cook, or I need to carry some snacks while going out for a few hours, I immediately turn towards you. You are my savior - so easily available to me. I adore you, really! And yes, I miss you when you are not around or become unreachable sometimes due to high cost. Love you for being always there for me. And I recommend everyone to fall in love with you. You are much better than Mr. Noodles and his wife Mrs Pasta or Mr. Samosa and his children Chaat-Pakoda. You are irreplaceable! Yours Anshu. P.S.- I love to click pictures of my fruit bowls. The attached pic is from my mobile camera.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you give me some wisdom for everyday life?
Answer: If you want to achieve something in life - be it your career, business, relationship, or some particular goal - don't reveal to anyone. Because your aspiration is just like a seed that is vulnerable in the beginning, wanting to sprout. If you share it with others in the beginning itself, you may receive a hundred pieces of advice. And you will be confused about which to pick and which to drop. You may also receive some demotivating ideas from others that will kill your enthusiasm for nurturing the seed. So, if you want to achieve something, you work on it secretly. You reveal it only when you get confident about it and are determined to have it or obliterate it from your life. At this time, other's opinions might help you strengthen your decision, or you would be able to shun them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is love to you? What do you think loving someone means?
Answer: “Will you be in my life forever?" she asked. “Yes, love, I want to live with you forever", he answered, gathering her in his arms. "I will end up in a mental hospital if you ever leave me." She confessed while tears rolled down her cheeks. "Then, we both will be in a mental hospital." He said firmly. She looked straight into his eyes and then melted back into his arms. The sheet, the pillows, and the subdued light in the room witnessed two souls becoming one. Loving someone means accompanying them throughout the journey of life. "I want to explore the world. Though I love you, I can't give you commitment because of my aspirations." She said. "Commitment? Unfortunately, this word doesn't exist in my dictionary. I am not willing to cage you. I want you to soar high and touch the sky - with or without me. I love and will love you no matter where you go." He said, smiling. Loving someone means giving them absolute freedom to grow. Buddha said, "You don't pluck a flower if you love it." "I don't want ever to become a trouble or burden for you, but a home where you come to feel relaxed. I wish to be your calm." She said. And upon hearing this, he kissed her neck gently and fondled her from the back. Loving someone means giving them peace. Love is an unselfish act by which you want to achieve only one thing - your lover's happiness. You become a giver - A giver who doesn't expect anything in return. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you do if your parents say that society is more important for them than their child's happiness?
Answer: "Society is my foot." I had said this to an acquaintance at 16, leaving him in awe when he was lecturing me on our association with society. And I still follow the same. I love my parents and respect them. Even I seek their approval on my decisions. But they don't thrust their opinions upon me. They know that I can not pursue anything mindlessly - be it my elders, their ideology, religion, society, etc. This is my life, absolutely mine. God has given me a brain, too, to analyze things. Then what is there to follow in others’ footsteps? I would rather prefer to walk my own path. During my graduation days, I learned that society is a group of people. So, people in the group can be foolish, too. We don't have to listen to them just because they are in the majority. In my life, I have experienced that no matter how good you are, you will be judged. People are always there to find a fault in whatever you do. If it is so, then why bother society? Why not collect so much courage to live on your own? This is what I believe. Answering your question, my parents have never forced me to do anything. But yes, they are not like me. They feel answerable to the society. However, when it comes to their child's happiness, they value it more than society. I am blessed. Thank you for A2A. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What things would you never want to change about India?
Answer: Years ago, I was living in a rented flat in Bangalore. A newly married couple shifted to the flat downstairs. Initially, it was tough to mingle with each other as both families belonged to different cultures and languages. However, my child (1.5 years old) mitigated this distance. The couple grew fond of him, and their house became his favorite place to explore. We couldn't realize when we women got closer and started sharing our feelings. She was highly ambitious and was preparing for competitive exams. She often shared her worries and aspirations with me and asked for guidance. Once, my mother offered her some homemade snacks, which she greatly liked. The next day, when I got back from the office, I learned that my mother spent hours in her house cooking the same snacks for her. After a year of this togetherness, I shifted to a new house. It's been six years since we saw each other, but we are still in touch and talk with the same warmth whenever possible. Thanks to technology! We Indians can find companionship everywhere. We start a relationship with our new neighbors by sharing snacks or through kids and soon become a family for a lifetime. I wish we Indians never change and continue this forever. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why aren’t some women interested in marriage anymore?
Answer: I am eligible to answer this question as I feel no more interested in marriage. I once had a failed marriage, and with a lot of struggle, I succeeded in coming out of it. Now, I don't want to be trapped by this again because the institution called marriage seems like a prison to me. Adjusting with a person who is not compatible with me is a pain. In Indian marriages, a woman doesn't have to adjust only with her husband but with his whole family. And the family politics suffocates me. Convincing the partner about how virtuous I am and constantly trying to prove myself true is a bootless errand. Instead, I prefer to utilize my time and energy to do something productive. Taking one's partner for granted is the most common trait in all marriages. Most of the men are never taught how to behave with their partners. They are unaware of the sensitivity of the relationship. We women are expected to contribute more to making the marriage successful. These extra expectations work like a killer for us. We feel overburdened. In our patriarchal society, husbands consider their wives their property. Wives are not allowed to live freely and are expected to get permission from their husbands for every small thing. Their individuality is often neglected. Then why not stay away from marriage? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you still like men? I am asking you this question because of your bitter experiences in the past.
Answer: Ah! A lot. Yes, I had terrible experiences with men in the past. They couldn't be loyal to me, so I developed bitter feelings about them. However, I couldn't hate the whole man community. I have always been welcoming to them. But I understand your question about where it is coming from. As a psychology student now, I am learning how our thought process is affected by our past experiences and how we become biased about a particular thing. However, I have not let my past make me a critic of this community. Let me tell you what I feel about men. I find them adorable. As a friend, men have been immensely good and supportive to me. Some men have been wise, and I have often turned towards them seeking guidance. Some seemed to be great lovers too. I come across men who are composed and confident. They attract me a lot. They have strong willpower and can make decisions for their life. I admire their guts. I have loved my dad. He is the best father who has always tried to make my life better. I have a brother-in-law, a genuine man, who has always supported me. Then, I had some lovely friends from this gender who always encouraged me to do better. They helped me in my career and showed me the right path. Some of my male readers are amazingly brilliant. With their beautiful hearts, they make me realize not all men are the same. I cannot have prejudice and hate all men just because of a few. I am not looking for a husband, and I don't think I will ever be because I don't need a man to take care of my wallet. If I ever need a man, I will need him to fill my life with colors and happiness because they have the capability to do so. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is life without a husband?
Answer: When my child was born, my husband was in a different city for two years. At that time, no work-from-home was given. I was handling everything all alone with the help of a nanny at home—office, home, and baby. I had many sleepless nights and dozed off in the office while working. I was busy on weekends, taking my mother-in-law to hospitals for regular checkups. I stepped out of my marriage when my child was three. Since then, It has been tough managing everything single-handedly. All these years, I have been too occupied with my daily chores. I have no time for myself. I am responsible for each and everything that happens in my life. I have no one to blame and claim. No matter how sick I am, I must work and care for my child. I have to cook, clean, teach, fulfill his demands, and the list goes on and on. Sometimes, I feel how difficult everything is when I drive alone late at night for any emergency. I have no one to ask me to sit at home and do the work on my behalf. So, life without a husband is challenging. Many of my female readers wish to know about life after divorce. I say - Go for divorce only if you have the zeal to survive and prove your worth; otherwise, you will break. You will have lots of mental peace after separation, but there will be other adversities, too, and you will need to learn how to tackle them. Life will be stable once you learn this skill and gain confidence. But it takes time. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you give homeless people money? Why or why not?
Answer: I would be 8–9 years old. One evening, I was playing outside the home under the supervision of our servant. He was 17. A bit harsh by nature. Our house was a beautiful bungalow. There was a big orchard on the left side of the house and a prominent Shiva temple on the backside. We didn't have any houses in the neighborhood. Suddenly, a saint (Sadhu) came to the temple. After performing prayers, he stood in front of our house gazing at it and asked me if my mother was available at home. Before I could say anything, the servant asked him what was the matter. "I am hungry. I need food. Call the lady of the house." He said firmly. The evening had darkened. The servant suspected him to be a thief or an impostor. "Nobody is there at home. You can leave." he said to the old man. The older man requested a few more times, but the servant had made up his mind to keep him from reaching my mother. He then left quietly. I ran home and explained everything to my mother. She got upset. My father had just returned home from his clinic. Mom asked him to find the older man immediately. My father started his scooter and drove in the same direction the older man had walked in. After going for 500 meters, he found him and brought him back home. My mother offered him food, and he slept on the veranda of our nursing home that night. This incident impacted me a lot. My parents believed that God can come to you in any form. You should not miss him. My mother always served the strangers who came home asking for food, money, or clothes. Once, my aunt even scolded Mom for this behavior. On this, my mother said everyone has their own share. We are just messengers of God to give them their share. So I, too, help people. I give them money or food, whatever I have, believing that I am not doing anything but just giving them their share. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: My husband beats me and I applied for a divorce. Now he is asking for forgiveness. What should I do?
Answer: Then forgive him. Forgive him, forget him, and move on with your life. I will never advocate an abusive partner - be it physical or mental abuse. It can not be accepted. Be it once, twice, or on a frequent basis - again not acceptable at all. So, proceed with divorce. We get life once, and we have all the right to relish it. We must not let anyone fill our life with miseries. We deserve happiness. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you like most about your son or daughter?
Answer: My seven-year-old boy is a good observer though he seems carefree and playful. Chicken momo is his favorite street food. I get him once a month. Recently, one evening, he demanded momos, and I took him to a shop nearby. I ordered one plate that consists of eight momos. I quickly finished two and wiped my hands with a tissue, leaving the rest for him. After eating the fourth, he asked me to eat the remaining two. "No, no, you eat. You love momos. You should eat." I said. “But I am full, Mumma. You take it." He persuaded me. As I always avoid overeating for him, I picked up one and asked him to finish another. Later, back home, he cheerfully explained how much he relished the momos. "I felt like eating all the momos of the shop." He exclaimed. "Then why did you ask me to eat if you liked it so much?" I asked wondering. "Because you should also eat. You didn't eat and gave me all." He replied while kicking his football in the living room. And I kept wondering if this little munchkin really thinks about me so much. He has witnessed all my ups and downs as a single mother, but I didn't expect him to become this considerate and sensitive at this age. He has given me many such surprises so far, for which I am immensely grateful to the universe. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Anshu Bharti throws light on women's miseries in a marriage and writes about how much they suffer due to the negligence of their insensitive husbands. Trolls: She is a fake feminist. Anshu Bharti writes about her depression and miseries to motivate people going through the same. Trolls: She is trying to gain sympathy. Anshu Bharti often mentions her achievement of writing a self-help book because she wants others to work on their passion, too. Trolls: She is a braggart. Anshu Bharti admires men in her writing as she finds them adorable and a source of happiness in women's lives. Trolls: She is a pervert. Anshu Bharti says divorce is beautiful as it is much better than living in a loveless marriage. She advocates a life of absolute freedom and criticizes social constraints. Trolls: She provokes men and women against the most sacred institution called marriage. Anshu Bharti appreciates the men who proposed to her.
