Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the difference between settling for things and accepting the way things are?
Answer: I grew up observing my maternal grandmother, who has been very calm all her life. My grandfather has been an angry, dominating husband who has learned only to rule. During my childhood, I saw him losing his temper and shouting at my granny. But she always stayed calm and serene. She never raised her voice and was always ready to serve him. Why? Because she accepted the circumstances, she wholeheartedly accepted an angry man as her husband. And then, she was at peace. She had no complaints, no regrets, and no sadness. She only focused on her duties. However, I was resentful, cranky, and sick when I was in a marriage. I was unhappy and full of complaints. At times, I was suicidal too. Because I had no guts to come out of this toxic marriage, I was trying to settle with my circumstances, which was causing a lot of pain to me. I had lost my peace. Settling with the situation is often against one's wish - a compromise, whereas accepting the situation shows one's willingness to adjust and adapt to the circumstances. I hope this clarifies the difference. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is one thing you just don't understand?
Answer: Why do people speak ill about others? I come across a lot of trolls on Quora. They denounce the writer in the comment section for their out of box opinions. Sometimes, there is no controversy in their writing. Still, the writer is criticized brutally. The criticism is often baseless if you scrutinize it closely. In our day-to-day life also, you will come across many people speaking ill about others. They may be your neighbors, relatives, colleagues, or family members. They have not learned to move on. They find it difficult to stop reacting. They don't understand that not everything is for them. Sometimes, somewhere, they just need to be quiet. Demeaning others will take you nowhere. If you don't like something or someone, please shun it. Observe good things in others, absorb them, and ignore the rest. That's it! Focus on your life. Concentrate on your growth and figure out what you can do to improve your personality, living standard, or anything you consider for improvement. Please use your time and energy wisely. They are precious. P.S.- By writing ugly comments, you don't denounce the writer but publicly announce your low level of thinking. Mind it! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do I get rid of this laziness and procrastination?
Answer: I would be 12–13. I was studious and ambitious. I wanted to secure the first rank in every class, for which I worked hard. I woke up early morning to read the chapters before the teacher taught them in class. However, I felt too lazy to wake up early in the winter. It was too cold and foggy. I wanted to get up and study but couldn't. I was disappointed. My uncle, a doctor and a visiting teacher in a high school, came to my home every day to teach me English and Sanskrit at 5:30 am. I shared my disappointment with him and asked for his advice. "Every human has Ram and Ravan in his body. Lord Ram is the sign of virtue and goodness. He wants you to wake up early and do the good work. He wants you to spread positivity in the world, whereas Ravan is evil and doesn't want you to progress in life. He is your enemy. He is dominant and wants you to procrastinate. Now, it's up to you who you listen to - your friend or your enemy????" he said. I am in my 30s now, and I still hate Ravan, whom I considered my enemy during childhood. I can't listen to a person who wishes ill for me. And therefore, I wake up. I do the task that I am willing to do. I am still ambitious and want to do many things in my life without listening to Ravan. Now, it's your turn to decide who you want to listen to - Ram or Ravan??? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Have you ever been proposed to on Quora?
Answer: On average, one proposal per day. Not kidding, it's true, and this is why I have almost stopped reading messages. I have more than 1500 messages to read, and I am afraid of opening them. I get proposals from men from their 20s to late 50s. They are brilliant. I find them passionate and composed. They try to find me everywhere - Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, and Instagram. I receive their messages on all the platforms wherever I have my account. I wonder how they search for me. I feel blessed to have so many lovers across the world who find me valuable and wish to have me as their partner. Sometimes, my eyes are moist reading their heartfelt messages, and I find it difficult to reject their proposals. I want to say sorry to those amazing men. I have become a flowing river that doesn't have a destination. It knows only to flow without stopping anywhere. Though it has learned to appreciate merges on the way, it doesn't want to get stuck with them. With my past experiences, I have become onerous. I can't afford to lose my individuality. I am a free soul now with a lot of aspirations. Because of this, I may not be liked by a man in the long term if I get into a relationship with him. So I look forward to living in my own cocoon. Thank you so much for loving me. I value your emotions and feelings with the same depth as you do. Please keep me in your heart forever. Thank you again. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What was common 25 years ago but has vanished today?
Answer: When the bus stopped, and my maternal grandfather got down, I shrieked with joy. I left my friends with whom I had been playing for an hour and ran home to inform my mother about his sudden arrival. My mother, who was busy preparing for evening snacks and dinner, left all her work and rushed to the dressing table to pretty herself a bit. It was all unexpected. We did not have a phone or mobile through which our relatives could inform us about their arrival beforehand. But we didn't have any complaints and immensely felt happy to see them. We fed them whatever we could by changing our menu after their arrival, and they relished every morsel. The way we welcomed our guests earlier is something that totally vanished today. We feel annoyed if we have unexpected guests without prior notice. Our lifestyle has changed so much that we find it difficult to spare time for our guests. And the unexpected guests often bring us adversity. Am I right? Let me post a recent picture of me with my maternal grandfather who is in his 80s now.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What small thing can tell you a lot about a person?
Answer: "Madam, whatever fruits you want, take today only. I will not open the shop for the next two days.” the fruit vendor said with a smile. "Why are you taking leave? Going to meet your girlfriend, ahan?" I asked, making fun of him. "Hahaha! No Madam, no girlfriend. I have my birthday tomorrow, so I am going to my hometown." He said, arranging the apples and pomegranates in their rows. "Oh great, happy birthday, Brother!" "But, Madam, I had a girlfriend. I broke up with her recently." He revealed. "Oh, that's sad, brother." "She didn't understand me, Madam. She only wanted my time. I am just 26 and want to focus on work for a better life because I don't wish to repeat the same life that my poor father lived. I sell fruits in the evening, and during the day, I do other business. On Sunday, I wash the cars in an apartment. But I made sure that I met her every Friday. Still, she was not happy." He said in one breath as if he desperately wanted to be heard. I could see the pain in his eyes. He must be a loving partner but focused on his work too. He is willing to beat the odds by working hard. He impressed me with his attitude. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your opinion on saying "I don't know" when your child asks you a question?
Answer: "Mumma, which ocean has more fish?" My child asked when I was cooking lunch yesterday. "Ummm…..no idea, Sweety," I said. "Google it, please, and let me know. I think it is the Indian Ocean." He said and quickly handed over the phone to me. This didn't happen only yesterday but many times in the past. Sometimes I didn't know how to explain an Olympiad reasoning question to him though I knew the answer. Then I called my brother-in-law for help. And I do all the research in his presence because I don't feel the need of proving myself a genius. I love to be honest with him. He is seven and understands that nobody knows everything. We can lack knowledge, and there is nothing to be embarrassed about. We should strive to gain knowledge however we can. My child and I together research on unknown and find an answer. This helps us become a team. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Will a memory remain with me forever?
Answer: Recently, I was talking to a friend when I told him how I used to roam all alone contemplating things or events during my childhood. In the backyard of my house, I often walked alone, repeating things in my mind that happened recently or I heard from someone. That repetition in my mind helped me remember things for decades. When I wrote my book, 'Towards A Better Life', and mentioned many events of my life in it, my sister was quite surprised to read them. Because she had forgotten those events and wondered how I still remembered them. Though it was a pleasant experience, she felt a few never occurred. I had to remind her of them by adding some past and future things related to those events. Memory remains with us only when they are replayed in our minds. Over and over again. Otherwise, they are forgotten. The more you are attached to something, the more you happen to recall them in the future. This is how memory works. In my subconscious mind, I always loved aloneness though I didn't understand its meaning or importance during childhood. I isolated myself from others and spent time thinking about things, events, and people, though I didn't do it deliberately. So - yes, a memory can remain with you forever if you are deeply attached to it. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do we need friends in life?
Answer: A few days ago, I had some trouble at work. I felt low throughout the day, and by afternoon, I realized I was being trapped by low spirits again, which I didn't want to happen this time. I didn't want to feel depressed. So with my moist eyes, I ran to the terrace expecting my neighbor's child there. He is just four and cheers me up with his broken words and cute yoga steps whenever I see him. Sometimes he comes to the terrace with his mother to play with his toy cars. I desperately wanted to meet him to get rid of my low feelings, but to my disappointment, he didn't turn up. After waiting some time, I returned and sat on the sofa, figuring out what to do next. I realized I could call a neighbor friend who didn't visit me for long. She has joined a new job and has been busy all these months. I wondered if she would come. However, I called her, and she was at my home within a few minutes. We talked, smiled, and had tea together. I explained to her the reason for my stress. She didn't give me any advice, but venting out in front of someone gave me instant relief. I felt better and restored. I was immensely grateful to her for this visit. So yes, we need friends. Friends can alleviate your pain and give you instant energy. Speaking to them, you can forget all your worries and stress. So be always thankful to your friends. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What makes you feel small?
Answer: I have been suffering from severe back pain for the last two weeks. I am unable to bend. Sometimes, due to this pain, I feel weak and sleepy. I need to buy a better chair for work which I have been postponing for a long due to its cost. In my daily conversation with Mom, I casually told her about my back pain and the need for a better chair. And the next day, I got a call from my sister asking to buy a chair urgently as it was mom's order. "Buy the best one and tell me the cost. Dad will send you money." She said. With a lump in my throat, I kept denying this offer as my mom always broke her FDs to help me like this. But my sister didn't agree. What makes me feel small? My parents' selfless love often makes me feel very small. They are always ready to give without expecting anything in return. I never share my financial worries and difficulties with them. In fact, I boast of having a lot, but they still understand. I wonder who will think about me like this after they are gone or how I will survive without them. I am short-tempered and get angry at them very soon, but they never keep grudges. They forgive and forget. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is fear a good or bad thing?
Answer: My child is not good at eating. He often comes home from school with leftovers in his lunchbox. I have frightened him, saying that if he continues wasting food, the god of food will be upset. And one day, god will stop giving him food as punishment. He is now afraid of it and tries to finish his meals. On the other hand, I teach him not to fear anyone when expressing himself. Speak up when you are right. A few days ago, he showed me his notebook where his teacher had written in bold, "Cheating." There was a test in the class. He told me that he had written all the answers independently, but at the end, he was checking in the book to see if he had written correctly. But the teacher mistook him. "Didn't you tell the truth to the teacher?" I asked. "She scolded me. She didn't listen and left." He said. I could see the fear in his eyes. He was afraid of the teacher at school, and now he was scared of me. I consoled him and explained that he didn't have to be afraid of anyone if he had not done anything wrong. "You must keep your point, else you would be mistaken," I told him. Fear is an emotion, and every emotion has its value. There is nothing in the world that can be completely wrong or bad. I gave you two examples here. In the first example, fear is executed to have a better outcome; in the second example, fear must be dropped off. If it's not done so, one can be crushed. I hope this helps. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is the joy of giving the greatest joy of life?
Answer: Did you watch the advertisement for Brook bond red level tea? At the hospital, an older woman offers tea to a guy whose father is admitted. He is upset and worn out. He first rejects her offer, but later the aroma of the tea tempts him to accept the offer. After drinking this homemade tea, he feels refreshed and cheerful and asks her if she has anyone admitted to the hospital. "No, I don't have anyone here. I just come for people like you every day who seem tired of staying continuously in the hospital for their loved ones. I feel happy offering them my tea", She says and smiles. You can see the satisfaction on her face. This is just an ad, but it is true for some people who find their joy in giving. Those givers are always cheerful and carefree, and become a source of happiness for others. Here, I attach the video of the advertisement for your curiosity. This is my favorite ad on TV. I hope you like it too. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some harsh realities of life?
Answer: When you are easily reachable, you are taken for granted. A woman was going through a painful marriage. Getting abused by her husband had become a daily ritual in her life. She was depressed and suicidal. She wanted to quit but survived. The reason for her survival was another man who came to her life as a savior. Let's call him X. X was in love with her. He hated to see her in pain. Whenever they met, he cared about her like no one could. She was overwhelmed by this gesture and eventually fell in love with him. However, she didn't want to leave her husband. Divorce seemed a big deal to her. She rejected the proposal of X, but X was madly in love. The more she appeared determined by her decision, the more desperate X felt for her. Finally, she took a bold step and divorced her husband. She then married X. After six months, she observed his fondness for her drastically reduced. She often felt unwanted. She had no clue what went wrong in this relationship. Let me now tell you what happened. Humans are strange. When a thing seems unreachable to them, they feel desperate. And when they get a hold of it, they take it for granted. They forget its value. This can happen to anyone, irrespective of their gender. The essence of this write-up is that many of us fail to value things when they are easily available to us as X did above. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Should you ever give up on the person you're madly in love with?
Answer: Finding a doting lover and being a doting lover are two different things. In many cases, both don't exist together. You may love your partner unconditionally, and your partner may not reciprocate the same. Or, your partner is extremely fond of you, and you may wonder about their craziness because you don't have the same feelings. However, if both partners are equally in love, there's no point in giving up. Giving up on such a relationship will be the most unfortunate thing one can do. Receiving love is easy. Most of us are receivers, and very few of us are givers. If you are capable of loving someone deeply and fondly, you can experience spirituality. You can feel the love in a true sense. You will be free from expectations and attachments. Such feelings are heavenly. If they truly exist, I don't think I will ever give up on the person I am in love with, no matter whether that person is available in my life or not. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What's something you don't "get"?
Answer: I know some people in my surroundings who are very moody. I have a habit of smiling at people if I know them even a little. I love to greet them. I grew up in a small town where people had concerns for each other. They didn't forget to greet each other whenever they met. They smiled and asked about how things were going at their end. In a city like Bangalore, some people are strange and unusual. They are super reserved and refrain from talking to others as if people are suffering from some infection, and it will spread if they have eye contact or exchange smiles. It amazes me to think how insensitive people are becoming nowadays. I get to see some people daily. Sometimes they answer my hello, and other times, they ignore me as if they have to pay some penalty if they do so. To my surprise, these people never take the initiative of greeting first. If I don't greet them, they won't. They pretend to be too busy. Looking at their faces, I get scared. There seems to be no ease in their life. Their faces are hanging, and they look depressed. I wonder if all are suffering from depression or if they are too arrogant to mingle with others. I am still looking for an answer. I may get the answer someday when I start treating people as a psychologist. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Life: What is the worst thing that can happen in life?
Answer: You don't live a life that you want to live: P.S. — You need to gather a lot of courage to survive in this world if you wish to live here on your terms. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you tell me something about yourself?
Answer: I always maintain a cordial relationship with people like my security guard, vegetable vendor, plumber, carpenter, aquarium cleaner, etc. I greet and talk to them whenever I meet them. I speak to their children and ask about their studies if I find them in the shop. I have even supported them financially if they needed to run their shop. No carpenter, plumber, or aquarium cleaner leaves my house without having tea and snacks. Sometimes, I give them homeopathy medicine too. They feel considered. And in gratitude, they are always ready to help me. When I restarted my life as a single mother, I panicked over small things, such as if the kitchen light was not working, I cried. If there was a leakage in the bathroom, I felt clueless and panicked. However, these people became my savior and proved to be my greatest support. They are just one call away whenever I am in need. They treat my parents, too, with respect when they meet them. "Oh! You are Anshu Madam's daddy. Please wait; I will give you quickly whatever you need." Or, "Your bag became heavy; let my staff drop it at home." They say, leaving my father awestruck. I respect people who, others think, are from the lower class. These lower-class people have bigger hearts than us. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: On what subject do you get messages practically every day these days?
Answer: How did I come out of my toxic marriage? This is the ask I have received from many readers, most of whom are women. Some of them are well-educated and even working. Their stories frighten me, sadden me and sometimes fill my heart with apathy towards men. I get to know how the husbands ignore the existence of their wives in the same house. They talk and lead a cordial relationship with every member of the family except for the wife. Some men need their wives only in bed. They do it forcefully, and some are too cold to have sex. They don't intimate for 8–9 months and live like strangers under one roof. I experience pain while reading the messages from these women. They feel depressed and unwanted. Some are seeing a therapist. However, they have no guts to follow the instructions given by the therapist because the therapist asks them to move on from their toxic marriage. I get such messages on a daily basis. And I wonder how I should console them. I try to guide them with my past experiences, but I hesitate to ask them to go for divorce because the life of a single mother is not full of roses. However, a question arises: why are some men so insensitive and careless? And if they are so insensitive, why do they go for marriage? At times, I feel agitated to hear about those careless men. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: My mother-in-law is 70, but she is constantly looking younger and even wears mini skirts. How do I tactfully explain to her that her time has already passed?
Answer: I have a dream. When I would be in my 40s, I will color my hair, and I will cut my hair short in my 50s. If I were alive, I would continue wearing my shorts even in my 60s and 70s. I wish to look young, beautiful, and energetic. I will keep myself updated with current affairs, fashion, and style to gel with all kinds of people. No matter how old I grew, I would prefer to look smart, confident, and impressive. This is how I look forward to living in my old age. And I will hate it if someone preaches to me, stating that my days are gone. It will be like they are trying to limit me and my potential, which I find ugly. No one has the right to cut my wings and restrict my freedom to live as I wish. So answering your question, I would say - you have no authority to advise your mother-in-law how she should live. This is her life, and she has all the right to relish it. You need to put a full stop to your orthodox thoughts and let others live as they wish. Please don't cap anyone's freedom. P.S. - I am in my 30s and love fashion. And I will not like it if someone instructs me what to wear and what not. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it bad to date right after a breakup?
Answer: After my divorce, I started getting advice from people to find someone and get married again. Such advice made me laugh. My soul was crushed, and it needed to be healed. For that, I needed space and time. How could I look for a partner? If you haste in dating, possibilities exist for being trapped by a toxic relationship again. Since you have not recovered from your previous relationship, you may see the old patterns in your new relationship and feel frustrated. Your expectations may be too high that the new person may find them toxic. And it wouldn't be your fault as you suffered and don't want to suffer again. After your breakup, you couldn't have enough time to analyze what went wrong that you need to work on in the future. So, it would be best to take some time before you date again. You must learn that you don't have to find someone to get happiness. Happiness is within you. You need a partner who can be an addition to your happiness, not a reason for your happiness. Also, you need to gain the confidence you lost in your previous relationship. So work on yourself. Be capable of facing the challenges that life throws at you. It's you, only you, who can accompany you until the end. Finding a partner is just an addition. When you understand the above, you will be able to find the right person for yourself. I bet! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can living alone ever be joyous?
Answer: I relish my aloneness. Sometimes I look for company and enjoy being with people, but this doesn't affect my mental health for being alone most of the time. I have aspirations and goals I wish to achieve, and living alone helps me focus on them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you absolutely love in life?
Answer: Having a great companion with whom I can talk for hours and hours. I never had anyone with whom I could experience this in my previous relationships. Either they were not interested in having a deep conversation, or they were just too ordinary to understand the depth of my mind. I once read somewhere that one should choose a partner with whom they can walk miles and talk for hours. If this trait exists in the relationship, they will never be lonely. Consider yourself fortunate if you ever find someone with whom your wavelength matches. You don't need to have a lot of similarities with them, but there should be a point where you both become one because your minds ultimately think in the same direction, and your hearts crave the same depth. When I read the thoughts of some writers and philosophers, dead or alive, I feel incredibly connected to them. I wish they were alive. I wish I could meet someone like them in this life. And then, life would have been absolute bliss! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should I do if I heard people start gossiping about me?
Answer: Recently, I heard something that made me split my sides. A relative told my mother what other relatives said about me. When I divorced my husband, they spread the rumor that I had an affair and would marry that guy after my divorce. Four years have passed since the separation, and I am still single. However, in these four years, my life became more stable; I gained more freedom, happiness, and peace and established myself as an author. The imaginary guy my relatives saw in their dreams didn't meet me yet, and I am sure he wouldn't ever meet me. Because my taste differs from my relatives, I will definitely not like a guy of their choice and imagination. So I laugh. I enjoy their gossip. And have fun with their rumors. Because I prefer to work on my aspirations rather than pay attention to the blabber of others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: My boyfriend called me ugly during an argument then told me his friend thought I was ugly too. What do I do?
Answer: Recently I read an article written by Srinath Nalluri where he says - Red flags will remain red flags only, no matter how many good things take place in the relationship. And I agree with him. Some people lose their minds in anger, which is acceptable, but it doesn't provide them the right to demean others. Belittling your partner in the relationship is mental harassment. For me, it's a kind of crime because it gives a scar for a lifetime. I am ugly, average-looking or beautiful - didn't you analyze this before saying yes to me for the relationship? If not, you are mindless and act on an impulse. I can not be with you at all. Once, I was sitting with my relatives, and we discussed marriage. They talked about adjustment, which the wife must do because her husband is the one who ultimately cares about her. He is a man with lots of work stress in mind. If he shouts at his wife because of his frustration, the wife should understand him. Then only a marriage can work. And they concluded by saying that marriage is all about adjustment. This kind of adjustment? I bewildered. If marriages are based on give and take policy, then this should be implemented to love, respect, and compassion too. If you love and respect me, I will reciprocate the same or vice versa. By marrying you, I didn't give you authority to demean, belittle or hurt me, no matter how disturbed you are in your personal life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the one story your parents always tell about you?
Answer: I was a crybaby. I had the stamina to cry at a stretch for hours. Without taking a break. I could cry the whole night. I woke up and cried when the cradle stopped moving. So my mother had to tie one end of the string in her leg, which was attached to the cradle. She moved her feet to move the cradle during her sleep. The moment the cradle stopped, I cried. People could easily irritate me and watch a cry show and giggle. While crying, I should not be left alone. If I didn't get the attention, I banged my head on the floor or against the wall. So my head was always swollen. If one part was swollen, I made sure I banged it with another part. My mom kept a homeopathy medicine (Arnica) handy for this hurt. So I was a horribly unique child. And Mom was pissed off with me. She wanted to drop me in a bin or at a temple forever. However, my dad still adored me. I think my mother could never succeed in her plans because of him only. I hope you enjoyed the story. A true story that I am also unable to believe. And looking at this innocent face, I feel all the allegations are false. P.S.- Joking apart, my mother had numerous sleepless nights while bringing me up. Her health drastically deteriorated from then and there. I am indebted to her. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What advice have you received from a stranger?
Answer: I would be 14–15. I was traveling with my parents on a train. A middle-aged man was sitting next to me. Somehow we both indulged in some discussions. And he told me something wise that I still implement in my life. He said, "Suppose you come to the railway station to catch a train and see a huge crowd waiting for the same train. Would you get afraid thinking about how you will get on the train? If yes, you will definitely miss the train. So it would be best not to be frightened but prepared to face the circumstances. You must give it a try." At present, I am pursuing my Master's in Psychology. Every day I struggle to manage time to study; sometimes, I succeed, and other times I fail. This is still okay. However, what scares me the most is that there is a separate subject for statistics where I feel blank. If I say I don't know even 'S' of statistics, there's nothing wrong. A few days ago, I joined an online class. After explaining the formula in the first class, the teacher gave students a problem to solve, where I miserably failed. I kept asking for an explanation, but he asked me to try again. I was upset and felt like quitting, but I remembered that stranger's advice and felt like continuing with the classes. In the second class, I could solve three problems, and the teacher was impressed. "You need to plunge into the ocean if you wish to find a pearl. You can not skip the challenges in the beginning itself". Please keep me in your prayers, dear readers. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the signs that a child is logical?
Answer: My son is going to be seven soon. I have observed that he maintains his own viewpoint. He is not submissive and asks for logic for things he is asked to do. He is naughty too. I receive many complaints from his school. Such as he doesn't sit in one place in the classroom. He jumps from one bench to another. He teases his friends and plays pranks with them like he can summon a spirit with his power and so on. Teachers laugh, too, but sometimes they are annoyed. When it comes to discipline, I am stern with him. Sometimes I make him understand with moral stories and sometimes scold him. Yesterday he came from school. He has a habit of telling me everything after he is back. So he came to me while I was engrossed in my office work. “Mumma, I am sorry." "Why sorry? What happened?" I asked, gluing on the laptop screen. "Please don't scold me upon hearing this," he pleaded. I looked at him and could sense how fear had engulfed him. "What happened, Sweetie? Tell me." I asked politely. "Today, my class teacher sent me to the vice principal's room because I did something wrong." "What did you do?" I frowned. "I asked a girl in my class to pour water into her food. And she poured," he answered hesitantly. I was shocked. Furious too. "But Mumma, she is known as intelligent in the class. Doesn't she then know what she should listen to and what not? Will she jump if I ask her to jump from the window?" He asked before I could utter a word. With this question, I calmed down because he had logic. I sincerely thought about it and concluded that instead of punishing this boy, the teacher should have given practical knowledge to that girl. It's much needed to survive in this world. I smiled at his logic because he was right. However, I asked him not to repeat this. Last month, I received the below remark on him from his school, which made me proud: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your definition of "feeling at home"? Do you think there is a specific time or place that you have to be in order to feel this way?
Answer: I grew up observing my mother. She has been very open-minded. Quite lively and welcoming! We used to have a lot of guests. Their children had real fun staying at our house. Relatives who stayed nearby and some neighbors left their children/babies in our home all day, and my mother happily cared for them. They are grown up now, and whenever we meet, they reminisce on old days. "Your mother used to give us all the freedom in her house. We were free to do whatever we liked to do. She cooked delicious meals for us. We could open the kitchen snack containers and finish them in one go. She never questioned us." They say when I meet them. And I, too, remember how they enjoyed being in our house. My aunt (father's sister) visited us with her husband and children once a year, and no one would like to stay in our relative's nearby houses. They just went to them for a few hours and returned because they felt "at home," only with my mother. My mother even let the elders, like my aunt, cook in the kitchen if they wanted. "All yours, enjoy it," I think this is how my mother treated her guests. And I love this quality of hers. This makes one comfortable with the new place and gives them lifelong memories. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If you could have a conversation with any historical figure, who would it be and why?
Answer: Sai from Shirdi. He was a great Indian saint who lived with us not long ago, but just 100 years ago. I have read and watched some TV shows about him and found him highly compassionate. He helped everyone who sought blessings from him. He guided them in paths of righteousness when they poured out their tales of woe. In the human body, he was an angel — a messenger of God. A pure soul that had overcome ego, jealousy, anger and resentment. He had attained the highest level of serenity and patience, which was incredible. When I learn more about him, I feel an urge to meet him once physically. His teachings inspire me a lot to become a better human. I read that he had once said to his devotees that he would always come if they summoned him for help. There have been times when I prayed to him for help, and he heard me. I could feel him around me. He gave me the strength to put up with pain if he couldn't rescue me from it. I wish to have a heartfelt conversation with him. I want to learn from him to overcome all kinds of negativity. The way he was always ready to help people is something I aspire to do in my life. Countless people are suffering in this world. I Wish I could receive his blessings to enlighten those people. I pray to him every day to come to this earth once again. The suffering earth needs him. I am yet to read these books about him. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What funny thing did your maid ever do to you?
Answer: When I conceived, I stopped eating food altogether. I felt sick, and whatever intake I took, I vomited the next moment. So one morning, while I felt exhausted and weak, I sat near the door. I missed my mother so badly that I felt the urge to cry loudly. It was only then my cook turned up. She was a middle-aged woman who had two children. Looking at my puppy face, she sat near me and asked if I wanted to eat something special. "I feel like eating something sour, spicy. Maybe something like Rasam - rice." I said. "Oh, Madam, I don't know to cook Rasam. But in Nepal, we add lemon in our food if we like to eat sour." "Umm….Good idea! Okay, I will try today", I said, thinking of adding a few lemon drops in dal for lunch. After an hour, she was done with her cooking. While she cooked, I sat outside the house as I could not abide the smell. "Madam, food is ready. You can eat whenever you feel like eating. I am leaving now. Take care of yourself, Madam", She said. Later, when I sat to eat, to my astonishment, everything was sour. The smashed potatoes tasted like lemon. Chutney made of roasted chana dal was sour. She had added lemon even in the dal, and rice, just because I wanted to eat something sour/tart. Though I was overwhelmed by this gesture of hers, I got furious too. I couldn't even eat a bite. I called my mom and sobbed over the phone. She quickly booked her tickets and flew to Bangalore. I was happy as my good days had arrived! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best way to get revenge on someone who broke your heart?
Answer: Work on yourself until you think the world is at your feet. Create some goals. Have some aspirations and work on them with all your capability, energy, and enthusiasm. No stepping back! Gain knowledge as much as you can. This will give you visibility in the crowd. Meet wonderful people and learn from them how you can groom. Confidence will come once you establish yourself in a career. So focus on building your career. Take care of your health and skin. It would be best if you glowed both in and out. Smile! This will break your opponent's heart into pieces. Don't waste your time thinking about punishing that person. It will take you nowhere. Understand that they were not suitable for you. So move on and focus on your life. The best thing I would do if I was deceived is forgive that person. I wouldn't wish ill for them. Because my energy is precious to me, I can't waste it thinking about people who could not value me. Life is too short. Live it with grace. Work on your happiness and live like a badass. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How many dates do you usually wait before kissing a new person?
Answer: If I genuinely feel connected to a person, I may kiss him on the second date itself. Or it may take thousands of dates to kiss a person, or a kiss never takes place if I don't feel the depth with him. I am not conditioned. I am only concerned with my feelings about him. The depth of love that I look for and the quality of the person that makes him different from the crowd are things that matter to me. Nothing else! I believe in expressing love and emotions. I strongly feel that our emotions shouldn't be conditioned. P.S. — By the way, my taste is different. I don't fall for people easily. My regular Readers must be knowing it now.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is wrong with India?
Answer: There is nothing wrong with India. India is a beautiful country with its vast cultural values. If there is anything wrong, that is with people residing in this country. They are obsessed with their culture and religion. They are obsessed with their beliefs and feel they are always right. Nobody is ready to change. They think the customs followed thousands of years ago are still valid. If you try to bring change in it, they feel offended. Triggered. They don't understand that everything gets stale and rotten with time. Be it our values, customs, rituals, or beliefs. They need to be modified, renovated, or reformed from time to time; otherwise, they will spoil the whole of humankind. What was worth following fifty years ago may lose its relevance in the modern age because our requirements have changed. Our lifestyle has changed. We have different kinds of wants and needs that were not present 50 years ago. But people are not ready to accept it. If anyone tries to break the stereotype, people consider him a spoiler and ostracize him. They are not receptive to new ideas which is hindering the growth of us citizens. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the signs of maturity?
Answer: Recently, I had a conflict with someone. Just out of futile ego, she was very angry with me. I couldn't defend myself due to her position. However, I was disturbed and needed someone to hear me. Can you believe I called three friends, and none answered my call? It was late at night, and I convinced myself that they were married women who might be busy with their families. So I called them again in the morning, but still no answers! When we sit together, these friends call me babe, sweetie, and darling. To be honest, I was hurt. Because I had developed a belief that they would be there when I needed them, but they failed to prove me right with my faith. Anyways, I could easily control my bitter feelings because I realized that friends are not that important in our life. We should not give them too much value if they don't deserve it. They didn't pick up my call because they didn't find it essential. Then, I, too, should not give them a chance to take my peace. They are just casual friends. It was my fault that I considered them important and wanted to share my agony with them. I hope you get what I am trying to tell you. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I am so alone. I am depressed and lonely and have no friends or significant other. What is wrong with me that makes me so lonely in life?
Answer: For the last two days, I have been feeling like you. I was down in the dumps and had no one to share my feelings with. The more I craved someone with whom I could share my pain freely, the more I felt stifled. "I am no one's priority. No one is concerned about my well-being. There is no one to enquire if I have eaten food or slept well." this thought made me sicker. I hardly ate or drank water. I suffered from insomnia, and during office hours, I dozed off. I felt too fragile even to walk. Out of exasperation, I got furious with a little mistake of my child, yelled at him, and ended up with shedding tears. My sister from far away sensed my despairs and called me to know how I was doing. I enthusiastically exaggerated the taste of chicken soup that I had recently cooked for my child. She couldn't guess what I was going through. This is how a depressed person acts. I felt like consulting a psychiatrist this morning because my depression doesn't seem to fade. Most of the time, I am bright, chirpy, and upbeat, but occasionally, I am clutched by low spirits. And life feels static and pointless. However, in the afternoon, I picked up a storybook by Ruskin Bond and started reading it. After reading a few pages, I felt a little stable. And then, I took the chance to analyze my life, past experiences, desires, and needs. "What is the guarantee that someone (if I find one) will keep me happy?" I asked myself. In the last four years, I have worked very hard to regain my mental peace which I can't ruin by giving someone else the remote control of my life. I have seen people who brutally walked out from my life without giving notice. Come on! I can't make the same mistake. I will work on myself. I am already in love with my aloneness and a bit of loneliness - I will convert it into fulfilling solitude. If I have taken responsibility for my life, I will ensure it is more gratifying. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the coolest excuse for being late to class?
Answer: Teacher — Why are you so late, doctor? Me — Sir, I am late because we had some puja (prayers/offerings to God) at home. Teacher — So? Education is your first puja. Isn't it? Me — Mmm….Mmmm….yes, Sir. I agree with you. Teacher — then? Me — Sir, due to that puja at home, my mother did not want me to come to school today. But I fought with her and managed to come, though it was late. Teacher — Shabash! I am proud of you. Other students must learn this from you. Now, go to your seat. A grin spread across my face quickly. I heaved a massive sigh of relief and walked in with pride. Sometimes, lies save our life. P.S. — My teachers called me 'doctor' because my father is a doctor.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your biggest achievement in life?
Answer: I am capable of expressing myself on paper. Penning down my thoughts was the only thing that kept me alive during the upheaval of my life. When things were going downhill, I found solace in my pen. And I believe, this is the most valuable thing the universe could bless me with. Every morning, I thank the universe for this. My writing creates oxytocin for me, and the words leave their pheromones in my mind, keeping me elated for the rest of the day. After writing a page, I get a sudden surge of dopamine in my brain, and then I feel nothing in this world can please me more than this. I am not interested in climbing the ladder of success in the corporate world. This materialistic world doesn't fascinate me much though I seek a comfortable life. The only thing that I really aspire to do is — Write, Write, and Write. I want to write with all my heart. I wish to be known by writing. For me, writing can not be a profession. It can not be a means of making money. I see the god in this. That's why I close my eyes and offer prayers before and after writing a page in my diary or an article on Quora. For me, writing is divine. And until I am blessed with this knack, I would consider myself successful. Thank you for all your love. I am immensely grateful. P.S. — My book, Towards A Better Life, is being loved globally. Please give it a read. You will get a new perspective of looking at things that you come across in your daily life. It's available on Amazon and Flipkart: Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would surprise men about life as a woman?
Answer: While I cook in the kitchen, My son sits at the dining table outside the kitchen and reads a chapter aloud that I am listening to. I answer his questions and explain the chapter in between. I open the fridge and check what all fruits and vegetables are left and what needs to be bought when I go shopping. I make a note on my mobile. While the food is being cooked, I put clothes in the washing machine on the balcony adjacent to the kitchen. While I explain the chapter to my child, I give him a dose of medicine and cut his nails if needed. I also check Quora notifications and reply to my readers' comments. I read an article online if my child is busy re-reading a paragraph in his book. Or, I pay electricity or water bills online if pending. Amidst all the chaos, I add salt and spices to the meal I am cooking and make sure the food is nutritious and tastes better. Gosh! I don't forget to give a lecture to my child on 'how important education is' and also a lecturer to my domestic help on 'how to do dishes neatly.' We, women, are multitasking. We can do many things at once, though it's tiring and stressful. However, we do it. And this surprises most of the men. Am I right? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are we meant to do in this world?
Answer: We are meant to live how we want to live. Happily, blissfully and with abundance. We are meant to do what we love to do — no pressure from our fellow humans to do something we are uncomfortable with. We are meant to be ourselves, so we can focus on our aspirations and personal growth. We are meant to love and be loved. Love people around you as if it were your last day. Feel everything around you — air, water, stars, raindrops, and your footsteps when you walk! We are meant to live with absolute freedom, which means we are not conditioned by society. Man-made rules and regulations are ugly, and we must be free from them. We are meant to create, nurture and bloom. Be it anything — the soul in you, a child, a flower, or a painting. Or a beautiful paragraph of soothing words. We are meant to express our thoughts, ideas, and feelings with zero restrictions. The fear of being judged needs to be completely mislaid. We are meant to avail equal opportunities, freedom, and values for others we wish to have for ourselves. We are meant to live in this world without regrets, despair, jealousy, anger, competition, and frustration. For this, we have to shrug off our egos and grudges. We are meant to make this world a better place. Posting my photograph as some readers have demanded it. They say my writing gets more positive vibes if it has my picture. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What screams "I'm a middle class Indian"?
Answer: "Do you have a yoga mat?" A woman came rushing to the supermarket while I enquired about the same. "Yes, we do. You can check on the second floor." the cashier replied. We both proceeded towards the elevator as our purpose of being there was the same. "Could you please show me a yoga mat?" We both requested the stock assistant in the chorus as soon as we reached the second floor. "Yes, Mam, here are the ones." I felt elated as I didn't have to struggle more early morning. The request for a yoga mat came from my child's school last evening, and I couldn't manage to get it due to my office work. When I dropped him off at school today, I immediately thought of buying it. While I was wondering what color of the mat would impress him, the lady interrupted by asking another question to the assistant. "Don't you have smaller ones? I want to buy one for my child. I am sure the smaller one will cost lesser." She said. "No, Mam. We have only these." I could sense her concerns. However, since she had no choice, she picked up one. And I too. At the cash counter, "Sir, the price is too high. If you had a smaller one, I would have taken that and saved money." She uttered. "Sorry, Mam. But you see, there is a special price written on it. The actual price is 680 Rs, and the special price is just 550 Rs." "Ummm…could you please make it 500 Rs?" She hopelessly demanded. The cashier nodded, and I could see the brightest smile on her face for saving 50 Rs. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some morning habits that can change your day?
Answer: Walking. I go for a stroll in the morning every day. For 10, 20, or 30 minutes as time permits. During this time, while walking, I think of myself. I avoid all negative thoughts and focus on what I want from my life, what I want to do being in this world, and how I want to live. This strengthens my thought process, determination, and willpower. I get to know about the conflicts between my mind and heart. If I can fix them, I try to find a way or leave them to time. I prefer to go with the flow. In my mind, I jot down all those beautiful things I have — my writing ability, my parents, my child, a few fantastic friends, my heartwarming readers, my house, my job, water, the cool breeze blowing my hair, and the ground under my feet. I feel elated, as if I am the most affluent person in the world. This helps me discover my being, the purpose of my existence, and how to work on my aspirations. I want you also to spare 20 minutes every morning for walking when you can spend time only with yourself. At this time, you become your priority. Thank the universe for the things that you have, and show your persistence in getting the things that you want in your life. The universe will definitely grant your wish. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the most important thing in a relationship?
Answer: Recently, over coffee, I met a friend who is certainly a wise man. We talked about many things, such as career, marriage, life, the quality of coffee, and simultaneously, the quality of the relationship. The relationship sustains as long as its quality persists. Humans are designed to feel loved, wanted, and heard. They are in desperate need of — love, affection, touch, and nudges. You feel left out if your partner is insensitive and least bothered about your needs. The relationship becomes cold, and you feel low. When I was in a loveless marriage for years, I felt my confidence was declining. Initially, I tried making my partner happy, I performed stupid activities to get his attention, but gradually, I gave up. I realized one-sided efforts are futile. But this caused pain. I was often hurt and demotivated. I read somewhere a child grows more confident when he is frequently hugged, loved, and touched by his parents. Otherwise, he grows suppressed. And I was that suppressed wife. Be it a man or woman — everyone is in the same need. They wish to be recognized for love. They want their partners to reward them with hugs, touch, and love because they are designed to feel emotions. The relationship is dead if there is no emotional touch. This touch has to be both mental and physical. Your body and soul — both should be equally touched for a successful relationship. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can I move out of state with my children and then file for a divorce?
Answer: Please don't do that. This action of yours might make him aggressive. Or, he might feel deceived and refuse to give you a divorce. The decision to divorce must be mutual. If you are considering separation, I assume things are not working between you and your spouse. And you both are aware of the situation. Then, I suggest you sit with him and discuss the matter. Please let him know if you are determined not to stay with him anymore. This will prepare him for the future, and he can manage his emotions for the children if he has. He has all the right to know your intentions and plans for ending the marriage, as you have lived together for years. You can't kick him out of your life just like that. Running away with children and filing for divorce may give him bitter feelings, and he will tend to revenge. In that case, he may look for a chance to harm you. So please be sensible and sensitive too. I hope this helps. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: In your opinion, can you have two crushes?
Answer: I can fall in love with many; you are talking about crushes. You need to understand that love doesn't always take you to bed... Love is a light that is in our hearts. However, we are so deeply conditioned by society that thinking of another person while already having one seems to be a crime to us. I wonder how I should control my mind not to find beauty in someone and not fall for him. Emotions that make us vulnerable and, at times, strong and determined. How can we put a full stop to our emotions? Why can't love be free? Why can't we fall for as many as we find suitable? Nothing wrong with that. But society calls you characterless if you do so. We can control our physical needs, and I think, it should be controlled; otherwise, one can become salacious and lustful. This may create some disorder in our life. But mental or emotional needs can't be controlled. If you suppress them, you will get depressed. And you see, most men and women around us are depressed because they have been suppressing their feelings for years. Feel your heart's emotions and sensitivity, appreciate the beauty wherever you experience, and fall in love. But for this, the rule that you have to adhere is: Neither you get conditioned, nor you condition others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: How do you know if someone has poor boundaries?
Answer: An acquaintance X. He still talks to people who have hurt him a lot in the past. Those people never lose a chance to demean him while talking. But X considers it okay and forgives them. Forgiving is great, but putting one's self-esteem on the radar shows that one has not drawn lines for oneself. He is unable to say NO to people. So he often does things he doesn't want to do. He still accompanies people who are not good to him, and he doesn't like them. But he fears losing them as he thinks about who will help him in his time of need. He doesn't know that the universe will arrange something if he is destined to receive help in need. He has a high emotional attachment to someone who doesn't value him. Still, he thinks of that person and always feels sad. He has not learned how to move on in life. He allows people to interfere in his personal life, decisions, and choices that he wants to make. And finally, he never accomplishes his goals. People take him for granted. They take advantage of his silence as he cannot take a stand for himself and speak up. After reading the above, if you think you are like X, it's time for you to change. Change your personality. However, you can not bring this change overnight, it will come gradually. Step by step. Learn to have self-respect. The world will respect you once you know to respect yourself and raise your voice when needed. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How should I teach moral values to children?
Answer: "What life do you want? Sam's life or Peter's life?" "Sam's life," my child answers every time I ask him the above mentioned question. Recently, he has been demanding a toy helicopter that can fly through a remote. We had once bought this for him when he was three. I want to avoid repurchasing it because this toy is expensive. Instead of buying this, I would like to enroll him in activity classes like drawing, swimming, etc. So one day, he was cranky and insisted on buying this toy helicopter. Then I concocted a story about two friends, Sam and Peter. Peter's parents were wealthy and bought expensive toys but never gave him time. They were an unhappy couple, always fighting and keeping themselves busy with work and parties outside the home, whereas Peter spent most of his time alone at home, of course, with the expensive toys that he was very proud of. He didn't realize what he was missing in life until he visited Sam's house one evening. Sam's parents were poor, but they were super loving. His mother fed him soup while Sam talked about his school and friends. She frequently hugged him while he tried fixing his broken toy car and clapped on every fix. She hugged Peter, too, and fed him soup. It was a chirpy environment when both the friends were running in the garden, and Sam's mother was also involved in their activities. After returning from Sam's house, Peter thought of his parents, who had never been available to cheer him up. Thinking of this, he cried a lot that night and slept alone in his bedroom. After I completed the story, I asked my son, "What life do you want? Sam's or Peter's?" "Sam's," he retorted. Since that day, he stopped ranting about the toy helicopter. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your idea of a perfect relationship or a perfect marriage?
Answer: An old, experienced man was traveling on a train. In the same compartment, a couple was also traveling. They were in their early 40s. At every station, small or big, the man got down from the train and got something for the woman - Coffee, fruit, chocolate, cookies, etc. Even though the woman denied eating, the man persuaded her to have them. The older man was observing everything, and then he asked the woman about her relationship with the man at one station when he got down searching for something. "Who is he?" He asked. "He is my husband." She answered. "No, he is not your husband." The older man replied. "Why? How can you say that?" She felt a little bothered. "A husband will never do so much. You are telling a lie." The older man smiled. The woman found some affection in his smile and confessed that he was not her husband but her husband's friend who was in love with her. While telling the truth, she blushed, and the happiness on her face was quite visible. This is a story, and I am sure many of you can relate to the statement that a husband will never do so much. Because, at some point in time, marriages lose their charm. The spouses take each other for granted. Getting attention from your partner seems like a dream. That's why I mentioned once that marriages should come with expiry dates. Suppose it has to expire in the next year, then the spouses will do their best to keep the relationship alive if there is a dependency from any side. They will long for the renewal of the marriage at any cost, and for that, they will try to keep their spouse happy and content. Then, no need to have a boyfriend or girlfriend from outside. What a great idea! No? Think about it. We are so conditioned by society that we cannot think of anything beyond the cultural norms. P.S.- this write up is not to glorify the extra marital affair but it talks about an idea of keeping the relationship/marriage lively for a lifetime. By the way, that older man was no one but Osho.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should I do if I am continuously rejected by a girls' parents and relatives for an arranged marriage?
Answer: Focus on yourself. A colleague in one of my previous jobs told me a beautiful thing. He was in love with a girl during his college days. His father had passed away long back, so his mother was somehow managing the house expenditure. So the economic condition of the family was not great. The girlfriend lived in his neighborhood, so he often visited her home. After learning about the affair, the girl's mother insulted him, stating that he has nothing to match with her daughter. That day, he cried a lot and silently moved on with life. He completed his engineering and joined an MNC. During this period, whenever he visited his hometown, he greeted his ex-girlfriend's mother, though the girlfriend got married to another guy. "Why did you greet her mom every time?" I asked in total surprise. "One day, I had to speak to her and inform her about my position. For that, I needed to be in touch with her." He was an engineer and earning well. Later, he got married and bought a house and car. On Facebook, I see him spending holidays in neighboring countries with his family. I am sure his ex-girlfriend's mother must be aware of this radical change in his life. I hope this true story helps you too. Focus on your personality and growth. Work on yourself as long as the world is at your feet. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would you do if you feel bored in the middle of a conversation?
Answer: Recently, I was sitting in a group of people in their late 20s or early 30s. They were acting like college-going students. They talked about smoking, drinking, parties, and Raindance, which didn't impress me. I am also in my 30s, but my mind is probably 40-50 years old. In addition to it, I have already experienced and explored everything that they were talking about. My mind wanted to stay neutral when they idolized smoking and drinking. I smoked once when I was 12 and drank enough in my 20s, and now, I know these habits can never be good for health and body no matter how much you modernize them. Late-night parties don't entice me anymore. So I was bored in the group but needed to stay there. No escape! I left the group mentally despite my physical presence to get rid of this monotony. Now, I was in another world where it was just me with my crazy thoughts and imagination. I thought of having a lover and smiled while feeling his soft kisses. I recalled a discussion with a wise man where we concluded that marriages should come with an expiry date and can be renewed every five years only when both partners want. In that case, the probability of taking each other for granted will lessen. I got goosebumps over this beautiful thought. I grinned and felt elated while everyone thought I was part of their conversation. But I knew where I was, and now, you too know. The picture is just for attention: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What's your perfect first date?
Answer: We met after three long months. Waiting was not easy. Every day it seemed painful and full of desperation. But we didn't give up. We dreamt together and hoped to meet soon. Finally, the meeting day arrived. We met at a coffee shop. It felt hard to have eye contact. Still, we dared to look into each other's eyes. We wanted to hold hands but couldn't. It was a public place. We were hesitant and also respectful towards each other's dignity. He ordered a sandwich and coffee. Things were moving faster. Time was running. Two souls quietly longed for love, though at a loss for words. He smiled whenever I blushed and looked out of the Glassdoor to avoid seeing him. Suddenly, I felt something wrong and needed to go to the washroom, where I realized I was on the rag. I panicked as I had not carried a sanitary napkin. My face turned pale. My eyes were slightly wet. I came out and sat quietly before him. Upon asking, I shared the problem. "Do you think I can do something for you?" He asked. "I want to go home," I said hesitantly. I knew I had spoilt our date and was waiting for his sour reaction. But to my surprise, he smiled and nodded. He then got the sandwich packed. While walking towards the car, he held my hand for support. And to cheer me up, he fed me the sandwich in the car. He dropped me home and left. Though it couldn't be a romantic date, it was perfect in its own way. P.S. — This story is not true. It does not exist in reality. The writer is trying to indulge herself in writing fiction. Sorry for the shock! 😅😅😅 The picture is just for attention: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are examples of women will be women?
Answer: Recently I visited my hometown. My sister, too, joined me. We had lots of fun together, and suddenly, I fell sick. When my body temperature increased, I felt too weak. And finally, I was on IV fluids. My sister was taking care of me when I was lying unconscious. So one morning, while my father's assistant was giving me an injection, I fondly recalled my newly bought lipstick to divert my mind from the pain. I imagined myself wearing the lipstick and walking. This imagination alleviated the ache. In the afternoon, my sister came to me and said sadly, "Be alright soon. I am feeling bored without you". "Oh yes, I need to be alright soon. I was thinking of my red lipstick today morning while being injected. It must not go to waste," I said in my meek voice and smiled. "Yeah, these lipsticks are a reason for our survival. Get well soon, darling." She commented, and we both giggled. Here is a picture of me from my hometown, of course, with my red lipstick…. hahaha! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: As a woman, what is something other women do that bothers you?
Answer: As a woman, sometimes I get to sit only with women as they feel like making a group, and men avoid joining this group. I encounter the same pattern whenever I join such a group of women. They talk about others. They appreciate and denounce others. In their talks, unfortunately, they are themselves nowhere. And this bothers me. I always ask myself why to talk about the third person who is unavailable. Why not talk about the first and second persons - I and you? I love to talk about myself if you are interested to know about me, and I look forward to hearing about you and your life. I love to learn things from you, and at the same time, I want to teach you about something that you need to be made aware of. But this seems like a dream! Some women like to make fun of others, which greatly bothers me. They are blunt and judge their friends or coworkers. They have the guts to speak to their face. This surprises me to the hilt. When they haven't lived that person's life, what gives them the right to judge it? I wonder. And I so desperately wish that they could change. They could become compassionate. Then they would have grown more composed and wiser. And the world would have been a better place. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should a 21-year-old girl do if she hates household chores?
Answer: She should focus on her career. She should be financially settled to hire a cook and domestic help. Then only she can escape household chores. Otherwise, she has no choice. Though it applies to both genders, it is more applicable to women in our patriarchal society. She is not supposed to sit idle and dictate. A husband is accepted to sit and dictate, but not a wife. Reality! If a woman neither earns money nor does household chores, she is considered useless. And there is nothing wrong with that. To survive, one has to accomplish a few skills. I always had a cook and domestic help to clean the house, but during the COVID, when I was jobless and could not hire a cook, I realized how much cooking skills matter. I learned it in a year. However, my family still considers me dumb when it comes to managing households. Still, I would say — if you are not willing to do household chores, there is nothing wrong with that. It's just a matter of interest. You can utilize your energy and time to do something else and always hire domestic help for your work. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is there something you realized you wrongly blamed your parents for?
Answer: I was immensely hurt when my mother separated me from my dad by sending me to my Aunt's house for schooling. I was six and hated studying. In my small hometown, I ran away from school. Or I troubled the teachers. The tutors at home have been frequently changed because either they could not sustain with me or I couldn't. I broke their sticks and cried non-stop. My father adored me, so he hated to see me in tears. He made up his mind to have me as illiterate and asked my mother not to pester me to study. However, my mom was another adamant woman who did not want to give up so soon on me. So she secretly planned to send me to my Aunt's house, which was in a different city. I got admission to a convent school where the rules were too strict. I had no way to run away from school. Initially, I hated it. I badly missed my father and sobbed in his arms whenever he came to meet me. It was a tough time for both of us. My mother was denounced for being a stone-hearted woman. However, this was a turning point in my life. There worked some magic, and I grew inquisitive and fascinated by books. Getting the first rank in the class became my goal ever since. So my mother's efforts proved to be a blessing in disguise. Now, I am grateful to her for taking such harsh steps during my childhood. A picture of me with my mom from those days: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Which languages would you teach to your daughter/son?
Answer: I have a six-year-old son, and he is fluent in English. Though my mother tongue is Hindi, I would say his mother tongue is English. My ex-husband and I always spoke in English. We both loved this language. So my child learned it by default. And I am proud of it. I am teaching him Hindi too. He can quickly write and read difficult words in this language. Since I write poems in Hindi, I expect my son to understand their depth once he grows. I will motivate him to opt for Sanskrit as a third language in the school. Sanskrit is the mother of all languages. It fascinates me to the core, and I can easily teach him after a simple brush-up. As of now, he is learning Kannada as a third language. Since I don't know this language, I have kept a tutor to teach him Kannada after school. I have studied German. If he is interested, I would also love to teach him this language. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Normally, what form of stories do you pick up to write your book? What are some of your creative poems?
Answer: Thank you Salendra Maharaj for A2A. My book "Towards A Better Life" is based on my life experiences. The stories are true and inspiring. You will find them unpolished and raw. You will get to know my flaws, insecurities, and fear, and also, you will learn how I overcame if I did. While writing them, at times, I felt scared of being judged. What will people think about me after knowing me and my past so closely — this was a concern. However, it didn't bother me for a long. I love my being and my originality. I am what I am, and there is no need to change myself. After writing this book, I gained some extra confidence to face this society. This book is for all age groups. Anyone can read it and understand it. I can assure you that you will get energized while reading it. It's a mixture of humor, inspiration, and guidance on how to live life. Before publishing it, I got it checked by scholars who were my friends too. They loved the content and gave me the green signal to publish it. You will find some poems in the book I wrote while I was going through that particular phase. The noise in my mind birthed them at the time of turmoil. They will definitely motivate you. So, I recommend you read it to look at things from a different perspective and gain confidence in what you do. My book is available on Amazon and Flipkart: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I let go of the past?
Answer: Why should you let go of the past??? I will never advise you to let go of the past. I will ask you to accept it with grace. I don't have a magnificent past though I have made some beautiful memories out of it. I cherish all good and bad moments in my heart — good moments bring me a smile, whereas bad moments remind me not to indulge in the same kind of affairs again. Your past is always beautiful. It teaches you how to act, behave and live in the future. It shows you a path to reach the right place. I have learned to accept my past wholeheartedly and gained the confidence to display it in public. This way, I get to meet the right people — the ones who can accept me with my flaws and cherish me forever. No diplomacy! I don't need to convince them how I am. They know me beforehand. This saves a lot of my energy and time. So I suggest you move forward, keeping the memory of your past in your heart. You don't need to get rid of it. Your past is the base of your future, and you can not build a roof without the pillars. I hope this helps. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you deal with Quora addiction?
Answer: Recently, in a conversation with a friend, he told me that people are no more interested in reading and writing. Social media has consumed most of their time and energy. Every time I hear such things, I feel disappointed. Because reading is the most beautiful habit one can imbibe. I often encourage my loved ones to read. Read anything. Since many people consider book reading as time-consuming, Quora is a boon to them. Quora is so handy that they at least get to read something — fiction, a true story, life experiences, some news, and whatnot! In recent years, Quora has always kept me updated on current affairs. Also, Quora has created an opportunity for aspiring writers to express themselves. It has become a diary for many of us. Through this platform, I got to know many amazing people who have become my extended family. So I say — there is nothing wrong with being a Quora addict. This is much better than other social media platforms. If you intend to explore new dimensions of life, you must be on Quora. I am grateful for this platform. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can reading change one's thought?
Answer: I am an uncultured girl from a very cultured family. I have lived my life exactly how I wanted. I focused on my studies and career because my freedom was something that I didn't want to compromise on. I have always been fearless in making mistakes. I take ownership of my mistake and look forward to making new mistakes. They are very precious to me because they teach me how to live. In my family, drinking and smoking is a crime. But I tried it because I didn't want to believe in others' words about how injurious they were. I wanted to feel it. I chose my groom in an arranged marriage where my father was disappointed with the alliance. But I still went ahead and married him. And soon, I realized that I had made a mistake. Still, I stayed in that marriage, being highly submissive. My emotional connection with my husband did not let me leave, though I suffered. However, after seven years, when I decided to correct my mistake, I walked out of my failed marriage. Now, again, I am living my life how I want. I have become a flowing river that can't be stopped. A free bird that cannot be caged. I like to explore things and people, which I am currently doing. I am working on my aspirations too. People are amazed by my out of box thought process. They wonder how and why I have become so. And I say — Meet those writers, dead or alive, who are responsible for making me different and giving me the courage to be on my own. They gave me the guts to face society and break its rotten rules. Can reading change one's thoughts? Of course, it does. Sharatchandra taught me to follow my heart, whereas Tagore gave me a new concept of marriage. If Kamladas showed me the path of discovering my being, Osho liberated me from dilemmas, confusion, and social norms. I request you all to read — Read to bring changes in yourself and others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Daily Life: What is the most valuable skill a person can have for their entire life?
Answer: My parents had a fight today. They are old and had 50 years of married life together. The pattern of their flights that I observe is always the same.
