They always try to change each other, which seems impossible. Both are adamant. I have seen more and more people like them who tend to change their loved ones. Maybe, out of love and concern. They worry about their people's health, safety, or future and try to do every possible thing to protect them. However, in this process, they forget their originality. They try to impose their wishes and habits on their loved ones, which is so suffocating. We should learn that we can make changes only in unbaked pitchers. The pitcher that is already baked will break if we try to change its shape. We can inculcate good habits in our children by practicing good habits ourselves. We can teach them the right things until they are children. But we can not change parents, spouses, neighbors, colleagues, etc. though we find a lot of things that could be improved because they are baked, solid, and hard. We can only bring changes in ourselves. We can learn to ignore things and let others live how they want, and if they are not close to our hearts, we can maintain a distance from them to suppress unnecessary conflicts. I hope this helps. P.S. — My parents are very close to my heart. They are kind people, but their circumstances have made them cranky. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do feminists seem to get a lot of hate even though they fight for women's rights?
Answer: Because some women have spoilt men's lives in the name of feminism. They couldn't understand the exact meaning of feminism and tortured the men, both mentally and physically. They have been depressed, suppressed, and dominated for ages. They saw their mothers and grandmothers suffering with their men, which agitated them. When they got a chance to revenge, they couldn't think of anything, but they wanted to ruin the lives of men. They filed false rape cases, dowry cases, etc., against them. They couldn't understand that such a step would take them nowhere. They just wanted to take revenge. The idea of feminism came into existence when women needed to be given equal rights as men. However, it is baseless to claim that men and women are equal. These two genders can never be equal. Both are unique; however, none of them deserves discrimination. The feminists needed to fight for the same, but they lost their ground and put their energy into taking out their frustration. Because of these so-called feminists, the concept of feminism lost its Genuity and is subjected to hatred. Also, there is a fault with men too. Men have been seeing their mothers and grandmothers as submissive for ages. Now, when a woman as their wife or colleague at the office demands equal rights, they get triggered and hate feminism. It's going to take a long to change the mindset. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is love in its purest form?
Answer: Recently, a reader from Quora shared his heartfelt story with me. He is in love with a girl who is getting an opportunity to study abroad. He is getting emotional and insecure. He knows about life in foreign countries and how difficult it is to settle down in India once lived abroad for many years. At the same time, he doesn't want to become an obstacle in his girlfriend's life. He messaged me as he had been feeling low all the time. I appreciate his maturity. Love does not mean holding people. If there is true love, one always lets another go. They allow their loved ones to fly and soar high; they never tend to cut their wings. They support them by all means. In the purest form of love, you don't force anyone to stay in your life, but you let them live however they wish. Their happiness becomes your preference over your own happiness. In Buddhism, there is a saying — if you truly love a flower, you won't dare to pluck it. This is how love is in its purest form. Thank you Gaayathri Reddy for A2A. P.S. —I have written a book based on my life - experiences which is available on Amazon and Flipkart. You can read it to look at things from a different perspective and gain confidence in things that you do. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best thing someone did recently to make you happy?
Answer: Last year, after reading my articles on Quora, a business journalist contacted me and asked me to write a book. He was impressed with my writing style and found my Quora answers quite appealing. I informed him that I was already working on my book. He showered me with his blessings upon hearing this. After that, I forgot him. In October 2022, when I was negotiating with a publisher, he pinged me again to know the status of my book. From then on, a journey of teacher and pupil commenced. He took a lot of interest in my book, which I had not expected from a stranger. Though I was discussing things with the publisher, I needed some clarifications as this was my first book. After he got involved in the publishing process, things started falling into place, and everything began to go smoothly. I will forever remain grateful to him for that, as his guidance was incredible. For instance, when I was struggling to finalise my book's front and back cover pages, he advised me to put my photographs on them. "I am not a famous writer. How can I put my photo," I screamed out of nervousness. "God has gifted you beauty and brain. Why can't you use both at once?" he responded. I blushed purple but still had zero confidence. He persuaded me to put my photos on the cover pages. And after a long-drawn discussion and arguments, I finally agreed. Surprisingly, it has turned out to be a good decision as my first book with my pictures on it is being loved by many readers. I get many messages stating that they get to see me daily due to this book. Hahaha! I, therefore, want to thank this business journalist Mr. Suresh Menon (who is also my friend now), for being with me when I needed him the most. I want him to know that I have immense respect for him. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is that one food item most people eat but you don’t?
Answer: The year 2009. It was my first day in the office in Bangalore. "Is it kheer?" I asked a colleague while taking lunch from the buffet. "It's curd-rice, dear.", She smiled. “Mmm…Mm…Curd-rice!”, I murmured. Though look-wise, it seemed normal to me; I never felt comfortable with curd-rice. To me, it felt like an accident - The rice accidentally fell into curd. When the summer entered the city, and due to the heat, I fell sick, my Manglorean manager advised me to have curd-rice. I quietly nodded but could never try this food. When I developed acid reflux, the doctors, including my South Indian friends, suggested me to eat the same. I had tears in my eyes but couldn't agree to eat it. However, I never disregarded it as I understood the health benefits of this scary food. So I taught my child to eat curd-rice, and he loves it with some spices. Living in the South, I realized that many habits like food, the way of living, and even the thought process depend on our upbringing. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the one thing you will never do again?
Answer: I tried changing people's minds regarding sex — both online and offline. According to ordinary people, there is no life without sex. A man or woman will get into depression without it. I have been without sex for many years now. I never felt depressed. I never felt a requirement for it. I have been asked how I control my sexual desires. This question amazes me to the hilt. For common people, having a male friend means having sex with him. I have been asked if I lost my virginity to my boyfriend during my college days. People really don't know the woman who resides in my body. For this woman, physical and mental intimacy are two different things. Physical intimacy is often lustful in today's world. Everyone is running for it. They are in a hurry to get it. However, my perspective on physical intimacy is different. Physical intimacy comes into existence when love reaches its peak — selfless love! And to know how selfless and unconditional love is, you must spend years together. But nobody is ready to wait. I have written about it in my book and many times on Quora, but I couldn't find any change in people's mindsets. I will never tell people again how sacred and divine sex can be. And every relationship with the opposite gender doesn't lead to sex, at least in my life. If I ever look for a partner, I will ensure that he first touches my soul and then, my body. And I know this is really hard to find someone like this in today's world. That's why I decided to remain single all my life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the best strong short stories?
Answer: "Dad, I want to become a pilot," she said to her father at the age of 6. "Okay, okay!" the father smiled. "Dad, I want to become a doctor just like uncle Rohil." She announced when she was 9. "Dad, I want to become a police officer." She changed her mind at the age of 13. "Dad, I want to become as strong as you are. I want to nurture my child how you brought me up. You never felt tired of taking care of me single-handedly. Though mom left you just after I was born, you never thought of running away from your responsibilities. I want to become as loving and selfless as you are." She said when she was 19. This was the best reward Mr. Sen had received from his daughter. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What relationship habits can lead to a happy marriage?
Answer: Walking. My sister and brother-in-law have been married for more than 17 years. All these years, there has not been any single night when they didn't go for a stroll after dinner. This is their habit — A rule that can not be violated. In this 30 minutes of walk, mobile phones, children, and guests are not allowed. This is just for both of them. They walk, they talk, and they discuss various topics, such as their expectations from each other, happiness and dissatisfaction, finances, children, parents, and things that are bothering any of them. During this time, they will hold each other's hands even if anyone joins them. I have seen this for the last 17 years and have always found them the most attractive and cheerful couple. They have their share of disagreements, conflicts, and disputes, but these factors never impact the relationship. Looking at them, I feel that making a relationship meaningful is absolutely in our hands. The only thing that is required is a mutual effort. One-sided efforts won't work. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your weirdest wish?
Answer: Recently a stakeholder at the office recognized me as a Quora writer. He has been reading me on Quora for a long, so he knew a lot about me. As a single mother, it amazes him that I manage so many things: job, child, household, reading, writing, and now my studies too. I couldn't say anything but just smiled. Deep down, I knew how I had been managing all alone for the last four years. I am always tired, sleep-deprived, and exhausted. At times, irritated too. Lately, I have developed a wish that you may consider weird. But I have been thinking about it a lot. I want to book a room in a hotel for four days and spend time all alone. No disturbance at all! No phone calls! I should be free of worries, office stress, households, and even my child. No one should bother me there. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner should be available in the room through a phone call. I shouldn't be worried about my look. So, of course, no clicking pictures. All alone, I wish to sleep as long as I want. I can read books, write journals or come out of the room in the evening, go for a stroll, and talk to hotel staff. Or, I would just sit idle. At present, this wish is a luxury to me. However, I am so desperate for it. The reason for this is that I am exhausted. I am tired, both mentally and physically. It's not like I am trying to run away from my responsibilities, but it's about restoring my energy, enthusiasm, and spirit for life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do actions truly speak louder than words or thoughts?
Answer: A few weeks ago, I was clearing the storage box of my bed when I discovered a small bundle of hundred rupees notes in a handkerchief. I smiled as I was not surprised to see it. Felt emotional and immediately remembered my hostel days. After spending a vacation at home, when I reached the hostel, I found money in my cashew container or cornflake packets my mother had secretly kept for me. She is 67 now, and I am a working mother, but she still remembers her old habits. Looking at the bundle of notes, I could not resist smiling and rushed to call her over the phone. My mother has not been good at expressing love. Both of my parents hardly said I love you to us children. They don't hug me or show a lot of concern, and I, too, have no habit of discussing my difficulties with them, but they have always been there whenever I needed them. During COVID, I was jobless throughout the year and was nearly running on empty. As a divorced daughter, I didn't want to become a burden on them, so I tried keeping all my worries to myself, but they understood my struggles and supported me by all means they could. So answering this question, I would say that actions speak louder than words or thoughts. My parents are an example of it. They don't talk much, and they don't show concern, but they can feel what I feel. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the most valuable life lesson you've learned from using social media?
Answer: I received immense love and respect when I expressed myself on Quora. I am known as a motivational writer. People from all age groups reach out to me through messages. Currently, I have 1,195 messages in my inbox to read. Everything sounds heavenly. But hold on! Some people on Quora have idolized me. They only want to see what they wish to see — goodness, virtues, and morals. They don't want to see my drawbacks. I am harshly denounced if I ever write about my bare feelings, including things I did, do, or will be doing. People don't understand that I am just a human being—an honest one who doesn't hesitate to express herself. When I say that I befriended a man during the upheaval of my married life or if I had a boyfriend during my college days — they get triggered. In all the cases, I must have lost my virginity; this is how they think. I wonder how obsessed they are with sex. They can not think beyond it. When I say I stole a unique-looking tiny glass from a bar just for fun — my morals and virtues come on the radar. When I say I love my aloneness and am no more interested in relationships, I am considered a narcissist. If I say that I expect my child to understand and give me space while I am writing — I get a lecture on the roles and responsibilities of a mother. If I write something against men or women, I receive hateful comments. They don't understand that this is how the writer has experienced, and her writing is based on her personal experience. People get personalized here with everything that I write. They take things to their heart and start abusing. All of a sudden, their maturity level goes down. I wonder, looking at People. How judgemental they are! They don't understand a simple thing — We are humans, and humans are emotional, vulnerable, and faulty. While expressing myself on social media, I learned I should only write what people want to read. I should portray myself how they want to see me, no matter if they are themselves full of faults. However, this lesson couldn't bring any change in me. Sorry! — I can not mould my personality as per people's wishes. I will continue to remain the same as I am. And I will be writing what I wish to write. P.S.- Your kind words make me emotional, whereas your hateful comments strengthen me. Keep commenting your heart out. The comment section is all yours! But in this process, remember that your maturity level, too, is measured. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would be the most important thing you would tell your younger self?
Answer: I fell in love at the age of 19. My boyfriend was a writer who found passion in describing me in his beautiful poems. Our love story began when he gifted me a small diary full of poems about me that he had written secretly. I adored that diary even after the breakup. After a few years, my marriage got fixed with a man with whom I thought of restarting my life, though I was not into him. I wondered how he would react upon learning about my ex-boyfriend. I grew up hearing that you should not disclose your past affairs to your spouse. So one evening, after coming from the office, I threw the small diary into the bin. I didn't have the confidence to showcase myself with my past — be it bright or rotten. Later, I even called off that wedding as his family started bothering my father with dowry stuff. And he supported it. I don't miss my boyfriend, as we were not compatible, but I miss his writing. Being a writer myself now, I regret discarding his writing in such a brutal way. So answering your question, I would say — I would be telling my younger self to accept herself with confidence. She must stand her ground. There is nothing wrong with having a past. She doesn't have to wipe it out to build a future emperor - The one who is willing to love her will love her irrespective of her past. A Picture of those days for attention: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: When should you stop pursuing a relationship with someone?
Answer: P.S.- As Indians, we grew up in a culture where separation/divorce is considered ugly. In our society, being single is not acceptable. So you stop pursuing the relationship with your partner only when you have the guts to face society and people who tend to take advantage of you while being single. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you think is the easy way that leads us to heaven?
Answer: My grandfather (paternal) was a religious man. He went on several pilgrimages. He never touched non-vegetarian food in his life. He never missed any fast for Ekadashi, which is considered the most auspicious fast in the Hindu religion. He spent his morning and evening offering prayers at the temple that he had only constructed. He donated money and lands to the welfare of society. He built a hospital. He was known for his kindness. He died in his late 80s. I am not sure if he went to heaven, as the concept of hell and heaven doesn't sound promising. However, looking at the crowd that came for his last darshan, I believed that he was God's child. No one in the crowd spoke ill about him. Everyone was just eager to touch his feet and see his face for the last time. Even if the concept of hell and heaven exists, I will not value it much as it comes into existence after death. Instead, I would insist on living like my grandfather, whose demise saddened everyone. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you think money can buy anything?
Answer: My father's best friend was in politics. He had a strong personality and owned a lot of property. It wouldn't be wrong if I said he had got swag with everything. The whole family had a luxurious life, and happiness was everywhere until my aunt was diagnosed with blood cancer. The waves of sadness and depression covered the whole family. My uncle spent a lot of money on her treatment which was taking place in one of the best hospitals in Mumbai. He did every possible thing to save her life but couldn't succeed. After six months, my aunt passed away. The children became orphans. Somehow they managed to escape that trauma but lacked guidance, empathy, and love. One of them committed suicide after a few years. Uncle didn't get married again. He became frail and emaciated with time and passed away later. Can money buy anything you want? Money can buy you entertainment but not happiness and peace. It can buy you fun-loving, gregarious friends but no true friendship. It can help you lead a luxurious life, but it wouldn't guarantee you have love and moral support. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do men fall in true love or is everything just casual for them?
Answer: I am going to write a controversial answer to this question. Feel free to disagree with me. Men do fall in true love, but the majority of them start treating it as ordinary in later years. They lose their feelings very soon and may get attracted to other women. This possibility is always there in their life. They love their women, no doubt about that. However, they don't carry the same feelings for long. For them, replacement is easy. They don't struggle to restart a new life with another woman. They are so casual. They don't hold the emotions they had with their previous partner once they move on from the relationship. They can easily erase all their memories and go on a new adventure. I am not writing this to offend men. I am just writing their characteristics. At times, they can be emotional, but their emotions are fickle. Or temporary. Or you can consider them 'Not Promising.' P.S.- Of course, exceptions are there. However, based on exceptions, we can not generalize the characteristics. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How has Quora polished your personality?
Answer: Quora has given me confidence. Not only confidence but recognition too. Before Quora, I was nobody. Though I was a nobody, I had a sheer desire to establish myself as a known figure. To be honest, I didn't know how. I used to write here and there — in my diary or company website. My friends and colleagues read me and appreciated. But I wanted a larger audience. At the same time, I was struggling with my personal life. Things were going downhill, and I was losing hope for everything. But when I discovered Quora, I felt the almighty didn't want me to vanish in the dark. It wanted me to survive and restore the zeal I had lost during the upheaval of my life. The opinion, beliefs, and my confidence in them that I had developed during my student life started reshaping. Reading people's opinions here, I learned to drop off my biases and think more logically and impartially. This helped me improve my personality. And I feel proud that I could establish myself as a published author. Quora has played a vital role in my life. People on different platforms, like LinkedIn, Facebook, etc., recognize me. It is an achievement for a small-town girl like me. I could also connect with amazing people through Quora, who helped me evolve stronger. Quora is a boon! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Does makeup increase your confidence?
Answer: Yes. I don't do heavy makeup. I don't know how to do it, but I wish I knew. I love my simple makeup, which contains cream, kajal, and lipstick or pink lip balm. I don't like stepping out without it because it gives me confidence. Makeup enhances beauty no matter how simple it is. One looks better. And there is nothing wrong with magnifying or enhancing the look. However, to me, the outfit and footwear too matter a lot. This is what I believe; you may differ. Me in my simple makeup: (An opportunity to post a picture, lol) Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What did your child ask you that threw you completely off guard?
Answer: I am pursuing my M.A. in psychology. And these days, I have nothing to think or talk about except psychology, as the final exam will take place in June. Last night, I was holding a psychology book and pondering where to start when my six-year-old interrupted. Him- what do you study in Psychology? Me- I study human nature in it. That means how a human behaves. Him- that means how a human thinks. Me- of course. And also, I study why a human behaves in a certain way. The reason for that particular behavior! Do you get it? Him- yes, I did. Me - Now, please go from here, and let me study. Him - But I have one more question. Me - what is it? Him - Do you also study why you get angry and scold me? Me - 😐😐😐😐 **A silence fell across the room while his face broke into a smile** Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What life lessons has your work taught you?
Answer: As an incident manager, my job is to get the customer's issues fixed by the support team. This is a respectful job where I get to interact with engineers globally. So once, I received an escalation from a customer where they expressed their frustration with our support. I immediately rushed to the engineer who had been working on the issue. However, I didn't get a proper response from her. I even explained the case's urgency, but she sounded cold. After a few follow-ups, she suddenly became rude with her response. I felt offended. Also, I was answerable to the customer and needed to share an update with them, for which I required her help. So, I immediately reached out to her manager and explained the situation. The manager assured me to look into it. After a few minutes, I got a call from the engineer. This time, she sounded weary and tired but also polite. She apologized and told me that she was not well. I asked her if she had lunch. She told me she did not get time for lunch. I politely advised her to have lunch on time. She thanked me, and then we discussed the work. My job taught me to have patience. I learned that sometimes people become rude due to circumstances. I learned to be kind to people as we don't know who is going through what. P.S.- I request you all to be a little kind to people around you. Here, everyone is going through something that we don't know. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is emotional abuse in a relationship? My ex threatened me. I'm trying to make her happy by doing small things for her.
Answer: Since the last year, I have received several messages from readers where they talked about emotional abuse, but they didn't know how to term it. Their partners made them feel inferior, lonely and guilty. Their confidence level has drastically decreased as they have constantly been criticized or mocked. They are brutally compared with others. Some told me their partners isolate them in the family as if they don't exist. They feel neglected, depressed, and unwanted. Though they never encounter physical violence, they are always hurt. This is more about emotional hurt. In our society, emotional abuse is often taken lightly. The victim is advised to adjust and do things to please their partners and improve the relationship. Sometimes it works. But most of the time, it doesn't. We need to understand that in a genuine relationship, we are never threatened by our loved ones. They don't warn us to behave in a certain way. We are not obliged to please them. However, I suggest people walk out of such relationships if it is still so. It makes no sense to stay with someone with whom there is no mental peace. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the things your parents did that you will never do to your kids or future kids?
Answer: My parents taught me about adjustment. Adjust with your loved ones even though they are always cutting your throat. All my life, I have seen them doing so with their relatives. They persuaded me too to stay in my toxic, loveless marriage for a long on the cost of losing my soul. I am not going to teach this to my child. He must know how long to stay with people and when to leave the relationship. In this cruel world full of insensitive people, Self-care and Self-esteem are more important than anything. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Have you ever had a weird dream that you could never forget and after so many years it still haunts you when you remember it?
Answer: During my teenage, I often used to see snakes in my dreams. They were in bulk. All in black color, moving simply near my feet. They didn't hurt me, but I used to be very afraid, shivering and sweating. I woke up from sleep with fear. And this dream came often. I told my mother about it. She discussed this with our temple priest, who gave me a stone and instructed me to wash it with milk and put it in a black string. And then, I had to tie it to my bed. I followed the instructions. And the frequency of dreams surprisingly reduced. And slowly, it disappeared from my life. However, I am still terrified of snakes. I can't see them in the zoo, in movies, in photos, or even cartoons. And the thought of those dreams still haunts me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something that you will never do?
Answer: I would never be quiet when witnessing wrongs. My child studies in one of the reputed schools in Bangalore. Recently, on a cold winter morning, I was attending a function at his school. The arrangement was made in the playground. They had arranged chairs for the parents, whereas the children were seated on the cemented floor. They had not put any mat or carpet for them. After sitting on a chair for 10 minutes, I realized the children were sitting on the cold floor. I immediately removed my shoe to check the surface. It was pretty chilled. I was shocked to encounter this carelessness of the management. I spoke to a few parents who were sitting near me. They agreed, felt sad, and criticized the school management, but none of them wanted to raise their voice. It was only I who immediately reached out to the management and complained. Finally, they handed over my child to me and allowed him to sit on a chair next to me. The rest of the children were still sitting on the cold floor. I wonder why people don't speak up when needed. I paid a hefty amount to the school, and I was not demanding anything extraordinary but a basic thing - a carpet on the floor! A few days later, I got an invitation from the management for the Makar Sankranti celebration. I wrote my concerns to them. But I didn't get any response. Due to my health issues, my child and I couldn't attend the function. But a few days ago, I saw they had arranged chairs for children and their parents in the same playground on Republic day. I was happy that I was heard and didn't let my child suffer just because of my silence. I have always wondered why people don't voice out, why they suffer, or why they don't support fellow humans in need because this is the only thing that makes us a human different than animals. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you still open doors for women?
Answer: My colleague Rohan was a friend to me. We often took a break together. He was funny and, at the same time, logical. He tried to find logic in everything we humans do. Once, he raised the same topic in our conversation mentioned in this question. "Anshu, how does it make me a more decent man if I open doors for you?" he asked. Before I could think and say something, he added one more question, "why is the same not implemented for women? Aren't the women supposed to be polite with men in the same manner as the men are expected to be?" And I agreed with him. When we demand equality — equal treatment, equal pay, and equal opportunities, then why this excess of expectations from men? Opening doors for women can not be a means of measurement through which we can rate the decency of men. It should be up to their preference or their choice of how they want to act in such areas. Later, Rohan concluded that he would open the door for any person in need, irrespective of gender. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If your parents hate the person you're going out with, does it affect your opinion of the person you're dating?
Answer: When I fell in love for the first time and told my mother about it, she heard me patiently. She neither overreacted nor overprotected. She just heard me because she trusted me. Later, when I chose my ex-husband in an arranged marriage, they supported me even though they were not very happy with that alliance. And I got married with their blessings. The way they have always trusted me, welcomed all my friends and treated them with grace, I feel fortunate. And at the same time, I feel guilty for not listening to them while I chose my ex-husband as the marriage ultimately failed. I profoundly respect my parents, and I believe that they will never wish ill on me. If they ever dislike someone in the future, I will definitely give it a thought. I will discuss things with them and take their opinion without being adamant about my choice. They are more experienced and have seen more of the world and people than me. I may fail to recognize the true face of a person. Their opinion and judgment can help me to understand better. If they can love me unconditionally, I can also give them the right to affect my opinion with theirs. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do people suffer in silence?
Answer: Some people in this world are not destined to have a better life. You accept it or not — but it's true. No self-help books help them to change their circumstances. Yoga, meditation, and therapy don't work for them. They are not heard. They are not wanted. They know no one will support them if they seek justice. They are aware that no one will pay heed to them if they voice out their sufferings. They are so unfortunate. They even have cruel, insensitive people in their surroundings who tend to increase their pain. Raising their voice against those people can be a worse experience. People prefer to suffer in silence if the circumstances are as mentioned above. Nobody can understand their fear, agony, anxiety, and pain. It's so individual. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Indian Men: What scares Indian men?
Answer: During my college days, a relative stated a strange thing about the importance of education on a gender basis. According to him, it is acceptable if a girl doesn't study and have a career. Parents can find a well-established groom for her. But a boy must focus on education and establish a job to run a family. Practically, it's true. In our society, we expect our men to take financial responsibility. We consider him useless and a wreck if he cannot make it. He is good for nothing. This pressure is so enormous that many young men get into depression. I receive messages from my young readers where they tell me how diligently they are preparing for competitive exams and feel dismayed when there is no result. They are directionless as they don't have any financial security in case of failure in their career. If there is no career, no marriage, and no family. Relatives and friends avoid talking to them. They feel like a burden on their parents. I believe this is the scariest thing for Indian men. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: At what point should someone get therapy?
Answer: Last year, a close friend called me over the phone. She sounded depressed and anxious. She told me that she was frequently falling sick. She was once admitted to the hospital as well. She had become frail and was losing interest in life. When I asked the reason for that, she felt clueless. She had no idea why she was going through this morose phase. Her anxiety was increasing as she had never been like that. Also, she had nothing to feel depressed about. She is blessed with a good husband and two intelligent children. She has financial stability too. While telling me about her mental state, she burst into tears. “What is wrong with me, Anshu? Am I mentally disturbed?” She sobbed. Before I could think of suggesting anything, she said she wanted to go for therapy. I appreciated her for this initiative. She consulted a counselor, vented out her frustration, and listened to their advice. She got his phone number and spoke to him whenever she felt disturbed. She followed his instructions and suggestions and got better in a few months. Now, she is leading a peaceful life. At what point should you get therapy? When you think that there is nothing that helps you come out of your despair. When you feel helpless to approach anyone and open up about your mental issues. Go for therapy. Nothing wrong with that. Your health — be it physical or mental — should be your priority. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something you have tried, but will never do again?
Answer: Smoking. I would be 10–11 years old. I desperately wanted to smoke. I wanted to experience the puff coming out of the mouth. I was born in a family where tea, coffee, drinks, and smoking were prohibited. My father, being a doctor, has never touched any of these. Talking about them was a crime in my family. However, I had made up my mind to try it. Unfortunately, I could not get cigarettes from any shop as everyone knew my father. The domestic help, who smoked 3–4 bidis in a day, refused to give me one. The poor creature was afraid of my parents. So I invented a Bidi on my own. I managed to get some dry leaves. I crushed them and rolled them on paper. Then I tied it with a thread just like a Bidi is tied up. It was a summer afternoon. When everyone went for a nap, I went backside verandah and smoked my self-made Bidi. As soon as I inhaled it, I got a severe cough that seemed to suffocate me to death. My eyes filled with tears. My face reddened. And out of nowhere, my uncle turned up to give me a slap across my cheek. Tears rolled down. His contribution to reddening my already reddened face was remarkable. He threw the Bidi and warned me not to repeat this. That was the first and last time when I tried smoking. Now, I can't even stand near a smoker. The smell of cigarettes gives me nausea, and I start coughing. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is a fake sign of intelligence?
Answer: I was in 5th grade. An acquaintance often visited my family whenever he was in town. He was preparing for civil services in New Delhi. My sister and I were startled to see him talk. He spoke in Hindi but used heavy English words in the conversation. My sister and I often looked at each other as we didn't understand what he was speaking. At times, we felt the need for a dictionary. Once, he asked us to stand in front of him and introduce ourselves in English. We were already demoralized by his way of speaking, and now this performance test. We both miserably failed. And he laughed at us. He compared us with the Delhi kids and mocked us. He had forgotten that he studied in the same school where we had been. He had forgotten that he was known as a below-average student in the school. You will come across many such people who claim to be very intelligent and know everything, but in reality, they are like empty vessel which makes more sound. Intelligent people are humble. They are often knowledge-seeker. They never show off and will even come to you asking about anything if they have the slightest doubt. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm. Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you ever tell family members when they are being ridiculous or doing things that are unneccessary?
Answer: My mother often feels lonely. She has her own share of dissatisfaction and sadness. I make sure that I call her every day. The day I find her low and hopeless, the frequency of my calls increases. I may call her 3–4 times. In every call, she speaks almost the same thing. The most ridiculous, unnecessary, or unwanted stuff I hear is about a TV serial that started recently. She tells me the whole story — a repeated story. I made myself understand that she needed to be heard, and I needed to have patience. I am not interested in TV serials, but I listen to her murmuring hmm, haan, ok, hu, yeah, is it, my god etc. And I will continue it for a lifetime without letting her know how monotonous or redundant I find those narrations. Because I love her and I want to fill her loneliness. I want to make her feel she has someone with whom she can talk or discuss things. I want to convince her that she is not alone. P.S. We don't know how much we bothered our parents with our unnecessary talks when we were children. Now, we definitely owe them. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do Indian parents give smartphones to their children at a young age? If so, why?
Answer: I gave a smartphone to my child when he was eight months old. It sounds weird, but I had no choice. He was not good at eating, and I struggled to feed him every day. I have been a working mother and have always been in a rush. All the passersby knew this adamant child as I fed him, making him sit on the wall near the main gate and showing him dogs and cows. I had hired an adult girl as a caretaker who used to feed him in my absence. It was chaos for that girl as well to feed him every time. However, I noticed he could easily take the first few spoons while watching YouTube videos. That eased our task to some extent. So I permanently gave my smartphone to him and bought a new one for myself. He watched videos while having food until the last year. Now, he watches TV or laptop. I have banned the mobile for him. You can blame me for being an irresponsible mother, but I was helpless. He needed some diversion to swallow the morsel; otherwise, he threw it out. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do I react when people talk behind my back?
Answer: My father was very fond of me when I was a child. He pampered me a lot though he could hardly manage time for family. Some of our close relatives knew it. So when I divorced my husband, they reached a strange conclusion. They said I couldn't adjust to my married life because my father highly pampered me during childhood. Hearing this, I was shell-shocked. My father's love didn't make me adamant, stupid, or narcissistic. It didn't give me arrogance. But yes, it gave me confidence. It availed me opportunities for higher education and independent life. That's it! Still, those relatives talked nonsense. Initially, I felt aggressive, but soon I could overcome my negative emotions. They have not lived my life, so they have no idea about it. They don't know how much ache and bitterness this heart carries. "Their rash judgment is something I must learn to shun. Their job is to gossip, and I must not be affected by it". I resolved. Then I restored my faith and channelized my time and energy towards inner and outer growth. I read books, wrote on Quora, talked to like-minded people, and, stitch by stitch, created a new life. P.S. — I have recently written a book based on my life -experiences which is available on Amazon and Flipkart. You can read it to learn how I restated my life after the havoc. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is my boyfriend trying to change me too much?
Answer: I had a friend in my hostel who was too good at fashion. I wondered how she matched an ordinary dress with a denim jacket and a leather belt and made it unique. She had a knack for fashion. We all admired her for that. Her boyfriend was orthodox and considered fashion ugly. Probably he thought of it as a spoiler that could mislead his girlfriend. Once they were on a date, and my friend had worn a beautiful long denim skirt with a split. The boyfriend asked her not to wear that skirt outside the hostel. She agreed. Later, he started instructing her on what to wear and what not to wear at parties. She even had to choose the colors of her dresses with his permission. He was fond of light colors. He even didn't like her to apply lipstick. She accepted everything. Probably happily, as she loved him. What I couldn't understand was the sort of love that they had. Loving someone means accepting them as a whole — their likes, dislikes, tastes, background, and whole personality. Irrespective of gender, if you feel suffocated in the relationship or you feel that a part of you is being lost just because you want to keep your mate happy, consider that your partner is trying to change you too much. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Can you write some random moments here?
Answer: It was 12:45 am. I was not getting sleep. The characters of the book, 'The stationary shop of Tehran,' were secretly calling me. My six years old had drifted into a deep sleep. However, he was still holding me tightly. I meticulously removed his hand from my bosom and shifted to another bedroom. Looking at the book lying on the bed, I felt relieved. The serenity of nights always pushes me to read and write more. So I picked up the book without wasting a minute and started reading it. While engrossed in reading, I felt a creature standing beside the bed. My heart pounded. I was afraid to take my eyes off the book. "Mumma, why did you come here?" I heard. I was surprised to see my moppet at this time. "Didn't you sleep, Jani? How come you here?" I asked. "I had slept but woke up because you were not there. I don't feel good without you. What are you doing here?" "I am reading, Shona baby." "Okay, then you read. I will sleep here only." He lay down in my lap, covering himself with his baby blanket. Before closing his eyes, he kissed me and smiled once. I was smitten with this gesture. And while I stroked his hair, he fell asleep again. This little munchkin is so close to my heart. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If I had 3 days to make you fall in love with me, what should I do?
Answer: P.S.- I have written this answer just for fun. Now please don't spam my inbox.😅😅😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What surprises you about people?
Answer: During college, I was a little popular among my classmates. I wanted to increase this popularity, so I asked my friend to spread a rumor about me being an astrologer. At first, she hesitated, but I convinced her that we needed to establish our reputation in the college. If I get fame, she will also get it as my friend. She agreed. She talked to other girls about my astrological knowledge. She told them some concocted stories about how I predicted the fortune. A girl showed interest. I first denied seeing her hand, saying my Guru would be upset if he learned I was misusing my knowledge. This ruse of mine worked. She trusted the authenticity of my knowledge. She insisted on saying something about her, and I dramatically told her about her personality and future. With pauses and timely silence! "You are very emotional. You are very close to your father. Mmm…. You are studious and hate to gossip. You get angry with liars. You will become a bank officer, but this line says you have to work hard for that." My acting worked. The girls believed in me. They often showed me their hands and requested me to tell them their fortunes. Initially, I enjoyed it, but soon I felt fed up telling concocted stories. Once even, I told the truth that I didn't know anything, but they didn't believe me. Still, they requested me to see their hands. In the meantime, my friend relished free samosas as a fee for persuading me to tell their fortunes. They wanted to know everything about their life, career, and marriage. One girl even asked me about children. I told her she would struggle to have a child for the first few years, and then she will get twins. She beamed with pleasure. What surprises me about people? Their curiosity to know about their future. Some people literally don't want to work hard and wish to go for an easy route to achieve success. They get trapped by imposters and spend money on false astrology. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the most frustrating feeling?
Answer: Recently I read the novel, "The stationary shop of Tehran," where a couple fell in love and desperately wanted to live life together. But the boy's mother didn't like this relationship, just out of her ego, and secretly created misunderstandings between the couple, which separated them forever. In the evening of their life, the couple meets again. The man reveals to the woman that only his mother was responsible for their separation. He wishes that his mother wouldn't have been this cruel. Once, a colleague told me her parents didn't like her boyfriend and tried her best to break the relationship. However, she could overcome her parents' stubbornness and marry her boyfriend. Now, she is living happily, and her boyfriend-now-husband takes care of her parents as well. She, too, wished that her parents could support her. When I remember my days with my ex-in-laws, my heart sinks with disappointment. They, too, tried hard to create differences between my ex-husband and me. What is the most frustrating feeling? When we get to know that our loved ones only don't like our happiness. Due to their possessiveness, insecurity, and trust issues, they tend to spoil our life. Instead of guiding us to save the relationship, they instigate us to break it. P.S. Dear teenagers, don't get misguided by this write-up. Sometimes, our parents are right too. They try to save us from being trapped in a relationship with the wrong person. So think wisely. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best way to start the new year?
Answer: It was a new year's morning. My mother was fully occupied with her cooking in the kitchen. My father's best friend was invited along with his wife for breakfast. The servant was asked to arrange the house beautifully, whereas the maidservant was helping my mother with cooking. I would be 6–7 years old. I was crying as the servant refused to find my kitchen set. "Why don't you keep your things in place? I don't have time to find your lost things all the time." He yelled. The maidservant, who was grating carrots for Halwa nearby, tried to console me lovingly. "Don't cry, child. He will find your things once he is done with his work." She said. "He won't. He doesn't do any work for me." I sobbed. "Look, if you cry on New Year's day, you will cry throughout the year. Is this what you want to do, child?" She asked. "No," My heart filled with fright. "Then smile. Go and do what you like to do so that you will be doing the same the whole year." She succeeded in convincing me. She had not only convinced me for that day but for a lifetime. Years went by, and such things never turned out to be true but deep down, I still carry the same belief. Recently I enrolled in a post-graduation in psychology as I aspire to become a Mental Health Expert. The books have arrived, but I have not yet started studying them. The statistics in one of these books have frightened me to my very bones. I kept them safe for the new year. I will study them from 1st Jan 2023, believing I will remain a good student throughout the year. As I suspect I will be able to complete the course, I don't want to miss any possibility that might motivate me to study well and achieve my goal. So I will be busy turning pages of my newly arrived psychology books. Please keep me in your prayers. I wish you all a happy new year. May you all achieve everything that you aspire to in 2023. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What did your divorce do to you?
Answer: Last but not least, it made me a Writer/Author. The trauma of divorce pushed me to express my feelings in words and gave me the zeal to motivate others stuck in life. My book Towards A Better Life is available on Amazon and Flipkart. Please give it a read. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What did you do today?
Answer: My six-year-old boy is unaware of religion, community, and caste. And I too don't want to corrupt his mind with my knowledge regarding this. So, a week ago, he announced that he would celebrate Christmas at home. And I happily accepted his proposal. So today, we both have been in a festive mood. I cooked egg biryani for lunch. Then, I baked a cake. We together decorated our table with our homemade decorative items. The evening was filled with the Christmas song we repeatedly played on our laptop. We clicked pictures. I wish to break all the religious barriers and celebrate life — just life with all its colours. Our smile and happiness must be more important than our religious intolerance. I remember a day during my childhood when I demanded Sevai (A dessert made of vermicelli, milk, and dry fruits) on an Eid holiday. And my mother happily cooked it for me. Later in the evening, a Muslim doctor, my father's junior, visited us with his wife. My mother offered them the same Sevai, and they were elated. However, today on a call, my mother said a very different thing. "I wish people from other religions too could show the same affection for Hinduism. Because of their insecurities, they are spreading hatred and violence all around the world", she said meekly. Anyways, I wish you all Merry Christmas. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: At what time exactly did you wake up today?
Answer: I have been busy with my child's exams and office work this month. I felt exhausted all the time and needed to restore my energy. From today, the school is closed for the Christmas holidays. No need to wake up early. No need to rush for everything in the morning. So today, I relaxed, thanking my bed until 9 AM. I lazed under the cozy blanket, though the room was already filled with the yellow sun. I was feeling fresh and stress-free after a long time. After waking up, I spent some time exercising and, at the same time, cooked breakfast. After breakfast, I read a few pages in a book I am currently reading, and then I sat to teach my child. In the afternoon, my office Secret Santa sent me a beautiful Christmas gift that contained ten shades of lipstick and a cute perfume bottle. Santa also wants me to look beautiful….. hahaha. Planning to go out with my kiddo in the evening. Wish you all Merry Christmas. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: As an introvert, why do I enjoy socializing with people?
Answer: I had always wondered, thinking about what sort of an introvert I was. I have been a reserved person and abstain from opening up. I like to remain in my own circle, which I hate to be invaded. I don't mind calling myself as choosy or fussy when it comes to select people for a company. I'm not particularly eager to mingle with everyone. However, on the other hand, I love people. Many of my friends call me a people's person, as I enjoy socializing. I like to spend time with them hearing their stories. At times, my curiosity is at its peak. I want to learn more about life, people and their thought process, which pushes me to socialize. The world then sees an entirely different Anshu, who is talkative, sympathetic, and more social. I believe that being an introvert or extrovert doesn't matter to socializing with people. As Aristotle said, man is a social animal. Socializing is in our genes. The only difference between an introvert and an extrovert is that an introvert might take more time to mingle with others or be more selective in choosing people for a company. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some life hacks for students in hostel?
Answer: I wish you a happy hostel Life. P.S. I lived in the hostel for eight long years. I have written this based on my experiences. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something a child said that left you flabbergasted?
Answer: My six-year-old boy is amiable by nature. He is popular in his class and made many friends in the school. Being a single mother, I have always been worried about his upbringing. My ex-husband unfortunately never tries to meet him. I always wondered how he would react upon being asked about his father. I wondered if he would be able to manage the question mark on the whereabouts of his father. But yesterday, something happened that obliterated all my worries. Here is the conversation with him after coming from school yesterday: "You know, Mumma, I was annoyed today with Nehan." He talked about his best friend. "Why so? What did he do?" "He was asking me again and again - where is your daddy?" He explained. My heart thumped with fright after hearing this. "What did you say then, Sweetie?" I asked, concealing my nervousness. "I told him that my daddy is the king of Russia. So he is in Russia," he said and giggled. "What did then Nehan say?" I asked in disbelief. "What will he say? He stood open-mouthed." He laughed again. And then, we both laughed together. Later, he told me that Nehan stopped asking about daddy. I felt happy to learn that this tiny creature is growing smart. He has learned to handle difficult situations humorously. And more than this, he has learned to accept life. What else does a single mother desire? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something you have never done?
Answer: I Never Lost Hope. I failed in many things in life, but I never lost hope. During childhood, I was compared with my sister for look and complexion and was told that I should focus on my studies as I didn't look that beautiful. Slowly, I started becoming an introvert, but I didn't lose hope. I focused on my studies more and more. All my school life, I was known as the best student and received immense love from the teachers. I was so used to the appreciation that a bit of downfall too unnerved me. When I went to college, I felt immensely demotivated during the initial days and cried almost every day as the college was a convent, and I had been a Hindi medium student. I needed help to grasp the lectures in English. The students were too good at speaking in English. Though I felt dejected, I never stopped working on myself. Now, the same students ask me how I write and speak so well in English. I am still in touch with the professors at my college. They often wish me good luck. In my career, too, I have always had ups and downs. Sometimes I was bright, and sometimes, I was known as average. I never liked corporate jobs, but I still work here as I need them for a living. I had been in a failed marriage for over seven years, where my self-esteem was crushed, and I felt like quitting. However, I always believed that things would change for me someday. And at present, I am in a much better situation. I am happier than before and living a dignified life in all terms. I recently wrote a book, 'Towards A Better Life,' based on my life experiences, which is available on Amazon and Flipkart. I recommend reading it to step towards a happier and more fulfilling life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some money saving tips?
Answer: When I was living with my parents, I had a sophisticated life. We had a beautiful house. My parents never bought our clothes from ordinary places. We travelled to big cities for shopping. And we went on trips from time to time. However, I never saw them being extravagant. No wastage at all. And this unknowingly taught me how to save money. Since I am now a single mother with a huge responsibility, I often shun spending money on unnecessary things. Before I buy anything, I analyze if it is really required. I don't fill all the demands of my child. Since I don't believe in show-offs and competition, this helps me save money and have my peace at the same time. I never buy any expensive gadgets on loan or EMI. Before buying, I look into my budget and then decide. Due to my health issues, I need to avoid frequent dining out. And by doing this, I control my expenses. Instead of living in a rented house and paying a hefty amount to the house owner every month, I preferred buying my own flat and delivering the same amount as EMI. Would you believe that I don't have a credit card? My bank executives are tired of convincing me to have one. I learned that many of us don't know to use credit cards wisely. So I have avoided it. The only thing on which I blindly spend my money is books. I love books, and I feel they are always worth our money. P.S. My book ‘Towards A Better Life’ is available on Flipkart: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What was your “It's finally happening” moment?
Answer: My friend Anirban Pal, who vigorously read me on Quora and reached the conclusion of comparing my writing style with Sudha Murthy's, asked me to write a book. I laughed. "I just vent out my thoughts on Quora. How can I write a book?" I baffled. And also, I had never read Sudha Murthy. I didn't even know that she was a writer. And then, this friend gifted me a book written by Sudha Murthy. I read and found so much of similarities between us. Her personality inspired me. And then, without any delay, I started writing. After working 9.5 hrs at the office, I sat on the sofa with my laptop, typing my book. I wanted to share with everyone about my dream when it comes true. My parents were with me at that time. "You say you are done with your office work, then what do you do again in your laptop sitting in the drawing room?" My father asked me every day. I didn't answer his question, but I wanted to show him the results. In the meanwhile, I fell sick and was admitted to hospital. I was so emaciated that I couldn't walk. I stopped writing. As a single mother, the responsibilities are already huge. Adding this new passion to it seemed unrealistic. At times, I wanted to give up. I then took a break. I just focused on my office work, child and households. After three months, I again felt the temptation to work on my book. This time, I didn't stop. I kept working on it until it took a form of a book. And finally, a few days ago, when the book got published, I cried out of joy to see my words on paper. The feeling of being a published writer is so overwhelming. Please read this book if you are stuck in your life and looking for motivation. You must go for it if you are willing to learn from others' experiences. My book "Towards A Better Life" is available on Amazon and Flipkart: For people outside India: Thank you for all your love and support. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you want to announce?
Answer: My book has been published, and it is available on Amazon and Flipkart. Dear Readers, I have written a book based on my life experiences. Many of you are already aware of my hardships and how I came out of them. There have been times when I found giving up easier than surviving in this cruel world. But hang on! The world has never been so insensitive as I assumed during my gloomy days. When I started interacting with people on social media, including Quora, I realized I was not alone in my miseries. Countless people are suffering more than me. I decided to help them with my stories. I wanted to fan the flames of courage in them to face life's challenges. And gradually, slowly and slowly, I started succeeding too. I received hundreds of thank you messages which pushed me to write a book. Many of my readers requested me to write a book they wanted to cherish forever. So I would like to confess that I could not have finished this book without your support. This book is about me, about you, and for all of us. Please give it a read; I can promise that you will find it worth reading. Here are the links to buy the books: Towards A Better Life Towards A Better Life on Amazon too. I would appreciate you managing a few minutes to write a review for the book on these platforms. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How often do you think about what God wants you to do?
Answer: Everyone has been sent to this earth with a purpose. A purpose of serving others by any means - financially, morally, physically, and spiritually. It's just about sharing a small part of things with others that you have. Recently I was reading the book "The Monk who sold his Ferrari" written by Robin Sharma, where he gives this brilliant statement — “As you entered the world with nothing and you are destined to leave with nothing, serving people with your kindness is only one reason for your being here”. In my quiet moments, I often think about my life's purpose. In my daily prayers, I ask God to give me enough strength to contribute to this world in a meaningful way. Initially, I was unaware of how I would contribute to the world. But when I started receiving such messages from my readers, I felt a triumph over my countless doubts regarding my contribution to the world. Until now, writing has been my passion. After receiving such messages, it has become the purpose of my living. If I can create awareness among people and make them feel better through my writing, I am doing something for humankind. And with this mindset, I have written a self-help book based on my personal experiences. I hope it will help people grow and evolve. I will inform you next week once it is available online. Please stay connected. Thank you for reading! Stay Calm Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it good to marry a divorced woman?
Answer: No. Never. A divorced woman is considered without a soul. The patriarchal society finds her a second-hand property. She is the one who could not learn to adjust and sacrifice and, therefore, couldn't establish a family. This is how she is portrayed in society. And no matter how progressive you consider yourself, deep down, you, too, have a similar opinion about her. In your relationship, you expect her to be polite, gentle, and calm as you consider yourself her life savior. I feel an ordinary man should never marry a divorced woman until he is not divorced, though he is in love with her. It needs a lot of courage to face society which he doesn't have. Not only courage but determination too. There are chances when you may feel as if you have done a favor to her by marrying her. During the conflicts, you may blame her for being responsible for the previous breakup, which would be heartening to her. It's good that you have asked this question on Quora. I advise you not to get trapped in such love affairs. P.S. I know I sound too harsh, but what to do? Truth is always bitter. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the one thing you do that most people don't?
Answer: I recall everyone by their names while offering my prayers. I have a habit of offering prayers to God after taking a bath. At this time, I thank him for everyone who is a part of my life in one way or another — my family members and friends, my colleagues, leads and managers, my readers, my apartment security guard, and the list goes on. I express my gratitude for surrounding me with kind-hearted people who help me in my daily chores or motivate me to live with vitality. Gratitude is the key to abundance. The more we feel grateful for things we have, the more we attract them. Also, I practice opposition thinking. Whenever I get negative thoughts, I immediately try to replace them with positive ones. For example, if I am worried about my health issues, I quickly think of myself happily standing in front of Eiffel Tower with my child though I cannot walk now. Sounds silly, but this is how I act. A digital painting gifted by a reader. I felt that 'Thank you’ wouldn't be enough for his efforts, so I am posting it here. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Your answers always makes me happy and it really makes our day more enlightening. What do you want to say to your readers or convey something?
Answer: Where do you live? You live in Bangalore; you live in Karnataka; you live in India. But before everything, you live in your body. Your body is your home, the real home. It gives you existence and recognition in this physical world. You are known by your body. No one recognizes you the day you leave it. You become invisible. So I say - the way you take care of your house, the same way you should take care of your body because it is your first home. Eat healthy food. Consume fruits and vegetables which are easy to digest. Avoid eating nonveg and junk food to ease your stomach's workload. I don't ask you to stop eating them altogether. I am just asking you to eat them in a moderate way. Go for a walk and exercise regularly. Don't be sedentary for long hours. Move every part of your body every now and then. While taking care of your body, don't forget your brain. Read good books to feed good thoughts to your brain. Don't let it think negatively but encourage it to think only good thoughts. Don't whine that you have no time to care for your body and mind. If you do so, you are that driver who is busy driving and has no time to fill the fuel in his vehicle. And then you know the results. Live your life in a way that you always feel exhilarated. Nourish yourself with childlike vitality and energy. My best wishes to you all. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Have you ever stolen something accidentally?
Answer: Yes. Not accidentally but deliberately. A few years ago, we were in a pub. The group consists of my ex-husband, his two friends, and me. The pub was elegant, and everything was captivating over there. We were enjoying the night with our drinks and music when I suddenly noticed a beautiful pitcher made of glass in our tray that the waiter had served with drinks. It looked adorable as its size was just a finger long. I wanted that. My husband immediately warned me not to do any such things. I then turned to his friend, who had always been my partner in crime, and asked him to get me that cute bottle. "As you wish, my lady!." He said while everyone chuckled. After a few hours, while leaving the pub, he picked up the bottle and passed it to me under the table. "I want two," I shamelessly whispered, keeping it in my purse. When he was stealing the second one, my husband left the table, saying he could not accompany us for robbery. "Come on! We are not doing anything wrong. We are just contributing to this spiritual atmosphere by our spiritual act," The friend remarked. So this was the success story of my robbery. I hope you enjoyed it. P.S.-Later, my husband approved of it, saying that let's consider it complimentary as the bill was huge.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is that one thing Indian parents are most scared of?
Answer: "Mom, Rohan is a decent man. I have known him for the last three years. We love each other. Please let me marry him." Arohi tried convincing her mother. "I know he is a good person but an orphan." Arohi's father interrupted. "Yes, Arohi, you need to understand this. He has no family, no relatives. If you tie the knot with him, you will also be like an orphan in terms of in-laws. You will have no one in the name of the family except a husband". Her mother said. "So what? Mom, I am going to marry a man, not his family. And I am sure I will be happy with him forever." Arohi insisted. "But what shall we reply to the questions of society? So many relatives of ours will attend your wedding. They will ask about your in-laws, family background, work, and reputation. How shall we answer them? They will laugh at us, Arohi. Please understand." This time both the parents chorused. Arohi tried keeping her points again with no results. And finally, Arohi gave up and married a man from an affluent family. They were not just rich but greedy too. Every day, they tormented Arohi for the dowry, and one day, Arohi committed suicide. Her parents, who had loved her greatly, were left with regrets. They regretted valuing society's opinion rather than their daughter's wish. The fear of "What will people say" was the only defect in their love for their daughter. Indian parents are bothered by society, people and reputation more than their children's desire. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: In a relationship, is it okay to act okay even though you are not?
Answer: The relationship is not meant for acting. If you have a true relationship with someone or you desire to lead a long-term relationship with someone, you need to be in your original form. You must remain as raw as you are. I have seen many marriages or relationships that lost their charm too soon. The reason was simple. The couple acted to be okay though they were not okay. They had conflicts and dissatisfaction with each other, which they never expressed. Maybe, they had a fear of losing each other after expressing themselves. They kept quiet for a long which led to monotony, frustration, and hatred. Unknowingly, they created a distance between themselves and could never truly enter each other's space. The relationship felt like a burden. A responsibility to carry for lifelong. If given a chance, one would run away from such a relationship. So I advise you not to act to be okay if you are not okay. Vent out your frustration, speak up and let your partner know what you are going through. Tell them that you need their attention. Also, have the freedom to let them know if you need some space from them to breathe freely. Be what you are. You will then see wonders happening in your relationship. All the best! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is getting married young a good idea?
Answer: During my college days, I visited a relative regularly. We developed a great bond, so we discussed many issues in our free time. One day, my relative told me a strange thing about marriage. According to him, the girls should get married young as this helps the relationship sustain. "Why do you think so?" I asked in disbelief as I had an opinion that every girl should be financially independent first, then they should go for marriage. "Look, the young girls are easy to be molded. They are vulnerable and open to accepting their husbands' ideas, which reduces the conflicts in the relationship." He retorted. I agreed with him. However, I wouldn't say I liked this idea. The idea was inclined to make the women submissive. And for me, being submissive means being a slave. You see, most of the women of the previous generation consider their husbands god because they got married early and were taught by their mothers to be obedient to the husband, no matter if he is abusive. They never had a chance to explore something beyond the circle in which they lived. If a girl is married in her early 20s, she has not seen the world enough. She has not developed any opinion of her own; therefore, she prefers accepting others' thoughts. However, this acceptance is not necessarily going to give her peace. She might feel suffocated in the long term. What do you say? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Who is the most annoying person in your life and why do you let them bother you so much?
Answer: My brother-in-law (Sister's husband). Brother-in-law (over the phone) - Do you miss me? Me - Nope! Him - Tell me the truth. Me - No. I don't. Him - Don't break my heart. Me - I don't mind. Him - huh! It won't break. I consume SAFFOLA. My conversation with him mostly goes like this. At times, he is funny, loving, and annoying.😅 I still let him bother me as he loves me like a little girl, no matter how much he tries to flirt with me. And I always reach out to him to discuss my decisions for my life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Which kind of feelings do you have while you write?
Answer: "I have nothing to offer you except my heart, dear Readers. You devour it or dispose of it; it's totally up to you!" I open my heart while writing. I write whatever comes to my mind and however, it comes. This is why my writing sounds raw, honest, and unpolished. Many of my readers come to me for this only. I don't hide my drawbacks, and I don't skip writing about how I overcame them. I don't keep secrets. I have become such an open book. The intention is to let people know that we are all in the same boat. I walked out of my failed marriage and am currently living single. Many people consider me the epitome of bravery and courage. I want to let them know that I, too, had been a vulnerable, doubtful and confused soul once upon a time. I was too timid to imagine myself in the light. But somehow, I managed to grow like an epipetric plant. When I write on Quora, the only feeling or longing I have is to light a candle for people in the dark. "Would the article I am writing be worth reading or motivating to the readers? Let me mention the setback that I had years ago. Who knows if that inspires them or they find solace in that?" I think while writing. I had always wanted to contribute to the world. When I started writing on Quora, I felt I was succeeding in my aspiration as many found solace while reading me. And now, I have written a book - A self-help book based on my life experiences which will be published this month. Through this book, I hope to contribute a little more to the world. I will keep you posted once the book is out. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How much can your life change in just one year?
Answer: I was emotionally attached to my ex-husband even after the separation. While in marriage, I had loved him a lot and could not believe that he had lost all interest in me, though I had been living in this loveless relationship for many years. I was still hoping that he would realize my love and come back. I could never imagine that he could have an extramarital affair too. Due to covid, our divorce case was not getting finalized as we couldn't attend court regularly. However, every time we met, I still felt protective of him. I kept our child from demanding anything expensive from him if we met at a mall. When I met him in the court, I carried cut fruits or food for him, assuming he lived alone. Last year, our divorce got finalized. With a heavy heart, I requested him to come home whenever he wanted. He didn't say anything except complain that he has nothing left in the city, so he will shift to his hometown. However, just after a week of divorce, I learned that he is very much in the city and married to someone. I was shocked. With tears in my eyes, I saw his wedding photo sent by a friend. After zooming in and out for nearly 10 minutes, I deleted it. And this was the turning point of my life. Loyalty seemed like a joke to me. And I laughed when people talked about honesty and morals. I am a free soul now. I don't care about any social norms. I do what I like to do. I am more privileged than my ex-husband with a spouse. I can spend time with anyone whom I like. I have nobody to question me. What bliss! And you readers got to see an absolutely new, confident woman in me. I am yet to date many and fall in love again and again IF I AM INTERESTED. P.S. I am currently dating all my favorite writers, dead or alive, by reading them vigorously. I have written a book based on my life -experiences which is published this month, and is available on Amazon and Flipkart: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you judge yourself?
