Answer: I look at myself in the mirror and exclaim, “Oh, I am so young, so beautiful, yet to grow and yet to see the world.” When I go out and feel tempted to eat samosa, noodles, or any other junk food, I remind myself of my age, “Shame on you! How can you think of junk food? Look at your age; your skin is getting dull.” And this certainly helps me avoid junk food. Lol! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: When did you realize that you had grown up?
Answer: "Take me out. Or Mumma, get me something to eat. I am feeling bored." My child had been nagging me since morning the last Sunday. And finally, I had to take him out in the evening and buy him some junk food. I then thought of myself. At times, I, too, feel bored. I am bored of everything — books, Quora, phone calls, work, and even my child. I like to be in bed on such days as I can't act like my child. I am grown up. I can't pester anyone to take me out or get me something to eliminate the boredom. I need to stay calm and quiet. The moment we realize that the freedom of expressing ourselves has seeped away from us, we are grown up. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What small things immediately brighten your day?
Answer: It was a monotonous day at work. I had a meeting with customers where I knew I had to face their dissatisfaction and complaints, and I was going to burn a good amount of my energy while convincing them, though I am not good at it. Also, for this meeting, I had to prepare a lengthy report to present. Thinking of all this, I felt drained. The clock was hastily ticking, beckoning me to expedite my work as I also needed to pick up my son from school. Soon, it was 2:45 PM, and I rushed to the school. All the children look similar in the same color uniform and shoes. Every day, I struggle to find my six-year-old. While trying to spot him, he came from behind crooning, "I am here, I am here, Oo my dear!!!" I hugged him, forgetting all my stress for a while, and again hurried to reach home as I had to attend the meeting. On the way, we talked about his day at school, friends, teachers and the lesson on division, which he recently learned. "Mumma, I love this school. Everyone is so nice here", he said. "That's nice, that's nice! I am happy to hear." I said. "But you know, Mumma, I sometimes miss you at school. I wonder what would you be doing at this time at home?" He added with disappointment, not knowing how delighted I felt hearing this. Children are called stress busters. They are a source of happiness. When they grow older, they lose their vitality and expression. But until they are young, let's relish every moment with them. So, if you ask what immediately brightens my day, such expressions of my child do the job. Here is a picture of my Peekaboo: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do people recognize you at public places or transport due to your popularity on Quora Forum?
Answer: I work as Incident Manager who deals with customers and support engineers. I talk to several engineers globally on a daily basis as I monitor their work and also the customer's satisfaction. They too approach me if they have something to convey to the customers or if they need my support in conflicts with customers. Recently, I got a ping over teams from an engineer with whom I had never interacted in the past. I didn't know him. It was the end of my shift and I was pretty exhausted, so I shut down my system without opening the message, considering it work-related. But the next day, I was elated reading the message. I was elated with the reason why he followed me on Quora. I have always longed to motivate people and it seems my dreams are coming true. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How did you celebrate your Diwali this year, was there something special you did this year?
Answer: Diwali is always special.😅 My child and I are very fond of this festival. Lights, diyas, rangoli and crackers thrill us to the core. Diwali 2022 was amazing and unexpected too. My washing machine stopped working just two days before the festival. Actually, I had to replace it long back as it was not working properly. Still, I was managing with it as I could not buy a new one due to financial instability. But this time, on the day of Dhanteras, I bought one with the latest model and it got installed on Diwali day. I was super happy. Two girls who had looked after my child in the past called me to wish me Diwali. One of them has been very close to my heart and after hearing my voice over the phone, she began to sob. It was an emotional moment. I transferred 1000 Rs to her as a Diwali gift, and 500 Rs to the other one. Though the amount was small, it gave me a chance to relish their delight. During the afternoon, I decorated our door and drew a rangoli. It came out really well. I felt great exultation after lighting diyas near the rangoli in the evening. After performing Puja, we went down to burst the crackers. I was startled looking at my child as he fearlessly burst the crackers. Every time, he picked up a small bomb to burst, my heart thumped with fright. My neighbour's three year old baby was cheerful and happily stayed in my lap for a long. Later, they called us to their home and we had wonderful talks. Hope you too had a wonderful Diwali. Wish you all happiness and prosperity together. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the most useful thought to remember during each day?
Answer: Amidst lacking so many things in my life, I keep reminding myself about the things I have. The moment I receive my electricity and water bills, I make the payment thinking that I have so much. I can easily pay. When it rains, standing on my balcony I thank the almighty for giving me a comfortable home. After taking food on my plate, I thank the universe for the same. I remind myself of having my parents, child and a few friends who truly love me. I often feel grateful for having a job and wonderful coworkers. If I ever feel disturbed, I start counting the blessings that I have. And I think I am rich. I feel elated and satisfied. Sometimes, this gratitude multiplies so much that my eyes are wet. I run to my wooden temple at home and thank the almighty for being so kind to me. I know no one has received everything in this world. Love, peace, success, happiness, money, and health didn't come to anyone altogether. One or other thing is missing in everyone's life. But not all have learnt to accept that scarcity and live with peace. This is what I discovered living in this world and then chose my thoughts to remember during each day. P.S. This picture is just for attention. However, I liked it a lot. I have recently clicked it in a hotel. The cart is full of varieties of breads in different shapes.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are your feelings when you realise that roughly 3 months are left until the year ends?
Answer: I am elated. During this month, in October, I took my child to visit the festival dussehra and made him feel that his mother can alone accompany him to visit such fairs. He doesn't have to compare his life with other children who are accompanied by their father. And I could experience his excitement when we together went on swing ride. We both are now desperately waiting for our favourite festival '’Diwali’. Lights, diyas, rangoli and crackers thrill us to the core. A dream is going to come true in November, most probably just before my birthday. And then, probably, a new phase of my life will begin. Curious? I know you all are my well-wishers. So I will definitely share it with you but let the right time come. Until then, please keep me in your prayers. Thank you for being with me and supporting me unconditionally. God bless you all. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your favorite thing to write about?
Answer: My emotional trauma has been a blessing in disguise. During this phase, I learnt a lot, experienced every bit of life and evolved stronger. I underwent all kinds of feelings and emotions — hatred, love, anger, craving, frustration, selfishness, fear and confusion. All at the same time. It seemed my inner world had turmoil and it could burst anytime. At times, it was too vulnerable and the other times, it was too strong and determined. It longed for love and attention and there had been times when it felt nothing. It had become so indifferent. After experiencing so much, I have somehow mastered the wisdom of human psychology. Though I have never studied psychology. In the last few years, I have developed a belief that we have come to this earth for a period of time. The moment it is over, you are gone. Then why not live like an emperor? I often write about being fearless. I insist on having the freedom of living life the way one wants to. There is no need to suffocate oneself in a relationship, at work or with anything else. I want my readers to drop their worries and despair about the past and put a full stop to their assumptions about the future. I want them to live in present. And this is what I would like to write about endlessly. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Whats the greatest act of love you've received?
Answer: When I went to live in a hostel, I was miserable. This was the first time I stayed away from my parents. I was always on edge and wept alone for hours. I didn't know how to wash clothes or even how to oil my hair. These two tasks seemed too difficult to me. There was a maid in my hostel. I guess she was in her late 50s. Once at night, I soaked my clothes in water mixed with detergent powder thinking of washing them the next morning. I stayed alone in my room. At midnight, I developed severe pain in my right arm. I was not able to move my hand. Out of pain, I was crying. This lady slept just outside my room. She knocked on my door as soon as she heard me crying. After knowing the matter, she ran into the kitchen, heated mustard oil and applied it gently on my arms. After 30 minutes of massage, I felt better and drifted into deep sleep keeping my head in her lap. In the morning, she washed all my clothes. Since that day, she became my second mother. She was always affectionate to me. She washed my clothes without others knowing. I paid money for this but still, it was not allowed in the hostel. She secretly came to my room every Saturday night to apply oil to my hair. I never ate the snacks sent by my mother without sharing them with her. Sometimes, I even gave my pocket money to her which she did not want to take. During my exams, before leaving for the examination hall, I touched her feet secretly as I didn't want anyone to know about this relationship. I did not have the confidence to do it publically. I still miss her. I wish I could see her once again. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would you do if people judge you?
Answer: I will stop giving a damn about them. I have actually done it in the last two years. I have become dumb and deaf. I don't hear what others say about me. And I don't react if I ever accidentally hear them. Sometimes, I do enjoy the gossip that they have about me. I instantly feel proud of myself. I have something in me that intrigues them to talk about me. Whoa! What a satisfying feeling! I really, really don't care about others' judgement. My relatives, friends and neighbours don't matter to me if I find them judgemental. They simply don't exist for me and I make sure I don't exist for them as well. I have maintained a distance from everyone who doesn't seem to understand me. I can't afford to waste my time in giving an explanation to them. My time and energy are very precious to me. So in a nutshell, I don't give a fuck to judgemental opinions and perceptions of people. I did, I do and I will do what I like to do. Simple! P.S. The picture is just for attention. Please focus on my writing.😅 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Don't married couples get bored with the same person all the time?
Answer: I had this question in my mind during my graduation days and my heart had a very controversial wish — One should be free to love. How many days, months or years do you want to live with your spouse? - live as long as you wish to live. And the moment you are bored of them, move on. Move on with grace. Find someone and love again. At that time, I advocated free love. The books that I read, approved me for my thoughts. After years, I got married and when I couldn't find a soulmate in my husband, I again felt the need for my old thoughts. However, I couldn't get back to them while being in marriage as I had become conventional and believed in loyalty. Also, I was emotional for my husband. But now, after my divorce, I again feel love should be free. It shouldn't be confined to marriage. In a marriage, most of the time, spouses become cranky towards each other. They nag each other to the extent that the relationship turns sour. One wants to run away if given a chance. Whether you agree or not — after a few years of marriage, love seeps away and there is only dependency or societal pressure due to which the couple feels obliged to live together. They are undoubtedly bored of each other as nothing is left for them to discover in the relationship. This is the reason why I don't support the institution called “Marriage” Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Share something you're grateful for today?
Answer: Last night, while stroking his hair, I narrated a story about my school teacher to my child and tucked him into bed. In a few minutes, he drifted into a deep sleep. I then got up as I had not switched off the balcony light. I got up quietly. But as soon as I left the bed, I heard my son asking “where are you going? Be here only”. I immediately came back and asked him if he had not slept yet. “I had slept only but woke up. You don't go anywhere", he responded with his eyes closed. I smiled and kissed him gently. I felt blessed and wanted. This six-year-old boy is everything to me. I feel miserably empty when he is away from me, even for a few hours. He is the world where I love to dwell every day. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: As a woman, what do some men do that creeps you out?
Answer: Years ago, I was travelling on a train. My co-passengers in my compartment were homely people. There was an old man and his wife, two middle-aged men and a bright young man who was a probationary officer in a bank. Since the journey was nearly 36 hours long, we got along well. The old man liked me for my thoughts and wanted to talk to me more and more. The bank officer grew interested when I shared my opinion on a few topics. The bank officer and I were almost of the same age so we became friends. We shared our Facebook account and he picked up some of my stylish pictures and sent me on WhatsApp commenting something funny but decent. I liked him. He had a great sense of humour. We made fun of everyone on the train through messages and giggled. When we reached our destination, we both exchanged our numbers. At this time, I had grown weary of my monotonous married life though it was just a year old. I really needed someone who could make me laugh. I began to talk to him every day during our office hours. Every day he asked me with care if I had my food on time. I was always smiling and shared the secret of this smile with my husband too. However, slowly, that young man started showing me a different aspect of his personality. He sounded cheap in his talks. His jokes turned obscene and the messages seemed ugly which forced me to block him everywhere. “You need to be careful”, said my husband later. Some men are real creeps. Or I can say, they tend to mistake the inclination that a woman has for them. They walk with a mask on their face which doesn't impress me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: When will life get easier?
Answer: I was living in a dilemma. I knew I was not happy in my marriage but I had no guts to come out of it. I was scared of living alone. I had no confidence to lead a life, taking all the responsibilities of a child on my own. On top of that, I was demoralised by a statement that I would come on road if I break the marriage. I was really scared. However, the constant pain of the toxic relationship was not letting me live either. I had developed a thin border between living in a loveless marriage and living life on my own. The borderline had to be broken and to do so, it needed a huge amount of bravery that I didn't have. With time, I realised I would die this side as well as that side. Then why not to take risk and see what is there that side of border. This curiosity gave me courage to break the line. And after breaking it, life got easier, at least it met my expectations. How does life get easier? When you overcome your dilemma, life becomes easier. When you take risk and be ready to face the consequences, you get a sense of winning. You feel at ease. Being in the dilemma makes you handicapped as you are unable to take an action and try to compromise with all the tantrums that life throws on you. If you make efforts to lessen the complications of life, it becomes easier. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What's classy if you’re rich, but trashy if you're poor?
Answer: I came across this picture of Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan on the internet. Look at her jeans. The torn jeans that she is wearing are considered classy. If a poor girl wears the same jeans, she would be considered a beggar and would be soon directed to be roadside. Even for me, being from the middle class, it is trashy. By the way, I couldn't wrap my mind around how she managed to put on these torn jeans. My salute to her! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How would you react if a stranger approaches you and says you are beautiful?
Answer: Years ago, I was at Pondicherry. With my ex-husband, a friend and his wife. I was wearing my favourite dress. It was new year's eve. All the pubs were crowded and we were looking for a table. Finally, we reached a restaurant with a sea view. This too was crowded and while the husband was talking to the restaurant manager to manage a table for us, I found two old men in their 70s staring at me affectionately. They were foreigners. They looked super lively and cute. When we had eye contact, one of them complimented me by saying, “You are beautiful" and smiled. I blushed purple and thanked him. While my husband had unnerved me by paying more heed to the friend and his wife, these cute-looking old men boosted my confidence for the rest of the evening. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do people get hurt in a healthy relationship?
Answer: I had a very beautiful friend who had always been there for me through thick and thin. He witnessed my divorce, unemployment, depression and my child's illness. He was sensitive and kind. I could reach out to him anytime — be it midnight. He never felt disturbed picking up my call. At that time, he understood me so well that he could feel my emotional turmoil. I could say anything to him all with right though he was just a friend. This friendship was perfect because it had two such people who understood each other very well. Still, there had been times when I felt hurt. And I am sure he too must have not liked something in me. The reason is simple. Nobody is perfect. And the expectations that we have from our loved ones, sometimes seem to be a killer. Especially, those impossible expectations! Such as, the person should understand my feelings without me telling them. How foolish it is! So answering your question, I would say — Yes, people do get hurt in a healthy relationship. Their expectations and the desire to see perfection in their loved ones are the reason for getting hurt. However, if the relationship is healthy, it doesn't take much time to fill the gaps. I had experienced this with that friend. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the biggest tragedy in life?
Answer: He was emotional. He was an introvert. He did everything for his children that a father is supposed to do. He loved his wife just the way a husband is supposed to love. Still, no one could reciprocate the same love to him. His children considered him a burden as he was reaching retirement. His wife has always been least bothered about him as she was influenced by modern thoughts and so-called freedom. He wondered if he could ever speak up against the misbehaviour that he received from his family. He wondered if he could ever know his fault for this mistreatment. He kept quiet as he felt emotional and helpless. He lived in silence as he didn't learn to raise his voice. He endured the pain of negligence and lived like an anonymous in his own house. He could never share this emotional turmoil with anyone outside as the fear of being judged and mocked has engulfed him. The belief “A real man is the one who knows to rule" established by society has only encouraged the lions to survive. “Men too can be vulnerable" is not acceptable here. So he lived all his life in negligence and with the feeling of being unwanted. And slowly, he too forgot if he existed. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are the biggest lessons you have learned in the corporate world?
Answer: Yesterday, a friend called me after many days. And the call went on for nearly 25 minutes. “Wouldn't you be noticed by your manager as you are not at your desk?” I asked her reluctantly. “I called you because I have been feeling bored. No work at the office these days. I sit idle throughout the day, scrolling Instagram.” She retorted. I still asked her to disconnect the call, sit at her desk and get bored. If you are working in a corporate, you need to show your diligent face to your manager all the time. If you think that your manager knows about the dearth of work and wouldn't mind you chilling, then let me tell you that you are living with some great illusion. If you are even working from home, you need to be online otherwise you will be considered irregular no matter if you have completed your task on time. The biggest lesson I have learnt in the corporate world by observing the nature of work and the mentality of management is one needs to showcase one's availability every minute. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the worst thing about the Indian education system?
Answer: “Mumma, my dinosaur was smaller and just okay. Other children had made it bigger and more beautiful.” my six years old child told me this sadly as soon as he reached home from school. “It was better because they didn't make it, but their parents made it. You should feel proud of yourself that you made it.” I convinced him. Today's education system in India is more about show-offs. In the name of creativity, the school is overburdening the children with unnecessary projects that kill their precious time. And parents? There are parents who take pride in doing these projects on behalf of their children. So, indirectly, these projects are not given to children but to the parents as homework. And to be honest, this irks me a lot. My son is in grade two and I never do his project work. If he is able to do it, I let him do it, maybe with a little guidance. Otherwise, I ask him to ignore it. I am the mother who motivates her child to be independent and also, doesn't push him in the race. I can't ask my child to align with the education system if it is rotten. Instead, I would encourage him to be himself. A picture of his skeleton project for attention: Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can any person speak English in one day?
Answer: I come across people who consider English a big deal and struggle to get hold of it. I would like to tell those people that English is just a language. Please don't make a fuss. Be it any language, it comes to us with practice. I tried to learn Kannada but never succeeded. The reason was simple. I never had people with whom I could practice. I had no one to correct my grammar. And gradually, I lost my interest too. For the last six years, I have always had an adult girl to look after my child. Most of them had just passed the primary school, but staying with us, they became fluent in English within a year. My ex-husband, my child and I always spoke in English. Listening to us, they learnt. Also, they had developed a sheer desire to speak English. They requested me to correct them if they made a mistake while speaking. This improved their language and the guests in my house admired them. So I would say — you can not speak a language in one day but yes, with practice and in the right environment, you can definitely learn it in a short span of time. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it worth leaving your parents’ house to live in a dorm at a college?
Answer: Of course, yes. I left my parent's house to live in a hostel at the age of 15. This was the first time when I was managing everything alone. In the past, whenever I got a chance to live without my parents, although just for a few days, I suffered from a high fever. My parents were anxious about my stay in a hostel. I was homesick and wept bitterly remembering them. The toughest job for me was washing my clothes. I locked myself in the bathroom and sobbed while washing them. However, this was a turning point in my life. I learnt to be independent. I learnt to face rowdy seniors and then this cruel world. Some taught me about harmony and adjustment in odd circumstances. I learnt to make decisions. It was impossible to call parents every now and then and seek their advice. So I had to become shrewd enough to choose things on my own. I learnt to face obstacles. Also, I got a chance to explore life which helped me see things from a different perspective. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What would you advise to all from your marriage life? How happy/sad are you?
Answer: Before Marriage: After Marriage: Now, answering the second part of the question — I walked out of my marriage as it was crushing my soul every now and then. I didn't find any need to suffocate myself in a relationship where my presence or absence didn't matter. And now, I am happily single. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some indirect ways in which some people ask for dowry in India?
Answer: “Sharma Ji, we don't want anything from you. You are giving us your precious daughter which is more important than anything. This is just the love and affection that you show towards your daughter. TV, fridge, and AC will only make your daughter's life comfortable and people will say, '’look how much Sharma Ji loved his daughter that he tried to give her everything that could make her happy. Isn't it?’” Now, Sharmaji feels obliged to show his love towards his daughter. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your favorite and most emotionally moving photo of all time?
Answer: Today, I will share with you an emotional story. My father is an emotional person and he has always loved me most though he finds it hard to express his feelings. Once I visited my in-law's place without my husband. After staying a few days over there, I heard that my father fell sick and was even unable to walk. Over the phone, my mother told me that he had stopped eating completely. With tears in my eyes, I went to my mother-in-law asking for permission to visit my father. Initially, she didn't agree but after talking to my husband over the phone, she let me go after three days. I couldn't control my tears when I saw my father. He had become too weak and thin. My mother was trying to feed him but every time he refused to eat. I took the plate from my mother and asked her to leave. I then kissed him gently, tears rolled down his face. “Please, have one bite…. please, for my sake,” I pleaded and he opened his mouth. By pleading like this (every time with a peck on his cheek), I could feed him one chapati. Mom was surprised. Again in 2017, he fell sick. He had become too weak and this time, he was with me in Bangalore. My child was just two years old. He was upset seeing my father lying in bed unconsciously all the time. So every now and then, he went near his grandfather and planted a kiss on his cheek which brought a smile to my father’s face when he was awake. And I managed to click this overwhelming action of my child. This picture will always remain close to my heart. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
